papers.title: EEG morphology and peri-ictal MRI abnormalities in status epilepticus and ictal-interictal continuum.
papers.abstract: Status epilepticus (SE) is a neurological emergency that may have long-term consequences. Peri-ictal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities (PMAs) may serve as marker of potential acute ictal brain injury and can be used for estimating the risk of SE-defining electroencephalography (EEG) patterns. We hypothesized that excitatory-predominant EEG morphologies reflect higher metabolic demand and a greater likelihood of PMAs than inhibitory-predominant morphologies. In this single-center prospective cohort (February 2019-April 2025), we included patients who had either SE or ictal-interictal continuum (IIC) reported on EEG and underwent acute magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (≤48 h). Excitatory-predominant morphology was defined by a sharp-wave amplitude greater than those of the positive and slow wave, a broad sharp wave (>200 ms), or superimposed fast activity. Inhibitory-predominant morphology was defined by the positive or slow-wave amplitude greater than that of a sharp wave. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between EEG morphology and PMAs on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) or fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR). Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho assessed correlations between the number of excitatory features (0-2) and MRI sequences showing PMAs (none, arterial spin labeling [ASL] hyperperfusion only, or DWI/FLAIR). Among 205 included patients (134 IIC, 71 SE), excitatory-predominant patterns and lateralized periodic discharges were associated with increased risk of DWI/FLAIR PMAs (p = .001 and p = .02, respectively). In IIC patients, excitatory-predominant morphology was the only predictor of PMAs (p = .002). In the subset with ASL, DWI, and FLAIR sequences (n = 145), the number of excitatory features correlated strongly with types of sequences affected by PMAs (Kendall's tau p < .001; Spearman's rho p < .001). Excitatory-predominant morphology, as opposed to inhibitory-predominant patterns, was associated with a more frequent occurrence of PMAs. These findings support an EEG morphology framework based on excitatory-inhibitory balance across IIC and SE.

papers.title: Chrono-Therapeutics in Type 2 Diabetes: Translational Perspectives Using Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Integrated Optimization of Pharmacological, Nutritional, and Lifestyle Interventions.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a multisystem endocrine disorder that requires multidisciplinary management in solving its global health challenge, as its prevalence increases despite the scientific advances in therapeutic and dietary interventions. The management strategies are expected to be personalized rather than "one-size-fits-all", as their efficacy has declined over time. This occurred because of the often-overlooked significance of circadian rhythms, despite their physiological roles in energy balance, endocrine, and β-cell function. The misalignment of pharmaceutical interventions, nutrition, and lifestyle with the biological clock contributes to and complicates T2DM. The advent of Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has now enabled comprehensive assessment of glycemic variability over a long period, allowing monitoring of the impact of nutrition, physical activity, and therapy. CGM has been shown to improve the precision of therapeutic interventions in alignment with the physiological clock. This will potentially enhance efficacy, minimize adverse effects, and improve long-term metabolic outcomes. However, several articles have separately explored chronotherapeutic, chrononutrition, and lifestyle modification for T2DM management, without a clinically integrated framework. This review, from a translational perspective, integrates circadian rhythms, chronotherapeutic interventions, chronotyping, lifestyle factors, and gene variants associated with glycemic dysregulation to optimize T2DM management. A CGM-assisted multilayered chronotherapeutic algorithm was further proposed to support more personalized T2DM management and to guide prospective clinical validation and hypothesis-driven research.

papers.title: Ambulatory CPAP initiation in severe OSAS leads to lower rates of treatment withdrawal and similar patient-reported outcomes compared to in-laboratory titration: a Belgian observational study.
papers.abstract: In the context of Belgian updates to the current obstructive sleep apnea (syndrome) (OSA(S)) treatment convention, the purpose of this observational real-world study was to compare 3-month patient-reported outcomes (PROs) in OSAS patients undergoing an 'in-lab' or 'ambulatory' continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) titration pathway. Consecutive uncomplicated severe OSAS (apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥30) were prospectively included. Patients were all eligible to undergo in-lab manual titration polysomnography (PSG) or ambulatory titration respiratory polygraphy (RP) under fixed CPAP (7 to 9 cm H20), in cases where they were compliant during the first 15 days of use. If not, they were moved to the 'in-lab' pathway. Clinical outcomes (PRO (questionnaires), CPAP pressure, compliance, RREs) were assessed 3 months after CPAP titration in both groups. A total of 317 severe OSAS patients were included (134 in the 'ambulatory' pathway, of whom 11% could not adapt to CPAP). PROs and compliance were similar in both groups but CPAP pressure, RREs, and withdrawal rates were significantly increased in the 'in-lab' group. The 'in-lab' group had more severe OSA characteristics at baseline and included difficult-to-treat patients from the 'ambulatory' group after CPAP adaptation failure. The closer monitoring of the 'ambulatory' group could also explain the differences. In this single-center observational study of uncomplicated severe OSAS, ambulatory CPAP management was associated with lower withdrawal rates and equivalent PROs compared to in-lab titration. These findings support the feasibility of broadening the ambulatory pathway, provided very close TMg-based follow-up is implemented from treatment initiation. Generalization to moderate or complicated OSA populations requires dedicated studies.

papers.title: Theoretical Study of Rovibronic Spectra of the Si2 Molecule.
papers.abstract: Accurate rovibronic spectra of the Si2 molecule were constructed using the DUO program, based on high-level potential energy curves and electric dipole moment data obtained at the MRCI+Q (multireference configuration interaction with Davidson correction) level employing the aug-cc-pVQZ-DK all-electron basis set. Absorption spectra spanning a wide temperature and broad wavenumber ranges are further derived within the ExoMol framework via the ExoCross program. Spectral analysis reveals that high-temperature conditions substantially extend the effective absorption range and activate high-energy transition channels, thereby modulating the overall spectral response of Si2. Comparison with the measured H3Σu- ← X3Σg- (2,0) spectrum provides a qualitative assessment of the calculated contour and reveals limitations in the reproduction of resolved fine structure and individual line positions. Full rovibronic structures of the K3Σu- ← X3Σg-(1,0) ladder and newly assigned 33Σu- ← X3Σg- (0,0), (0,1), and (1,0) bands are simulated at room temperature 298 K, compensating for the deficiencies of previous experimental measurements, which resolved only the band heads without complete rotational profiles. Quantitative comparison of spectral features and transition energies unambiguously distinguishes the literature-reported N3Σu- state from the newly identified triplet state (33Σu-), thus resolving the long-standing confusion in the assignment of the ultraviolet triplet excited state series of Si2. The high-precision spectroscopic and thermodynamic benchmark data established herein provide a robust fundamental support for refined theoretical calculations, astronomical spectral identification, and in situ plasma diagnostics of silicon-bearing molecules.

papers.title: High Prevalence of Weight-Related Comorbidities and Applicability of Screening Criteria Among Children With Overweight but Without Obesity: Insights From a Dutch Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Current guidelines recommend assessing comorbidities in children with overweight, but without obesity only when specific risk factors are present. Data on the prevalence of comorbidities in this group remain limited. Weight-related comorbidities (Type 2 diabetes, dyslipidaemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome and depressive symptoms) and precursors (elevated blood pressure and insulin resistance) were assessed in 102 children with overweight but without obesity. Risk factors frequently cited in international guidelines as screening criteria were evaluated. Children (55.9% girls) had a mean age of 11.9 years (SD 2.6; range, 3.5-16.7 years) and a mean BMI z-score was 2.4 (0.3 SD). Comorbidities were identified in 66.7% of the children, and two or more comorbidities were present in 33.3%. Dyslipidaemia (35.3%), impaired liver parameters (33.3%) and hypertension (24.0%) were most prevalent. Prediabetes was observed in 7.8%, and indications of obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome in 8.5% and depressive symptoms in 5.7%. Children with comorbidities had a significantly higher waist circumference z-score than those without. Common screening criteria were met by 80.6% of the children with dyslipidemia, 50.0% with prediabetes, 41.2% with impaired liver parameters and 26.5% of children without comorbidities. The majority of children with overweight, but without obesity, had comorbidities. Common screening criteria appear insufficient to accurately identify these children, suggesting current criteria may not fully capture true risk profiles.

papers.title: Visual function and circadian rest-activity rhythms in US older adults: The National Health and Aging Trends Study.
papers.abstract: To evaluate associations of visual function with accelerometer-derived rest-activity rhythm (RAR) metrics and 24-hour continuous activity patterns among older adults. We analyzed data from 728 U.S. Medicare beneficiaries (weighted mean age 79.1±6.0 years, 78% White, 56% female) who completed objective vision assessments and provided ≥ 3 days of accelerometer data in NHATS Round 11 (2021). Visual functions included distance acuity, near acuity, and contrast sensitivity. Wrist-worn accelerometer data were used to derive parametric RAR metrics (amplitude, mesor, acrophase, alpha, beta, and percent rhythm) and nonparametric RAR metrics (relative amplitude, intradaily variability [IV], interdaily stability [IS]). Associations were examined using weighted linear regression and function-on-scalar regression (FOSR). Poorer visual function, regardless of type, was associated with lower amplitude (rhythm strength, both parametric and non-parametric metrics) and lower percent rhythm (rhythmicity), but not with mesor (average activity level), acrophase (peak activity timing), or alpha (peak-trough width). Distance acuity showed a statistically significant nonlinear association with IS. We did not observe any statistically significant associations for beta and IV after type 1 error correction. FOSR showed lower daytime activity and higher nighttime activity during typical sleep hours among those with vision impairment, with simultaneous significance limited to a small portion of the day. Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. Worse visual function was associated with weaker and less robust circadian RARs in a representative sample of older adults. Longitudinal and mechanistic studies are warranted to understand the intertwined relationships between visual function and circadian health.

Screen Time: Adherence to Recommendations, Daily Patterns and Health in Swedish Preschoolers.
papers.abstract: To describe screen time outside preschool and adherence to the 60-minute daily recommendation across the week among Swedish preschool children, and to examine secondary associations with socioeconomic and health indicators. This citywide observational study included 2624 children aged 3-5 years from 124 public preschools in Stockholm. Parents completed repeated 24-hour screen-time diaries in 2020-2021, contributing 27 401 daily reports. Mixed-effects models compared weekdays with weekends and assessed socioeconomic and health associations. Mean reported screen time outside preschool was 61.5 minutes per day, and 53.7% met the recommendation. Reported screen time was 19.9 minutes per day higher on weekends than weekdays, while adherence was 42.8% and 60.7%, respectively. Adherence declined markedly on Friday. Socioeconomic differences were inconclusive. Exceeding 60 minutes per day was associated with shorter sleep, greater behavioural difficulties and lower adherence to the physical activity recommendation. Associations with poor sleep quality or grip strength were inconclusive. Only around half of preschool children met the screen-time recommendation. The pronounced Friday and weekend decline suggests that family-focused strategies should complement preschool policy; health associations were modest and observational.

papers.title: Mapping the Developmental Landscape of Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes and Cardiac Organoids Relative to Native Heart Tissue.
papers.abstract: The development of physiologically relevant human cardiac models is essential for drug discovery and disease modeling; however, achieving the transcriptomic and metabolic maturity of adult human tissue remains a challenge. In this study, we performed a comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic comparison of in vitro-induced pluripotent stem cell cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) in 2D cultures, 3D cardiac organoids, and native fetal and adult human cardiac tissue. CMs from both 2D and organoid cultures were immature compared to adult CMs. 3D organoids exhibit a more complex cellular architecture comprising multiple cardiac cell types, and they possess a unique proliferative fibroblast population that is not represented in the adult or fetal heart. Organoids also showed immaturity in non-CMs as well as CM cell types. Both iPSC-CMs and cardiac organoids were metabolically immature with enhanced expression of both glycolytic and reduced fatty acid oxidation genes. However, maturation was not a binary state, as the in vitro CMs were distinct from fetal CMs, and had transcriptionally advanced calcium handling and electrophysiology, but immature metabolism and stress responses. When assessed versus adult heart tissues they were also distinct. Our work provides a molecular roadmap of the gaps between in vitro models and the native adult heart, highlighting areas for future improvement in in vitro CMs.

papers.title: Identification of Insomnia Disorder Using Machine Learning and Wearable Technology.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder. Wearable electroencephalography (EEG) combined with machine learning (ML) offers a promising, low-burden approach for home-based sleep monitoring and objective assessment of insomnia. The study included 112 patients with insomnia disorder (ID) and 98 healthy controls (HC), who underwent overnight forehead EEG recording. For each subject, macro-sleep metrics, as well as EEG-derived features including aperiodic and periodic features, were extracted. To classify ID and HC, we constructed predictive models based on three feature categories and their combinations. Specifically, we trained five ML models, namely Elastic Net, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost and CatBoost. All models performed significantly better than chance. Performance was highest for feature sets including periodic features, with the CatBoost periodic and macro + periodic models achieving the highest AUC (0.765). SHAP analysis of the full-feature CatBoost model showed that delta-band power and sleep timing ranked at the top, whereas aperiodic features contributed less but remained informative. This study explored the value of objective metrics derived from wearable sleep devices in insomnia assessment and the role of aperiodic and periodic sleep features. These findings support the hyperarousal model of insomnia and the feasibility of wearable sleep monitoring as a low-burden adjunct for insomnia assessment.

papers.title: Understanding daily bedtime procrastination using generalized linear mixed model trees: A daily diary approach.
papers.abstract: With sleep disturbance becoming increasingly prevalent, bedtime procrastination has attracted growing research attention. According to Temporal Self-Regulation Theory, bedtime procrastination may reflect both relatively stable differences in self-regulatory capacity and day-to-day variations in situational prepotency of competing behaviors. However, most previous studies have examined bedtime procrastination and its correlates primarily at the between-person level, with less attention to day-to-day fluctuations. To address this gap, the present study conducted a secondary analysis of daily diary data to examine correlates of daily bedtime procrastination. Daily assessments of problematic smartphone use, self-control, physical activity, psychological well-being, and bedtime procrastination were collected from 160 undergraduates (56.87% female; mean age = 20.34 ± 1.53 years) over 30 consecutive days. Generalized linear mixed model trees were used to identify combinations of person-level and daily correlates associated with different levels of bedtime procrastination. The highest levels of bedtime procrastination were observed among individuals characterized by lower mean self-control, greater previous-day bedtime procrastination, higher mean problematic smartphone use, and lower within-person moderate physical activity. These findings illustrate the value of considering both between-person differences and daily variations in understanding heterogeneity in bedtime procrastination.

papers.title: Age-Adjusted Exploratory Analysis of Spectral, Aperiodic, and Microstate Electroencephalography Features in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) can characterize functional brain alterations in multiple sclerosis (MS), but many EEG features vary with age. We, therefore, examined resting-state EEG associations with MS using age-adjusted models while explicitly accounting for the severe age imbalance in the available dataset. Resting-state 128-channel EEG data from the BrainLat dataset were analyzed. Demographic files included 32 patients with MS and 32 healthy controls (HC); global-feature models included 29 patients with MS and 32 HC, and channel-level sample sizes varied by feature. Diagnosis and age were entered in linear models. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied separately to five global spectral/aperiodic tests, 16 global microstate tests, and the 128 channel-wise tests within each feature. Within-MS continuous age regression and exploratory age-stratified ANOVA were evaluated with the same family definitions. After correction, diagnosis coefficients were significant for global bandwidth (β = 1.928, q = 0.0287), global aperiodic offset (β = 1.816, q = 3.29 × 10-7), and offset at all 128 channels (β range = 1.52-2.41; q range = 3.56 × 10-8 to 7.43 × 10-5). Global central frequency, exponent, power spectral density, and all 16 microstate measures did not survive FDR correction. No within-MS continuous-age or age-stratified result survived FDR correction. Aperiodic offset showed the strongest diagnosis association under the specified age-adjusted model. However, the MS and HC age ranges did not overlap (21-55 vs. 56-83 years), so the diagnosis coefficient depends on extrapolation and cannot establish an MS-specific effect. The findings are exploratory and require age-matched replication with detailed clinical, vigilance, site, sex, and magnetic resonance imaging characterization.

papers.title: Changes in Clinical Management Related to Continuous Versus Routine Electroencephalogram in Critically Ill Adults: Analysis of a Randomized Trial.
papers.abstract: Continuous electroencephalogram (cEEG) is increasingly utilized in the intensive care unit for consciousness-impaired patients with various conditions. It is, however, costly in terms of technical and human resources, and its impact on prognosis compared with routine EEG (rEEG) remains debated. We aimed to characterize the effect of cEEG vs. rEEG on clinical management modifications, and to determine if these correlated with a better outcome. This is an ancillary analysis using data of CERTA (NCT03129438), a randomized trial comparing cEEG versus repeated rEEG in critically ill adults with altered consciousness. Clinical management modifications due to the EEG intervention, predefined as performed within 60 h of EEG start, were prospectively recorded (anti-seizure medication [ASM], sedation, new radiological examination, new surgical intervention, withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy). Correlation with the EEG type was analyzed by 2 × 2 tables; Mantel-Haenszel tests explored the impact on mortality and functional outcome at 6 months. The trial included 364 patients completing follow-up (182 each in the cEEG and rEEG groups). While 58.2% of cEEG and 45.6% of rEEG patients had any management change (p = 0.018), ASM was modified in 22.0% (cEEG) and 12.1% (rEEG) (p = 0.012); other clinical interventions were comparable across EEG groups. Adjusting for ASM modifications, mortality (p = 0.845) and functional outcome (p = 0.619) remained similar between the EEG groups. In critically ill adults, cEEG is associated with more clinical management modifications compared to repeated rEEG, particularly regarding ASM, but this does not seem to translate into improved patients' outcomes.

papers.title: Functional Neural Ensembles and the Development of Cognition: A Developmental Framework.
papers.abstract: Functional neural ensembles, temporally coordinated groups of neurons or neural populations whose activity supports specific computations and behaviors, are increasingly recognized as important intermediate units linking local circuit dynamics to large-scale brain function. Most studies, however, have focused on their role in the mature nervous system, with relatively little consideration of how ensemble organization emerges across development. In this review, we propose a developmental framework in which functional neural ensembles are conceptualized as progressively assembled and refined substrates of cognition from prenatal life through adulthood. We synthesize evidence from developmental neuroscience, electrophysiology, neuroimaging, and systems neuroscience concerning spontaneous neural activity, sensorimotor coupling, thalamocortical development, oscillatory coordination, and large-scale network maturation. Current evidence suggests that coordinated neural activity emerges prenatally through intrinsically generated activity patterns that contribute to early functional organization. Following birth, sensorimotor interactions, activity-dependent plasticity, and environmental engagement refine and stabilize these patterns, promoting increasing specificity and efficiency. Across childhood and adolescence, ensembles become progressively specialized and integrated through oscillatory synchronization, hemispheric differentiation, and the maturation of long-range connectivity. Mature cognition is proposed to depend upon the flexible recruitment and coordination of ensembles across distributed neural systems. We argue that functional neural ensembles should be viewed not solely as products of mature brain organization but as developmentally constructed entities shaped by interactions among intrinsic activity, experience-dependent processes, and environmental constraints. The developmental ensemble framework advanced here provides a conceptual model linking early neural activity to later cognitive function while generating testable predictions regarding typical and atypical neurodevelopment. Framing cognition in terms of the developmental assembly, refinement, and coordination of neural ensembles offers a unifying perspective for understanding how complex cognitive functions emerge across the lifespan.

papers.title: Chronic Sleep Deprivation-Induced Anxiety-Like Behaviors Correlate With Altered Peripheral S100A10+ Immune Cells and Hippocampal Metabolic Dysregulation.
papers.abstract: To characterize biological alterations associated with chronic sleep deprivation (CSD)-related anxiety-like behaviors in mice and to explore the parallel association between peripheral immunity and central metabolism. A mouse model of CSD was established by subjecting mice to 7 days of sleep deprivation. Anxiety-like behaviors were evaluated using the open field test (OFT) and elevated plus maze (EPM) test. Peripheral blood immune cell subsets and S100A10 levels were analyzed using flow cytometry. Blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and inflammatory levels in peripheral blood and hippocampal tissues were assessed through immunofluorescence staining, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Hippocampal metabolic profiles were characterized using untargeted metabolomics. Intrinsic interactions among behavioral, immune, and metabolic indices were evaluated through correlation analysis. The functional pathways associated with the differential metabolites were determined using the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analysis. CSD mice exhibited typical anxiety-like behaviors, characterized by reduced time spent in the central area in the OFT and fewer entries into that area, as well as increased latency to enter the open arms in the EPM test. At the peripheral immune level, CSD did not alter the proportions of total T cells or total monocytes. However, the proportion of proinflammatory Ly6C+ high monocytes increased, whereas that of anti-inflammatory Ly6C+ low monocytes decreased. CSD disrupted the BBB, promoted microglial activation, and elevated proinflammatory cytokine concentrations in the peripheral blood and hippocampal tissue. Furthermore, CSD upregulated S100A10 expression in CD45+ leukocytes, CD8+ T cells, and total monocytes. At the hippocampal metabolome level, CSD induced 157 differential metabolites. The levels of metabolites including ginsenoyne K were significantly upregulated, while those of metabolites such as phosphatidylinositol were downregulated. Additionally, multiple metabolites were associated with core anxiety-related behavioral parameters. KEGG enrichment analysis revealed that differential metabolites were primarily enriched in neurofunction-related pathways, including the cAMP-signaling pathway and glutathione metabolism. Correlation analysis further unveiled that the proportion of peripheral T cells, the balance between monocyte subsets, S100A10 levels in total monocytes, and key hippocampal metabolites were closely associated with anxiety-like behaviors. CSD induces anxiety-like behaviors in mice, it alters the distribution of peripheral monocyte subsets, upregulates S100A10 levels in specific immune cells, and remodels hippocampal metabolism. Moreover, CSD disrupts BBB integrity and activates microglia in the hippocampus.

papers.title: Differential Neurophysiological Signatures of Asymptomatic Carotid and Intracranial Atherosclerotic Stenosis: A Multimodal Resting-State EEG Study.
papers.abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion associated with asymptomatic atherosclerotic cerebrovascular stenosis may induce functional-network alterations before overt neurological deficits emerge. Asymptomatic carotid stenosis (ACS) and asymptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (aICAS) represent distinct large-artery phenotypes with differing perfusion distributions. However, whether these location-specific hemodynamic constraints are associated with different patterns of functional brain reorganization is poorly understood. This study investigated the multiscale electrophysiological alterations associated with ACS and aICAS. In this cross-sectional study, 68 participants, including ACS (n = 29), aICAS (n = 17), and age-matched healthy controls (n = 22), underwent resting-state electroencephalography (rs-EEG) recording and neuropsychological assessment (Chinese Mini-Mental Status [CMMS], Trail Making Test Parts A and B [TMT-A/B]). Microstate dynamics, power spectra, and α-band source-space functional connectivity were analyzed. Network-Based Statistic (NBS) controlled for family-wise error in connectivity analysis. Partial correlations adjusted for age, hypertension, and diabetes. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) performance was evaluated using bootstrap confidence intervals and repeated five-fold cross-validation. CMMS scores did not differ among groups, whereas TMT completion times were longer in the ACS group, indicating subtle performance alterations. Both patient groups showed reduced microstate A (MsA) coverage and decreased transitions between MsA and microstate C (MsC). ACS additionally exhibited shortened MsA duration, reduced α-band power, and increased connectivity within a distributed network identified by NBS. The aICAS group showed increased bidirectional transitions between microstate B (MsB) and microstate D (MsD) but no significant NBS component. Selected microstate measures remained associated with TMT performance after covariate adjustment. ROC analyses showed moderate discrimination, with apparent areas under the curves (AUCs) of 0.672-0.744 and cross-validated AUCs of 0.675-0.744. ACS and aICAS showed shared and location-specific electrophysiological alterations. These exploratory findings may help characterize early functional brain changes associated with asymptomatic cerebrovascular stenosis, but require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

papers.title: Violet Light-Induced Changes in Voice Vitality Indices and Their Associations With Sleep Improvement in Patients With Depression.
papers.abstract: Violet light (VL, 360-400 nm) has recently emerged as a potential neuromodulatory intervention for depression. Prior randomized controlled trials demonstrated antidepressant and nonspecific sleep-improving effects of VL irradiation. Voice-derived vitality indices, computed from sound pressure change acceleration, have been proposed as non-invasive surrogate markers of depressive symptoms and treatment response. In this study, we examined whether VL irradiation alters voice vitality indices and whether these changes are associated with clinical outcomes, particularly sleep improvement, in patients with depression. This exploratory sub-analysis was derived from a sham-controlled, double-blind, randomized crossover trial (jRCTs032210260) in adults with mild major depressive disorder. Participants received 4 weeks of active or sham VL irradiation. Depressive symptoms, sleep quality, cognition, and voice indices were assessed before and after each intervention period. Two vitality indices were extracted: vitality-all (overall vocal energy) and vitality-depression (segments containing positively valenced words). Statistical analyses were conducted using linear mixed-effects models with subject-specific random intercepts, supplemented by correlation analyses and multiple regression. Active VL irradiation significantly improved the depression-specific vitality index (vitality-depression) compared with sham stimulation, as indicated by a significant time-by-intervention interaction, whereas the overall vitality index (vitality-all) did not show a significant interaction. In univariate analyses, higher baseline vitality-all, but not vitality-depression, was significantly correlated with greater sleep quality improvement (i.e., a greater percentage reduction in the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [PSQI] score) under the active VL condition; however, the difference between the active and sham correlations was not statistically significant. When both indices were evaluated simultaneously in a multiple regression model to control for baseline covariates, higher baseline vitality-all emerged as a significant predictor of greater percentage sleep improvement (i.e., a more negative percentage change in PSQI), whereas higher baseline vitality-depression was associated with less sleep improvement or potential worsening of sleep quality (i.e., a more positive percentage change in PSQI). VL irradiation was associated with increases in vocal vitality, and these voice changes were further associated with sleep normalization. Voice-derived vitality indices represent promising non-invasive biomarkers; however, their external validation remains limited, and mechanistic interpretations should be considered preliminary. Replication in larger and more diverse samples will be essential to establish their generalizability and clarify their potential clinical utility. jRCTs032210260. Registered 19 August, 2021, https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/latest-detail/jRCTs032210260.

papers.title: Machine Learning Methods for Automatic Sleep Stage Classification: Current Status and Future Challenges.
papers.abstract: The intricacies of sleep architecture hold significant implications for understanding human health, making automated sleep staging a critical frontier in sleep research. While existing literature predominantly delves into deep learning methods for sleep staging, the current landscape of lightweight, home-use sleep monitoring devices necessitates a closer examination of traditional machine learning algorithms for sleep pattern recognition and analysis. In response to this need, in this paper we provide a comprehensive review of machine learning methods for automatic sleep staging. By synthesizing state-of-the-art approaches, we traverse the entire process, from data collection devices to feature extraction and selection, culminating in diverse sleep stage classification methods. These methods encompass single-modality, dual-modality, and multi-modality approaches, reflecting the evolving complexity of sleep stage classification methodologies. Moreover, we delve into the challenges, identify emerging trends, and outline future directions in the field of sleep staging. By offering these insights, we aim to equip researchers, clinicians, and technologists with a roadmap for advancing automated sleep staging methodologies within the realm of machine learning.

papers.title: The Histaminergic System: A Key Regulator of Pathogenesis and an Emerging Therapeutic Target in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition defined by core deficits in social communication and restricted, repetitive behaviors. However, its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood and no therapy targeting the core symptoms has been approved for clinical use. Converging evidence now links ASD to dysregulation of the histaminergic system. Histamine H3 receptor (H3R) antagonism attenuates ASD-related neuroinflammation both by enhancing histaminergic transmission and acting directly on microglia. Histamine H1 receptor (H1R) and Histamine H2 receptor (H2R) signaling jointly supports synaptic plasticity and cognition, whereas the balance between H1R and H3R shapes the sleep-wake cycle. Molecular remodeling of the histaminergic system in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of individuals with ASD has been reported as a coordinated transcriptional signature linked to neuroinflammation and core behavioral abnormalities. Moreover, in preclinical ASD models, H3R antagonists/inverse agonists (e.g., DL77 and A-366) have produced encouraging effects on social and repetitive behaviors. Collectively, these results suggest that the histaminergic system integrates genetic risk, environmental triggers, immune impairment, and neuronal-circuit defects associated with ASD.

papers.title: Post-traumatic stress, distress, coping and sleep quality in early-career paramedics.
papers.abstract: Paramedics are exposed to trauma, placing them at elevated risk of mental health symptoms. However, limited research has examined symptom trajectories and associated factors in early-career paramedics. This study explored changes in psychological distress and post-traumatic stress symptoms during the first year of paramedic practice and whether coping styles or sleep quality are associated with these changes. Intern paramedics (N = 21; 71% female; Mage = 24.2, SD = 4.1) completed measures at five timepoints, including the General Health Questionnaire (psychological distress), Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5), Coping Strategies Inventory and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Longitudinal analyses explored symptom trajectories and associated factors over 12 months. PTSD symptoms significantly increased (B = 0.9 [95% CI 0.2-1.6] P = 0.013). Psychological distress showed a significant quadratic effect (B = -13.5 [95% CI -23.7 to -3.4] P = 0.011). There was a significant association for between-person sleep quality and both PTSD symptoms (P < 0.001) and psychological distress (P < 0.001), indicating that participants with poorer average sleep quality over the 12-month study period experienced higher overall mental health symptoms. Coping styles and within-person sleep quality were not significantly associated with mental health symptoms. Psychological distress and PTSD symptoms increased during the first year of paramedic practice, with overall sleep quality a correlate of mental health. Early identification of sleep difficulties may support targeted interventions. Further research is needed to explore whether coping strategies become more influential as paramedics transition into autonomous roles.

papers.title: Immediate responses to stimulation of trigeminal-associated sites using conventional suction-type and wearable silicone SSP electrodes: An exploratory randomized three-arm study in healthy adults.
papers.abstract: BackgroundComparative evidence regarding the immediate subjective and physiological responses to conventional suction-type and wearable conductive silicone silver spike point (SSP) electrodes remains limited.ObjectiveTo compare responses to conventional SSP stimulation at V1-associated sites and wearable silicone SSP stimulation at V3-associated sites with a nonequivalent no-current control.MethodsFifty-four healthy young adults were randomized to control, conventional SSP, or silicone SSP groups (18 per group). Conventional electrodes were applied without current in the control group, whereas both active groups received 20 min of stimulation. The primary outcome was pre-to-post change in the Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (KSS). Exploratory secondary outcomes included electroencephalography (EEG), heart rate variability (HRV), and masseter electromyography (EMG). Analyses included mixed repeated-measures ANOVA and Welch ANOVA with Dunnett T3-adjusted comparisons.ResultsA significant time × group interaction was observed for KSS [F(2, 51) = 4.693, p = .013, partial η2 = .155]. Mean ± SD changes were 0.53 ± 1.77, 1.14 ± 1.95, and 2.92 ± 3.28 points in the control, conventional SSP, and silicone SSP groups, respectively. Post hoc analysis showed a significant difference between the silicone SSP and control groups (mean difference, 2.389; 95% CI, 0.154-4.624; adjusted p = .034), but not between the two active stimulation groups (adjusted p = .162). No significant time × group interactions were observed for EEG, HRV, or EMG.ConclusionKSS changes differed between silicone SSP and no-current control, but superiority or equivalence relative to conventional SSP was not established. The simultaneous differences in stimulation site and electrode design prevent attribution of the observed findings to either factor independently.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

papers.title: Phox2b 25-Ala expansion leads to Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome like phenotypes in mice.
papers.abstract: Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome (CCHS) is a rare genetic disorder caused mainly by PHOX2B mutations and characterized by severe impairment of the autonomic nervous system and central control of breathing. The cardinal feature of CCHS is hypoventilation during sleep and an impaired hypercapnic ventilatory response. This defect has been linked, in part, to anatomical and functional abnormalities of phox2b-expressing neurons in the retrotrapezoid nucleus (RTN), a key component of central CO₂ chemoreception. Although existing mouse models have provided major mechanistic insights, the severe and often perinatal phenotype of several models has limited their use for longer-term therapeutic testing. Here, we generated and characterized, for the first time, a new mouse model bearing the +5 alanine (+5Ala) expansion mutation (phox2b25Ala/+ mice) that reproduces CCHS-like phenotypes described in humans. Phox2b25Ala/+ pups suffered from hypoventilation and had a blunted response to hypercapnia at birth, leading to premature death in 75% of the pups. At the network level, the frequency of inspiratory activity in vitro was significantly reduced in phox2b25Ala/+ mice, and the response to acidosis was affected. At the cellular level, phox2b25Ala/+ mice had a reduced number of phox2b-expressing RTN neurons, with this reduction being less pronounced in the 25% of pups that survived. In conclusion, the +5 alanine expansion that causes CCHS reproduces CCHS-like phenotypes in mice. Phox2b25Ala/+ mice suffer from life-threatening hypoventilation that leads to premature death at birth and a lack of chemosensitivity. However, 25% of phox2b25Ala/+ mice survive until adulthood, representing a valuable opportunity for drug testing in CCHS.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Lung cellular and molecular physiology

papers.title: Changes of response inhibition in patients with epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Background: Response inhibition is a core executive function for the brain to suppress impulsive or irrelevant responses. Epilepsy disrupts response inhibition via epileptic discharges. The specific response inhibition capabilities in drug-resistant epilepsy and during seizure-remission, as well as the underlying electrophysiological mechanisms of impaired response inhibition in these patients, remain unclear. This study aims to explore the differences in response inhibition ability among drug - resistant epilepsy patients, seizure - remission patients, and healthy controls, and to investigate the electrophysiological mechanisms of impaired response inhibition in epilepsy. Methods: The study encompassed 112 participants, including 35 with drug-resistant epilepsy, 37 with seizure-remission, and 40 healthy controls. We employed a stop-signal task and electroencephalogram assess response inhibition in individuals with epilepsy. Event-related potentials and event-related oscillations were used to investigate the neurophysiological mechanisms underlying these responses. Results: The stop signal reaction time of drug-resistant epilepsy patients was markedly extended. The stop signal reaction time of the seizure-remission, while shorter than that of the drug-resistant epilepsy group, remained longer than that of the healthy controls. In the stop trial, the latency of the N2 component in drug-resistant epilepsy and in seizure-remission was significantly prolonged, the amplitudes of N2 and P300 were diminished, and theta oscillations were attenuated. Conclusions: The drug-resistant epilepsy group had prolonged the stop-signal reaction time, with electrophysiological results indicating prolonged latency of N2, reduced amplitude of N2 and P3, and decreased theta oscillations. The seizure-remission group still had residual impairment in response inhibition despite clinical remission of the episodes.

papers.title: Effect of Evodia rutaecarpa plus oseltamivir in regulating body temperature and inflammatory cytokines in infants and young children with viral fever.
papers.abstract: viral fever is a common acute infectious disease among infants and young children. Oseltamivir, a first-line antiviral drug, has limitations in inflammation regulation. In contrast, Evodia Rutaecarpa (E. Rutaecarpa) has been proven to exert antipyretic effects in traditional Chinese medicine. This study, for the first time, systematically evaluated the efficacy of topical E. Rutaecarpa acupoint preparation plus Oseltamivir in treating viral fever in infants and young children. In this retrospective analysis, we included 60 pediatric cases between the ages of 6 months and 3 years and assigned them 1:1 according to propensity score matching (PSM): a combined group (topical E. Rutaecarpa acupoint application + oral Oseltamivir) and a control group (oral Oseltamivir alone). The treatment course lasted for 5 days. The main outcome measure was antipyretic time and the secondary outcome measures included changes in body temperature at different time points, serum inflammatory factors (tumor necrosis factor-α [TNF-α] and interleukin-6 [IL-6], interleukin-1β [IL-1β], high-sensitivity C-reactive protein [hs-CRP]) levels, treatment comfort score (TCS), sleep quality index (SQI), adverse reactions and parents' satisfaction. The antipyretic time was found to be shorter in the combined group than in the control group. Besides, the combined therapy led to markedly milder body temperature fluctuations at 24 hours and 48 hours, as well as greater decreases in serum inflammatory markers (tumor necrosis factor-α [TNF-α] and interleukin-6 [IL-6]), compared to Oseltamivir monotherapy. Additionally, improved TCS and PSQI scores were found in pediatric patients receiving E. Rutaecarpa + Oseltamivir, together with superior parental satisfaction (P<0.01). The two groups showed no notable difference in the incidence of adverse reactions, with no added burden on liver and kidney functions with the combination therapy. Topical E. Rutaecarpa preparation exerts a three-dimensional effect of "acupoint stimulation‒transdermal drug delivery‒systemic anti-inflammation", synergizing with oral Oseltamivir. This combined therapy demonstrates greater advantages in rapidly reducing fever, regulating inflammation and improving patient comfort.

papers.title: Pharmacological treatment of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children with autism spectrum disorder and epilepsy: Current evidence and safety considerations.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms frequently coexist with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and epilepsy; however, seizure manifestations, antiseizure medication (ASM) effects, sleep disturbances and sensory or emotional factors can complicate diagnosis and treatment. Current evidence on ADHD pharmacotherapy in children with these overlapping conditions was synthesized in a narrative review of English-language clinical studies, reviews and professional guidance published mainly between 2020 and 2025, together with the 2018 International League Against Epilepsy consensus. Interpretation focused on diagnostic differentiation, seizure-related safety, tolerability and functional outcomes. Evidence specifically involving all three conditions remains limited. Methylphenidate has the strongest published support for core ADHD symptoms in children with epilepsy, particularly when seizures are stable and standard therapeutic doses are used. Atomoxetine is an alternative when stimulant treatment is unsuitable or poorly tolerated; alpha-2 adrenergic agonists may address selected symptoms of hyperactivity, impulsivity, or hyperarousal. Antipsychotics can be used for defined ASD-related behavioral indications but should not be regarded as primary ADHD treatments. A proposed clinical pathway links multisource diagnostic confirmation, seizure and ASM baseline assessment, individualized medication selection, gradual titration, seizure diaries, monitoring of sleep, appetite, growth, vital signs and mood and functional feedback from caregivers and schools. The suggested pathway provides an organizational aid rather than a validated risk prediction instrument. Medication decisions should prioritize demonstrable improvements in participation, learning and safety while maintaining neurological follow-up.

papers.title: A protocol for a prospective single-arm feasibility study of preoperative home-based hydrogen gas inhalation in liver surgery.
papers.abstract: Hydrogen therapy has been reported to exert antioxidative and anti-inflammatory effects and has attracted increasing clinical interest across various medical fields. In cancer treatment, a waiting period often exists between the treatment decision and surgery; however, structured and evidence-based preoperative interventions during this interval remain limited. Home-based hydrogen gas inhalation, which enables long-duration, repeated administration, may represent a feasible and practical strategy for preoperative optimization. This study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of a standardized home-based hydrogen gas inhalation protocol in patients scheduled for liver resection. This is a prospective, single-center, single-arm, open-label exploratory clinical trial with a planned enrollment of eight participants. Eligible patients scheduled for liver resection will undergo home-based hydrogen gas inhalation during sleep and, additionally, for approximately 1 hour each morning and evening for 14 consecutive days in the preoperative waiting period. The primary endpoint is feasibility, defined as protocol adherence based on predefined inhalation duration criteria. Safety will be assessed by the incidence of adverse events. Secondary and exploratory assessments include changes in inflammation-related, immune-related, and nutrition-related indices, oxidative stress markers, body composition parameters, questionnaire-based quality of life, and tumor markers. This study is registered in the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCT: jRCTs062250073). This study protocol is designed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of preoperative home-based hydrogen gas inhalation and to generate preliminary data to inform the design of subsequent clinical trials investigating its potential role in perioperative care for liver surgery.

papers.title: Senxor: A Real-time Acoustic Decision-support System for Bone Layer Discrimination in Rib Remodeling Surgery.
papers.abstract: Ultrasound-guided monocortical rib reshaping is a minimally invasive technique; nevertheless, for surgeons in training, safe advancement toward the inner cortex remains a significant technical challenge. In this context, ultrasound enables precise anatomic identification of the ribs and accurate preoperative planning of the fracture site, provides real-time intraoperative guidance during access and advancement of the piezotome, and allows the confirmation of both the monocortical nature of the osteotomy and its angulation; however, it does not permit continuous discrimination of bony planes during active cutting. We propose a compact, autonomous, and wireless acoustic sensing system based on a microelectromechanical systems microphone and embedded processing, capable of real-time capture and analysis of acoustic emissions generated during piezotome-bone interaction. Spectral analysis based on the fast Fourier transform, combined with a deterministic algorithm, enables discrimination between cortical and cancellous bone by classifying 3 operational states and providing immediate feedback through a red, green, and blue light-emitting diode signal. The system, called Senxor, operates without physical coupling and is designed to complement ultrasound guidance. Its functionality was preliminarily evaluated in porcine tissue as a proof-of-concept model.
papers.journal: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open

papers.title: Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms in Psoriatic Arthritis: Prevalence and Associations With Sleep, Lifestyle, and Inflammatory Markers.
papers.abstract: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are clinically important but frequently under-recognized comorbidities in psoriatic arthritis (PsA). We aimed to estimate the prevalence of anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients with PsA and to explore their associations with demographic, lifestyle, sleep, treatment-related, and inflammatory characteristics. This single-center analytical cross-sectional study included 110 adults receiving treatment for PsA at a specialist rheumatology clinic in Bengaluru, India. Participants completed the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Scores of 8-10 and 11-21 on either subscale were classified as borderline and abnormal, respectively; a score of at least 8 was considered screening-positive. Clinical, lifestyle, treatment, baseline erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and self-reported sleep data were obtained from the study dataset. Associations were tested using two-sided Pearson chi-square tests; exploratory paired sleep responses were assessed with the continuity-corrected McNemar chi-square test. The mean age was 47.4 years (SD 13.7), and 67 participants (60.9%) were women. Twenty-nine participants screened positive for anxiety (26.4%; 95% CI 18.4-35.6), 22 for depression (20.0%; 95% CI 13.0-28.7), and 18 for both (16.4%; 95% CI 10.0-24.6). Baseline sleep disturbance was significantly more frequent among participants with depressive symptoms than among those without depressive symptoms (77.3% vs. 47.7%; Pearson χ²(1)=6.18; p=0.013). Sleep disturbance was also more frequent among participants with anxiety symptoms (69.0% vs 48.1%), although this association did not reach statistical significance (Pearson χ²(1)=3.72; p=0.054). In an exploratory retrospective self-reported comparison, sleep disturbance was reported by 53.6% of participants before treatment and 1.8% after treatment (continuity-corrected McNemar χ²(1)=55.02; p<0.001); this was not a formal prospective follow-up assessment. Approximately one in four participants screened positive for anxiety and one in five for depression. Depressive symptoms were associated with disturbed sleep, whereas baseline ESR and CRP did not distinguish participants with and without psychological symptoms. Routine screening and multidisciplinary assessment may help identify unmet mental health needs in PsA; longitudinal studies with validated disease activity and sleep measures are required.

papers.title: A case of dissociative disorder with attenuation of EEG alpha power during a depersonalization episode.
papers.abstract: Dissociative disorders are characterized by disruptions in consciousness, memory, identity, and perception. Similar symptoms can occur in patients with frontal lobe epilepsy. Although dissociative disorders are generally classified as psychiatric conditions, several studies have reported electroencephalogram (EEG) abnormalities in only a small proportion of affected patients. The relationship between EEG abnormalities and dissociative symptoms remains poorly understood; further accumulation of similar cases is therefore required. We present the case of an adolescent female with a dissociative disorder, who had experienced depersonalization symptoms since childhood and developed recurrent episodes following COVID-19. The available clinical, magnetic resonance imaging, and scalp video-EEG findings did not support a diagnosis of epilepsy. Inpatient 24-h video-EEG monitoring at age 15 revealed a widespread reduction in alpha power across the brain during an episode of depersonalization. Previous studies have implicated alpha power in the maintenance of stable perceptual states. In this case, quantitative EEG analysis captured a transient widespread reduction in alpha power coinciding with the patient's depersonalization symptoms. Although the specificity, causality, and reproducibility of this finding remain unknown, it may reflect the patient's dissociative symptoms. This case report suggests that a patient's subjective experiences can be captured using objective neurophysiological measures such as EEG.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences

papers.title: Applications of sensor-based technologies in vegetable crops: a narrative review.
papers.abstract: Sensor-based technologies are increasingly used in vegetable crops to characterize plant traits, monitor crop health, and assess quality throughout the production cycle. Conventional approaches for measuring plant traits and crop performance remain constrained by low throughput, high labor requirements, and subjective variability. Recent advances in sensing and imaging technologies have enabled precise, non-destructive, high-throughput, and spatially and temporally resolved assessment of vegetable crops. This narrative review provides a detailed synthesis of sensor-based technologies and their applications in vegetable crop phenotyping, with emphasis on morphological, physiological, biochemical, and physical trait phenotyping, as well as preharvest stress and health monitoring and postharvest assessment. Major imaging and sensing modalities, including RGB, multispectral and hyperspectral imaging, thermal and fluorescence imaging, LiDAR, VIS-NIR spectroscopy, and wearable and flexible sensors, are discussed in terms of their principles, capabilities, applications, and limitations. The integration of these sensors with proximal platforms (handheld and ground-based systems) and remote platforms such as unmanned aerial vehicles enables multi-scale data acquisition and rapid monitoring of crop performance. Data processing and analytical approaches, including image and spectral analysis, machine learning, and deep learning, are discussed as important components for extracting meaningful information from sensor-derived data. Key challenges, such as sensor calibration, environmental variability, data integration, and model transferability, are also discussed. Overall, the review highlights the expanding role of sensor-based technologies in vegetable crop phenotyping, crop monitoring, and postharvest assessment and provides a decision matrix to guide the selection of sensing strategies according to crop group, target trait, and spatial scale, recognizing that suitable combinations depend on the specific applications and conditions.

papers.title: Source-reconstructed EEG graph signal processing: Pitfalls and workarounds.
papers.abstract: Graph signal processing (GSP) enables studying brain structure-function coupling by examining how functional signals vary on the structural connectome (SC). While traditionally used with fMRI, GSP applied to electroencephalography (EEG) is gaining interest due to EEG's repertoire of brain activities and higher temporal resolution. To this aim, source activities are reconstructed through electrical source imaging (ESI), summarized into parcellated time series via singular value decomposition (SVD), and analyzed using graph Fourier transform based on SC Laplacian's eigenvectors. This study investigates two methodological biases: SVD polarity ambiguity and ESI spatial leakage. Using simulated epileptic spikes, we validated a method to resolve SVD sign ambiguity and tested it on real interictal epileptogenic discharges. We then quantified the leakage effect on simulation, by comparing graph power spectra between ground truth and its ESI reconstruction, across inverse solutions (exact low-resolution electrical tomography [eLORETA], vs. linear constraint minimal variance) conditions (baseline vs. spike), and connectomes (structural vs. Euclidean distance-based [EC]). We found that uncorrected polarity ambiguity increases high-frequency content, a bias mitigated by the proposed sign control. Conversely, ESI leakage inflates low-frequency content, with stronger effect during spikes, for eLORETA and EC. These results suggest caution in GSP-EEG analyses and inform analytical pipeline selection.

papers.title: Editorial: The brain and social interactions: from paradigms of social emotion recognition to hyperscanning.
Sleep Physiology and Psychomotor Vigilance Across 2,200 m and 3,700 m in Clinically Healthy Adults: A Within-Subject Study.
papers.abstract: To characterize sleep physiology and psychomotor vigilance at 2200 m and 3700 m and explore associations with overnight vigilance changes. Clinically healthy adults underwent overnight polysomnography (PSG) and 10-minute pre-sleep and post-sleep psychomotor vigilance tests (PVT), first in Xining (2200 m) and then in Yushu (3700 m). Paired PSG, four-session PVT and linked analyses included 27, 26 and 23 participants, respectively. Post hoc analyses covered 17 sleep measures, eight PVT measures and 56 contrasts, including differences in overnight changes (DiD). Associations were adjusted for body mass index (BMI), sex, residential altitude and high-altitude exposure history. Estimates, pointwise 95% confidence intervals (CIs), uncorrected p values and multiplicity-adjusted values were reported. Eleven of 17 sleep measures had uncorrected p<0.05 and Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) q<0.05. Mean oxygen saturation was 8.32% points lower in Yushu (95% CI -9.26 to -7.40; p<0.001; q<0.001). The total-sleep-time difference was -22.53 minutes (95% CI -47.44 to 0.82; p=0.0838; q=0.1187). Fastest 10% reaction time increased overnight in Yushu by 12.81 ms (95% CI 6.18 to 19.59; p=0.0016; q=0.0507); its DiD was 13.50 ms (95% CI 1.67 to 25.29; p=0.0325; q=0.3899). Five of 56 PVT contrasts had p<0.05; none had BH q<0.05. Among 408 primary associations, 32 had p<0.05; only a Xining heart-rate association had global BH and Holm values below 0.05. No Yushu-night or change-coupling association met either threshold. Paired assessments identified physiological changes after further ascent. Behavioral and association estimates remain uncertain and do not establish a mechanism for Yushu overnight vigilance changes.

papers.title: Cold Compression Devices Have Limited Effect on Opioid Consumption and Pain After Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair Compared With Ice Wraps Alone.
papers.abstract: To assess the impact of cold compression devices (CCDs) compared with standard ice pack therapy on opioid use, pain, and sleep after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair. Patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair over a 15-month period were enrolled into this prospective, randomized controlled trial. The control group received standard postoperative care, including an opioid prescription, sling immobilization, and physical therapy, with instructions for ice pack use daily. The CCD group received the same care with instructions for CCD use instead of ice packs. Subjects self-reported opioid consumption and pain (via visual analog scale) daily for 35 days postoperatively. The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index was performed pre- and postoperatively. Thirty-six patients were included in the opioid and pain analyses and 29 in the sleep analysis. The CCD group experienced a steeper slope of decline in morphine milligram equivalents (MMEs) consumed (CCD: -1.42/day, P < .001; control: -1.32/day, P < .001) and visual analog scale pain scores (CCD: -0.15/day, P < .001; control: -0.09/day, P = .039), but each was similar to that of the control group (MME: P = .42; visual analog scale: P = .20). Peak difference in opioid consumption occurred on postoperative day 7 (control MME-CCD MME = 7.57; P = .305). Hours of sleep per night (CCD: mean = 6.4, standard deviation [SD] = 1.2; control: mean = 6.1, SD = 1.2; P = .5848) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores (CCD: mean = 2.8, SD = 0.6; control: mean = 2.3, SD = 0.8; P = .07) were similar between groups. No significant differences in opioid use, pain, or sleep were observed between patients using ice packs versus a CCD postoperatively. Level II, low-quality prospective randomized controlled trial.

papers.title: Effects of a virtual reality-based nature video intervention on sleep quality and mental well-being in patients with multiple sclerosis: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Sleep quality and mental health are negatively affected in many patients with multiple sclerosis (MS). The study was conducted to evaluate the effects of virtual reality (VR) on sleep quality and mental well-being. The study was designed as a randomized controlled trial. Data were collected from patients with MS who presented to a hospital in Türkiye. The study was completed by 21 participants in the experimental group and 22 participants in the control group. Participants in the experimental group watched nature videos using VR headsets for 6 weeks. Participants completed the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-Being Scale (WEMWBS). The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT06074419). Baseline PSQI and WEMWBS scores were similar between the experimental and control groups (p > 0.05). After the 6-week intervention, the mean total PSQI score was significantly lower in the experimental group than in the control group (p = 0.024), with a moderate-to-large effect size (Cohen's d = 0.679), indicating improved sleep quality. Additionally, the mean WEMWBS score was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p = 0.047), with a moderate-to-large effect size (Cohen's d = 0.687), indicating improved mental well-being. Overall, the VR-based nature video intervention was associated with improvements in sleep quality and mental well-being. The VR-based nature video intervention may enhance the quality of nursing care for patients with MS. While the VR-based nature video intervention may enhance nursing care for patients with MS, the absence of any intervention in the comparison group prevents the specific effects of VR from being fully distinguished from placebo or novelty effects. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted with caution. Further research is required to confirm these findings and support their implementation in clinical practice.

papers.title: Brain-body dynamics are asymmetric and stable across cognitive states.
papers.abstract: The human body displays slow, correlated fluctuations in brain activity, autonomic physiology, and incidental behavior. These fluctuations are commonly linked to arousal and cognition, yet it remains unclear whether they reflect task-dependent reconfiguration of brain-body interactions or arise from a stable endogenous dynamic. Here, we used a multivariate dynamical systems approach to analyze simultaneously recorded neural activity, autonomic physiology, and behavior during rest and during attentive and distracted listening to spoken narratives. We found that narrative listening did not substantially alter the endogenous dynamics observed during rest. Instead, peripheral physiology and behavior predicted cortical activity more reliably than the reverse, revealing a pronounced directional asymmetry. In contrast, stimulus-driven physiological responses were primarily mediated by cortical processing rather than direct autonomic drive. Together, these findings indicate that slow brain-body dynamics are stable across cognitive states and provide a structured context through which narratives influence physiology.

papers.title: Participant characteristics and health- and work-related outcomes associated with persistent musculoskeletal pain and common comorbidities: A cross-sectional study of UK biobank data.
papers.abstract: Persistent musculoskeletal (MSK) pain is prevalent and often co-occurs with other chronic conditions, which complicates clinical management. To examine the interaction between persistent MSK pain and common comorbidities for a range of participant characteristics and health- and work-related outcomes. A cross-sectional analysis of UK Biobank data. Persistent MSK pain was defined as self-reported pain lasting >3 months. We identified seven prevalent comorbidities spanning multiple body systems (asthma, headache, cancer, cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes mellitus, mental health conditions, and thyroid disease). Interaction effects between persistent MSK pain and comorbidities were assessed across participant characteristics (socioeconomic deprivation, BMI, physical activity, alcohol use, smoking, sleep problems) and health- and work-related outcomes (GP mental health visits, work status, pain medication use). Of the full cohort (N=498,531) (mean age 56.5 (SD 8.1)), females comprised 54%, and 38% reported persistent MSK pain. Among people with persistent MSK pain, 33.1% had no comorbidities, while 66.9% had ≥1. Interaction effects were generally small and varied by outcomes but were consistent across comorbidities. When pooled over all other comorbidities, average interaction estimates were statistically greater than expected for socioeconomic deprivation (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.07; 1.12), BMI (OR 1.08, 95% CI 1.06 to 1.09), and physical inactivity (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.00; 1.10), and statistically lower than expected for alcohol consumption (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.89; 0.93). Having both persistent MSK pain and one of seven prevalent comorbidities was associated with lifestyle and social characteristics, but generally not with health- and work-related outcomes.

papers.title: A Multiscale Neural Interfacing Device for Cross-Brain-Region Electrophysiology.
papers.abstract: Elucidating brain network dynamics requires simultaneous, cross-scale decoding of local field potentials (LFPs) and single-neuron spiking across distributed regions. However, current electrophysiological systems often force trade-offs among channel count, noise performance, and real-time processing, limiting comprehensive recordings in behaving animals. To address this, we developed a miniaturized, 128-channel-capable modular architecture integrating a low-noise analog front end and a real-time cascaded comb filter, achieving an input-referred noise of ~3.0 μVrms for broadband spikes and 2.6 μVrms in the LFP band. The system features a highly lightweight headstage (weighing only 1.3 g per 64-channel core module) with on-board signal digitization and supports highly reconfigurable, dual-mode (wireless/wired) data transmission, ensuring robust data acquisition across diverse experimental scenarios (anesthetized or freely moving). System utility was first rigorously validated through independent in vivo state evaluations, confirming high-fidelity extractions of LFP and full-bandwidth spikes. Furthermore, simultaneous dual-region recordings (N = 5 mice) in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and dorsal CA1 (dCA1) demonstrated robust macroscopic regional synchronization (low-frequency coherence in the 0.5 to 5 Hz band). Crucially, integrative analyses revealed significant micro-to-macro cross-scale coupling, wherein dCA1 single-unit spikes were tightly phase-locked to the low-frequency rhythmic phase of NAc LFPs (paired t test, P = 0.0032). By delivering synchronized, versatile acquisition down to <1 μs precision, this device establishes a robust framework to bridge the gap between mesoscale network oscillations and microscale cellular computations.

papers.title: Healthcare professionals' experiences with discrimination in clinical settings: Advancing the discussion.
papers.abstract: Although discrimination against patients in clinical settings is well documented, an increasing number of healthcare professionals (HCPs), especially physicians and nurses, report experiencing discrimination and harassment themselves. These experiences lead to serious consequences such as burnout, depression, and job loss. Despite numerous proposed strategies, incidents continue to rise, highlighting the urgent need to critically evaluate and improve existing interventions. In addition, ambiguity surrounding the definition and historical origins of "discrimination" highlights the importance of conceptual clarity in guiding effective solutions. To critically synthesize available evidence about discrimination encountered by HCPs, explicate the conceptual foundations by exploring the historical roots of the term discrimination, and assess proposed strategies to mitigate discrimination within healthcare environments. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and gray literature sources (e.g. books and professional association guidelines). Relevant materials were identified, synthesized, and organized into thematic sections of the article. Drawing from historical foundations and scholarly perspectives, six core elements consistently appear in definitions of discrimination. Based on these, we propose the following definition: "discrimination involves unjustified differential treatment of individuals or groups, based on attributes associated with social group membership, using a standard of comparison that results in unfair disadvantage and is expressed through communication, actions, or institutional structures." HCPs are discriminated against in healthcare environments through overt or subtle behaviors and policies of institutions. Consequences include lower motivation, job dissatisfaction, emotional strain, fatigue, sleep problems, and reduced care quality. While interventions such as neutral reporting systems, education, and respect-based initiatives are documented in literature, their effectiveness requires continuous evaluation and improvements and putting in place other strategies. Discrimination against HCPs remains a global challenge requiring diverse and context-specific strategies to mitigate it. Strengthening conceptual clarity around the term "discrimination" is essential for effective interventions. We recommend that institutions adopt integrated strategies rather than relying on single measures to address discrimination cases and prioritize ongoing evaluation of organizational policies aimed at supporting affected personnel. Collaborative engagement among healthcare organizations, policymakers, stakeholders, and society is key to eradicating discrimination and creating an inclusive healthcare system.

papers.title: Psychometric properties and validation of the Hungarian version of the Sleep Hygiene Index among healthcare professionals.
papers.abstract: This study aims to culturally adapt and validate the Hungarian version of the Sleep Hygiene Index (SHI-H) among healthcare professionals and evaluate associated demographic, occupational, and psychological factors. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among Hungarian nurses and physicians (n = 470). Psychometric evaluation included internal consistency, test-retest reliability (n = 21), exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. Sleep hygiene was evaluated against age, gender, and work schedule. Psychological profiling utilized the Hungarian version of reduced Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (rMEQ-H), Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS-H), Perceived Stress Scale-14 (PSS-14-H), and Patient Health Questionnaire-15 (PHQ-15-H), analyzed via multivariable General Linear Modeling (GLM) and bootstrap mediation analyses. The SHI-H demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.727) and excellent temporal stability (ICC = 0.85). Construct validity was supported by a preliminary five-factor structure (CFI = 0.928, TLI = 0.900, RMSEA = 0.053, 90% CI: 0.041-0.065), reflecting multidimensional sleep behaviors. The GLM explained 34.9% of the total variance in SHI-H scores (p < 0.001). Chronotype (rMEQ-H) emerged as the strongest independent predictor (ηp2 = 0.090, p < 0.001), with morningness linked to superior sleep hygiene. Shift workers reported significantly poorer sleep hygiene (p < 0.001) and greater insomnia severity (p = 0.016) than day workers. Furthermore, bootstrap mediation analyses revealed a significant indirect statistical association, indicating that the relationship between morningness-eveningness orientation (rMEQ-H) and insomnia severity (AIS-H) was accounted for by sleep hygiene behaviors (SHI-H) within this cross-sectional model. The SHI-H is a reliable, psychometrically sound instrument for healthcare populations. Sleep-related behaviors are heavily influenced by chronotype and shiftwork demands, showing significant indirect associations with insomnia symptoms.

papers.title: Clinical trial exit interviews in patients with moderate-to-severe chronic hand eczema: perspectives on disease burden and treatment experiences with delgocitinib cream in the phase III DELTA 1 trial.
papers.abstract: Delgocitinib cream showed superior efficacy vs. cream vehicle in patients with moderate-to-severe chronic hand eczema (CHE) in pivotal phase III studies. Qualitative clinical trial exit interviews can be utilized to explore patient experiences, supplementing trial results by providing insight into patient perspectives on disease burden and treatment experience. To explore patient insights into CHE and treatment experience with delgocitinib cream. DELTA 1 (NCT04871711) was a phase III trial in which adults with moderate-to-severe CHE received double-blind treatment with delgocitinib cream 20 mg g-1 or cream vehicle twice daily for 16 weeks. Patients enrolled in Canada or the UK were invited to participate in a semistructured exit interview within 2 weeks of completing treatment at 16 weeks. These were conducted using open-ended questions, and data were analysed using thematic analyses to identify key themes related to disease burden and treatment impact. A total of 27 patients were interviewed [mean (SD) age 43.5 (14.0) years, 67% (n = 18) women]. The most frequently reported signs and symptoms of CHE before the trial were cracking, pain, dryness, itch and flaking. Participants described significant impacts on activities of daily living, emotional wellbeing, work, physical functioning, sleep and social functioning. Most participants who received delgocitinib cream described improvements in signs and symptoms and noted a positive impact across multiple quality-of-life domains. These exit interviews provide additional understanding of the lived experiences of patients with CHE, highlighting the profound impact on daily life and improvements achieved with treatment beyond that measured with clinician and patient-reported efficacy endpoints.

papers.title: An EMG-driven virtual reality platform for physiology-based motor interaction: technical and functional validation.
papers.abstract: Harnessing experience-dependent neuroplasticity has become a central goal of modern neurorehabilitation. Immersive virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising tool, enabling task-oriented training in ecologically valid scenarios that are difficult to reproduce in conventional clinical settings. Despite these advances, interaction in most existing VR rehabilitation systems remains primarily mediated by external interfaces, such as motion tracking or handheld controllers, rather than by the user's own physiological motor activity. Consequently, rehabilitation often fails to directly engage the physiological motor commands that naturally drive voluntary movement. We present and validate an integrated VR-electromyography (VR-EMG) platform that enables closed-loop, physiology-driven interaction between users and immersive virtual environments. The platform combines a standalone VR architecture with wearable EMG systems, online EMG decoding, and cloud-based performance monitoring within a unified framework.
