A standardized motor-command interface enables different EMG acquisition systems to control both anthropomorphic and non-anthropomorphic virtual effectors without modifying the decoding strategy or rehabilitation scenarios, providing a flexible framework for diverse applications. The platform was validated through complementary technical and functional evaluations performed on the two supported EMG acquisition systems. Technical validation assessed signal quality, gesture classification accuracy, communication latency, and system reliability. Functional validation was conducted in individuals with upper-limb amputation and able-bodied controls while performing object-interaction tasks across multiple immersive virtual scenarios. The platform demonstrated stable closed-loop operation, reliable gesture recognition, and the ability to quantify objective performance metrics, including task score, completion time, gesture classification errors, precision errors, correctly recognized gestures, and user-reported workload. Findings demonstrate the feasibility, technical reliability, and functional versatility of the proposed platform by providing a physiology-driven framework for immersive motor interaction that is compatible with different EMG acquisition systems and dissociates motor control from the morphology of the controlled virtual effector. Because the two systems were used for different components of the validation, we do not establish equivalence in their performance. By integrating online EMG decoding, VR, and quantitative performance monitoring, the platform offers a tool for future applications in rehabilitation, prosthetic training, and studies using functional magnetic resonance imaging and high-density electroencephalography to address whether training with the platform induces changes in functional brain organization.

papers.title: From hemodynamics to function: the role of fNIRS and hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems in next-generation assistive technologies for rehabilitation.
papers.abstract: Assistive technologies (AT) serve as fundamental tools for rehabilitation because they help people with neurological or physical disabilities to restore their abilities, independence and their overall life satisfaction. Existing AT control methods, which include manual operation, eye tracking, voice commands, electromyography (EMG) and electroencephalography (EEG), have improved rehabilitation results but still face challenges because of their inability to maintain reliable performance during user exhaustion and difficulties operating in challenging situations. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has recently become a new neuroimaging technique that provides excellent imaging capability, can be used while moving, and has portable design features. fNIRS-based devices such as wheelchairs, robotic prostheses, and brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have proven their ability to decode user intention and assist rehabilitation. The limited ability of fNIRS to measure time intervals prevents its use in real-time systems. The hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems combine EEG technology, which provides high-speed temporal measurements, with fNIRS technology, which provides spatial and hemodynamic measurements. The multimodal techniques combine different measurement methods, which improve accuracy while decreasing false positive results and increasing system adaptability. This review critically examines how AT control modalities have been evolving, and it also measures what fNIRS can do technically, plus what it struggles with, and then it pulls together the available evidence on hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems as a possible way toward more adaptive, user-centered rehabilitation technologies.

papers.title: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition network based on moment channel attention.
papers.abstract: While most cross-subject EEG emotion recognition studies focus on average accuracy, the high inter-subject variability of EEG signals causes severe performance inconsistency across individuals. This inconsistency poses a critical barrier to real-world deployment but has received insufficient attention. To address this issue, this study proposes a hybrid emotion recognition model integrating moment channel attention and Transformer, termed the Moment Attention Convolution-Emotion Transformer Network (MAC-ETN). The proposed hybrid network consists of three components: a local temporal feature extractor, a Moment Channel Attention Network (MCA), and a global temporal feature extractor. Specifically, depthwise and separable convolutions are employed to extract local temporal features. The moment channel attention mechanism incorporates the first-order moment (mean), second-order moment (variance), and third-order moment (skewness) for channel importance calibration; and global dependency modeling is achieved through a Transformer encoder. Performance evaluation is conducted on two public datasets, DEAP and MAHNOB-HCI, using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV). The experimental results show that the main advantage of MAC-ETN lies in markedly reduced cross-subject performance variability rather than higher mean accuracy. On the DEAP dataset, the mean accuracy of MAC-ETN (61.26% for arousal and 60.47% for valence is lower than that of the strongest baselines reported under the same LOSO protocol, while its accuracy standard deviation (7.88% and 5.31%) is the lowest among all compared methods. On the MAHNOB-HCI dataset, the F1 standard deviation of MAC-ETN is 1.48% for arousal and 0.30% for valence, far below the values reported for the baselines in the literature, although the latter were obtained under a subject-dependent protocol and with a different F1 definition, so this comparison is indicative only. These results indicate that MAC-ETN reduces cross-subject performance variability at a moderate level of accuracy, which is relevant for practical EEG-based emotion recognition applications.

papers.title: Depression is associated with endometrial polyp occurrence and convergent gut microbiota-mitochondrial alterations: a multi-omics case-control study.
papers.abstract: Endometrial polyps (EPs) affect 7.8%-34.9% of women and cause abnormal uterine bleeding and reproductive failure, yet their pathogenesis is unclear. Depression is over-represented among women with EPs but is usually read as reactive distress; whether that association involves the gut microbiota and mitochondrial biology is unknown. We combined a hospital-based case-control analysis (n = 466), faecal full-length 16S rRNA and blood leukocyte RNA-seq in 30 participants (PD n = 11, PND n = 12, NPND n = 7), and a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model with bacterial supplementation. Depression was significantly associated with higher odds of EP in the full cohort (unadjusted OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.55-3.34; P < 0.001), and this trend remained stable following confounder adjustment, propensity-score matching and multiple sensitivity analyses. Signals were partitioned into EP-specific, depression-specific and dual-associated classes. In the EP-specific class, predicted microbial functions showed less electron-transfer gene content (complexes I-II), while host ETC subunits spanning complexes I, III and IV (NDUFA1, UQCRH, COX6B1, COX7A2) were coordinately downregulated and CCR2, CCR5 and UMPS upregulated, with enrichment for oxidative phosphorylation. Dual-associated signals comprised higher Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and lower Eggerthella lenta, negatively correlated (Kendall τ = -0.37, P = 0.007; PD > PND > NPND), together with downregulation of GDF15, HIC1, TCF7L2 and ICAM1. In mice, restraint stress was accompanied by stromal proliferation exceeding that in estradiol-treated controls and by reduced uterine TOMM20; oral F. prausnitzii given after stress was associated with higher TOMM20 and lower proliferation, whereas E. lenta was not. These findings place a convergent gut microbiota-mitochondrial axis at the intersection of depression and endometrial proliferation, and nominate candidate taxa and transcripts for hypothesis-driven validation. Limitations: multi-omics profiling included 30 participants (11, 12 and 7) with no depression-only cell; microbial functions were predicted by PICRUSt2 and no metabolite was measured; medication use, diet, physical activity, sleep and hormonal status were incompletely captured; and each bacterial group contained three animals. The axis proposed here is therefore hypothesis-generating and requires longitudinal, metabolomic and tissue-specific validation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

papers.title: Association Between Vitamin Knowledge, Practices, and Sleep Quality Among Undergraduate Students at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Sleep disruptions are prevalent among university students and negatively impact well-being. Vitamins, including B6, B12, and D, support sleep regulation via neurotransmitter synthesis and circadian pathways. However, empirical data evaluating student literacy and dietary practices regarding these micronutrients remain scarce in low-resource African settings. This study aimed to evaluate vitamin-related knowledge and practices, examine their associations with self-reported sleep parameters, and determine the sociodemographic factors associated with vitamin knowledge among undergraduate students at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana. A cross-sectional survey was conducted between March and May 2025 among 381 undergraduate students recruited via convenience sampling. A validated structured questionnaire captured sociodemographic data, vitamin knowledge, dietary practices, and sleep parameters using an adapted composite sleep scale based on the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression in SPSS version 26. Self-reported sleep disturbances were widespread, characterized by short sleep duration (< 7 h: 59.9%), nocturnal awakenings (45.6%), and daytime fatigue (48.8% at least weekly). The mean vitamin knowledge score was 13.39 (±6.22), with 56.4% classified as having good relative knowledge; health program students demonstrated higher knowledge across multiple domains (p < 0.05). The mean practice score was 4.00 (±0.49), with 60.4% categorized as having good relative practices, although food label checking (13.1% always) and healthcare consultation for supplement use (19.7% always) were low. Mean adapted composite sleep problem scores were significantly lower (more favorable) among students with good vitamin knowledge compared to poor knowledge (t = -2.511, p = 0.012), whereas no significant difference was observed by vitamin practice category (t = 1.048, p = 0.48). In adjusted logistic regression, female sex was associated with lower odds of good vitamin knowledge (aOR = 0.605, 95% CI: 0.382-0.958, p = 0.032), while married status was associated with higher odds (aOR = 3.833, 95% CI: 1.058-13.891, p = 0.041). Self-reported sleep disturbances are prevalent among undergraduate students at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana. Although higher vitamin literacy was associated with fewer self-reported sleep problems, self-reported dietary practices showed no direct association, and notable micronutrient knowledge deficits persisted. Integrated campus wellness initiatives should address both sleep hygiene and practical nutritional literacy, while future research requires biochemical validation and longitudinal designs.

papers.title: Factors Associated With Insomnia Among Medical Students Across Latin America During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Multicenter 2020 Benchmark Study.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted medical education and mental health. This multicenter study examined factors associated with insomnia among medical students from 13 Latin American countries during the first pandemic wave. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted using an online questionnaire. Insomnia was measured with the Insomnia Severity Index. Exposures included physical activity, eating disorder symptoms, burnout, resilience, smoking and alcohol risk, and sociodemographic, educational, and clinical variables. Prevalence ratios with 95% confidence intervals were estimated through regression. Among 2,019 students, the prevalence of insomnia symptoms according to the ISI cutoff was 46.9% (95% CI: 44.7-49.1). Higher prevalence was observed among students who reported being a son or daughter within their family, those with relatives diagnosed or deceased from COVID-19, prior mental health problems, eating disorder symptoms, or smoking risk. Lower prevalence was found among seventh-year students, those with children, those perceiving the pandemic as serious, and students reporting high physical activity or resilience. Almost half of medical students screened positive for insomnia symptoms during the early pandemic. Family COVID-19 impact, prior mental health problems, eating disorder symptoms, and smoking risk were associated factors, while advanced training level, parenthood, physical activity, and resilience were associated with a lower prevalence of insomnia symptoms. These findings provide evidence for sleep health in Latin American medical students and may guide post-pandemic comparisons and interventions.

papers.title: Preliminary clinical experience with combined semaglutide and methylphenidate therapy in young people with Prader-Willi syndrome: A four-patient case series.
papers.abstract: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is associated with severe hyperphagia, obesity and substantial metabolic morbidity. This descriptive, uncontrolled case series reports clinical observations in four young people with genetically confirmed PWS who received semaglutide and extended-release methylphenidate within a multidisciplinary program incorporating inpatient dietary restriction. Outcomes included body weight, body mass index (BMI), caregiver-reported Dykens Hyperphagia Questionnaire (HQ) scores, metabolic parameters and tolerability. At the reported post-treatment assessments, body weight decreased from 54 to 50 kg, 99 to 74 kg, 149 to 130 kg and 82 to 76 kg in patients 1-4, respectively. BMI and HQ scores decreased in all four patients. In the patient with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c decreased from 12.0% to 6.5% and insulin was discontinued while metformin continued, this represents improved glycemic control rather than documented diabetes remission. HbA1c normalized in the three patients with baseline prediabetes. Sleep-related outcomes and liver biochemistry improved in some patients. No serious adverse events requiring permanent treatment discontinuation were reported. Follow-up duration and treatment doses varied, and concomitant inpatient dietary and environmental interventions preclude attribution of the observed changes to either medication or their combination. These preliminary observations warrant prospective controlled evaluation of efficacy, durability and safety.
papers.journal: Therapeutic advances in endocrinology and metabolism

papers.title: System-level challenges and unmet needs in profound autism: an exploratory caregiver survey of non-verbal individuals.
papers.abstract: Individuals with profound autism, particularly those with minimal or absent verbal communication, frequently present with very high levels of clinical complexity and support needs. Despite increasing recognition of this subgroup, little is known about the real-world experiences of families and the adequacy of current service systems in responding to these needs. The present study aimed to characterize the lived experience, clinical complexity, and unmet needs of parents of non-verbal individuals with autism within a defined territorial context. A cross-sectional descriptive survey study was conducted in a defined Italian catchment area. A structured caregiver questionnaire including 128 items across ten thematic domains was administered online. The present analysis was restricted to parents of non-verbal individuals with autism (n = 24), representing the non-verbal subgroup within the broader profound autism population. Domains included diagnostic pathways, medical comorbidities, daily functioning, therapeutic interventions, healthcare access, sensory profile, educational context, and family impact. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and exploratory bivariate analyses. Parents described a profile characterized by severe functional dependence, pervasive communication impairment, and high levels of medical and behavioral complexity. Sleep disturbances were reported in 75.0% of cases, epilepsy in 20.8%, and current pharmacological treatment in 58.3%. Difficulty recognizing medical conditions because of communication limitations was reported as moderate to extreme in 91.7% of cases. Service use was characterized by heavy reliance on private interventions and limited availability of respite care. Public intervention intensity was low, while substantial family-level impacts were reported in caregiver employment and social participation. Aggressive and self-injurious behaviors were common, and more than half of families reported the need for physical containment at least occasionally. The data indicate a potential mismatch between the high and multidimensional support needs of non-verbal individuals with autism and the intensity and availability of formal support. The observed pattern was characterized by low levels of publicly funded intervention, heavy reliance on private care, limited access to respite and home assistance, and marked family-level impacts. These findings support the need to examine how integrated and lifespan-oriented models of care can better address the needs of individuals with profound autism and absent verbal communication.

papers.title: Cognitive load detection using hyper-learning dragonfly optimization for feature selection.
papers.abstract: Cognitive load detection is essential for understanding brain responses to mental effort and cognitive demands. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals provide valuable information about neural activity and offer a non-invasive approach to identifying cognitive load. However, accurate detection and the identification of brain regions with superior discriminative capabilities remain important challenges. This study proposes an EEG-based cognitive load detection framework using empirical Fourier decomposition (EPFD), entropy-based feature extraction, and the hyper-learning binary dragonfly feature selection algorithm (HLBDA). EEG signals recorded from each brain lobe over four-second intervals were decomposed into 10 intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). Entropy-based features were extracted from the IMFs, and the most informative features were selected using HLBDA. The selected features were classified using machine learning (ML) classifiers. The proposed framework was evaluated on the MAT, STEW, and MLR datasets. Additionally, lobe-wise cognitive load detection was performed on the MAT and STEW datasets to investigate the discriminative capabilities of five individual brain lobes. Subject-wise leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) was employed to prevent data leakage. The proposed framework achieved classification accuracies of 97.13%, 96.48%, and 98.2% on the MAT, STEW, and MLR datasets, respectively, using the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) classifier for MAT and STEW and the ensemble subspace KNN (ESSK) classifier for MLR. In the lobe-wise analysis, the frontal lobe demonstrated superior discriminative capability for cognitive load detection, achieving accuracies of 96.7% and 96.6% on the MAT and STEW datasets, respectively, using the ESSK classifier. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed EPFD-HLBDA-based framework for EEG-based cognitive load detection across multiple datasets. The superior performance of the frontal lobe suggests its potential as a particularly informative region for distinguishing cognitive states. Furthermore, the use of subject-wise LOOCV strengthens the evaluation by reducing the risk of data leakage. Compared with recently reported methods, the proposed framework demonstrates competitive classification performance and highlights the potential of lobe-specific EEG analysis for reliable cognitive load assessment.

papers.title: Longitudinal symptom-cluster trajectories and associated factors in patients with peripheral facial paralysis: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: To characterize stage-specific symptom-cluster organization, identify heterogeneous longitudinal trajectories of fixed-core psychological-sleep and fatigue burden, and examine sociodemographic, clinical, psychosocial, and treatment-timing correlates of trajectory membership in patients with peripheral facial paralysis (PFP). In this prospective longitudinal cohort, 283 adults with PFP were assessed during the acute phase and at 1, 3, and 6 months after onset. Principal component analysis described stage-specific symptom-cluster organization. To ensure longitudinal comparability, trajectory analyses used fixed-core symptom-burden composites measured identically at all four assessments: anxiety and disturbed sleep for psychological-sleep burden, and lack of energy, drowsiness, and difficulty concentrating for fatigue burden. Piecewise random-intercept growth-mixture models were estimated in 239 complete cases, with full-information maximum-likelihood (FIML) sensitivity analyses in all 283 participants. Baseline factors associated with the final two-class solutions were examined using multiplicity-aware screening and Firth penalized binary logistic regression. The number of common symptoms decreased from 20 at baseline to 5 at 6 months, and time-specific PCA components were reorganized across recovery. Fixed-core psychological-sleep and fatigue burden both declined overall (Friedman χ 2 = 217.825 and 274.458, respectively; both p < 0.001). Two numerically admissible trajectories were retained for each domain. Psychological-sleep burden comprised an early-decreasing trajectory (n = 199, 83.3%) and a delayed-decreasing trajectory (n = 40, 16.7%); fatigue burden comprised a low-rapid-decreasing trajectory (n = 200, 83.7%) and a high-persistent trajectory (n = 39, 16.3%). FIML analyses in all 283 participants closely reproduced both two-class structures. No robust baseline predictor of psychological-sleep trajectory membership remained after multiplicity correction. For fatigue, autumn/winter onset (OR = 7.049, 95% CI 2.525-23.364), non-acute acupuncture initiation (OR = 11.281, 95% CI 4.625-30.030), and higher MCMQ avoidance scores (OR = 0.646 per point, 95% CI 0.482-0.810) were associated with membership in the high-persistent trajectory. Symptom organization changed across recovery, while fixed-core psychological-sleep and fatigue burden showed two heterogeneous longitudinal courses. The primary class structures were robust to FIML handling of missing repeated measures, although censored-normal sensitivity analyses indicated that latent-class allocation may be sensitive to floor effects, particularly for fatigue. Associations with baseline characteristics should be interpreted as exploratory and non-causal.

papers.title: The prognostic significance of Lipoprotein(a) is modified by obstructive sleep apnea in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
papers.abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established residual cardiovascular risk factor in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), a common cardiometabolic disorder, may modify the association between Lp(a) and cardiovascular outcomes. Therefore, the present study aimed to further evaluate whether OSA statistically modifies the association between Lp(a) and long-term cardiovascular outcomes in a prospective cohort of patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). A total of 1027 consecutive patients who underwent PCI and sleep study were initially screened. After prespecified exclusions, 846 patients were included in the final analysis. Moderate-to-severe OSA was defined as an AHI ≥15 events/h, whereas patients with an AHI <15 events/h constituted the comparison group. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), including cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, heart failure and stroke. During 3.5(2.8-4.2) years of follow-up, 169(19.97%) cardiovascular events occurred. Post-PCI patients who experienced MACEs exhibited significantly higher Lp(a) levels compared to those without MACEs (median 26.50 vs.11.00 mg/dL, P<0.001). Post-PCI patients with high Lp(a)(>30mg/dL) were associated with increased risks of cardiovascular events with hazard ratios of 1.881 (95%CI 1.168-3.029, P<0.001). There was a statistically significant interaction between Lp(a) and OSA status in relation to MACE risk (P for interaction=0.005). Among patients with AHI ≥15 events/h, elevated Lp(a) (>30 mg/dL) was associated with a 2.286-fold higher risk of MACEs compared to Lp(a) (<10 mg/dL), whereas no statistically significant association was observed among patients with AHI <15 events/h. OSA status may statistically modify the association between elevated Lp(a) and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. These findings support further investigation into the prognostic relevance of combined OSA and Lp(a) assessment, while additional studies are needed to validate these observations and determine their implications for clinical practice.

papers.title: Effect of an esketamine-based opioid-sparing perioperative regimen on early postoperative anxiety in women undergoing total laparoscopic hysterectomy: a randomized participant- and outcome-assessor-blinded controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Postoperative anxiety is common after hysterectomy and may impair recovery. We evaluated whether an esketamine-based opioid-sparing perioperative regimen could reduce early postoperative anxiety in women undergoing total laparoscopic hysterectomy. In this single-center, randomized, participant- and outcome-assessor-blinded controlled trial, women aged 45-60 years were assigned 1:1 to Group K or Group C. Group K received an esketamine-based opioid-sparing perioperative regimen comprising esketamine during anesthesia induction and maintenance and esketamine-containing patient-controlled intravenous analgesia, together with lower protocol-specified sufentanil and remifentanil dosing. Group C received a conventional opioid-based perioperative regimen, with normal saline used as the study-drug control. The primary outcome was the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) score on postoperative day 1 (POD 1). Secondary outcomes included POD three anxiety, quality of recovery, pain, sleep, postoperative nausea and vomiting, and neuropsychiatric adverse events. Of 170 randomized patients, 167 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis (83 in Group C and 84 in Group K). POD 1 SAS scores assessed 24 h after surgery were lower in Group K than in Group C, whereas no significant between-group difference was observed at 72 h after surgery (POD 3), after completion of PCIA. Group K also had higher QoR-15 scores, lower POD 1 pain and insomnia scores, and longer device-estimated total and deep sleep duration. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in the incidences of the recorded common adverse events. An esketamine-based opioid-sparing perioperative regimen was associated with lower SAS scores at 24 h after surgery during the early postoperative treatment period; however, this between-group difference was not maintained at 72 h after completion of PCIA. [https://www.chictr.org.cn/historyversionpub.html?regno=ChiCTR2300074484]: identifier [ChiCTR2300074484].

papers.title: Sparse EEG neurodynamics of hypoglycemia in type 1 diabetes with personal euglycemic baseline adaptation.
papers.abstract: Hypoglycemia alters cerebral electrophysiological activity, providing a physiological basis for EEG-based detection. However, translation toward subject-independent monitoring remains constrained by uncertain minimum input requirements, insufficiently characterized stability of sparse representations and their physiological associations, and inter-participant baseline variability. This study benchmarked 24 models spanning engineered-feature machine learning, feature-domain deep learning, and raw-waveform deep learning under leave-one-subject-out validation. Channel-Feature Sparsification was applied using a predefined performance-preservation criterion. Sparse representations were evaluated for selection stability, cross-paradigm concordance, and physiological association. Personal Euglycemic Baseline Adaptation (PEBA) was subsequently applied using a short personal euglycemic reference without participant-specific model retraining. LDA achieved the highest observed balanced accuracy within the engineered-feature paradigm, whereas Sinc-SSNET performed best in both deep-learning paradigms. Sparsification retained the F7 log-theta descriptor for LDA, the F7 channel row for feature-domain Sinc-SSNET, and two channels for raw-waveform Sinc-SSNET. F7 was retained across all three paradigms, and its log-theta descriptor increased during hypoglycemia in 30 of 34 participants (88.2%). PEBA improved balanced accuracy from 0.71 to 0.77 for LDA, from 0.68 to 0.83 for feature-domain Sinc-SSNET, and from 0.71 to 0.78 for raw-waveform Sinc-SSNET. Compared with the corresponding full-input models, reduced configurations decreased parameter counts by 88.51%-99.88%, parameter storage requirements by 87.20%-99.88%, and multiply-accumulate operations by 94.72%-99.91%. These findings demonstrate the preservation of hypoglycemia-related EEG information under a predefined sparsification criterion, while personal euglycemic normalization improves cross-participant discrimination. Physiological consistency and reduced computational requirements support further evaluation of compact EEG-based hypoglycemia detection. Independent cohorts, continuous glycemic-transition recordings, and native sparse EEG acquisition are required before prospective application.

papers.title: Trustworthy AI for multimodal load-response modelling in team sports: a scoping review and full-text validation audit.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), machine-learning and conventional statistical prediction methods are increasingly used in team-sport athlete monitoring, but it remains unclear whether current studies are validated and reported in ways that support trustworthy prospective use. This scoping review mapped predictive-modelling studies in team-sport athlete monitoring and multimodal load-response modelling and audited their validation and reporting practices. Searches were conducted in OpenAlex, PubMed, Scopus and SPORTDiscus for records published from 2010 to 2026. After deduplication, screening and updated OpenAlex rerun screening, 258 studies were included and audited from full text. Systematic duplicate screening was not performed; full-text eligibility assessment and original audit coding were completed by a single reviewer. Data were extracted on publication characteristics, sport context, data modalities, modelled outcomes, model families and validation practices. A 10-domain trustworthy-AI audit assessed prediction context, temporal validity, repeated-observation independence, external validation, leakage control, calibration, class-imbalance handling, interpretability, uncertainty reporting and deployment/actionability. Bibliometric and NLP analyses provided complementary field mapping. A second reviewer independently assessed 45 studies from the original 223-study audit subset across all ten audit domains. The literature expanded rapidly after 2021, with performance modelling and injury-risk prediction as the dominant applications. Studies frequently used GPS/GNSS, session-RPE/internal load, wellness/sleep, HR/HRV, neuromuscular testing, IMU/accelerometry and video-derived features. Random forests, logistic/linear models and gradient boosting were the most common model families. Deployment-relevant validation remained limited. After targeted reassessment and updated-search incorporation, temporal validity was strongly documented in 28 studies (10.9%), while independent external validation was strongly documented in one study (0.4%) and partially documented in one additional study (0.4%). Leakage control, calibration, repeated-observation independence and model-level uncertainty reporting were also uncommon. Pre-correction exact agreement in the independent audit subset was 65.3% overall and varied substantially across domains. Predictive modelling in team-sport athlete monitoring is expanding, but model development has advanced faster than trustworthy validation practice. Future studies should define the intended decision context, preserve temporal and player-level data structure, prevent leakage, report calibration and uncertainty, validate models under realistic deployment conditions and translate outputs into practitioner-facing decision support.
papers.journal: Frontiers in sports and active living

papers.title: Frequency-embedded sequence learning for multi-class EEG-to-text interface.
papers.abstract: A brain-computer interface (BCI) is an emerging technology for decoding users' intentions, enabling speech decoding from electroencephalography (EEG) signals. This study proposes a multi-class (i.e., 5 words or phrases) EEG-to-Text classification pipeline based on a lightweight 1-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) architecture. The model is trained using both time-domain EEG signals and frequency-embedded power spectral density (PSD) sequences, facilitating systematic comparison of feature representations. EEG signals were preprocessed using a bandpass filter (4 - 120 Hz) and a notch filter (60 Hz) followed by PSD estimation using the modified Welch method. The processed signals were then used to train the proposed 1D-CNN architecture designed for sequential data. In intra-subject evaluation, the proposed approach achieves classification accuracies (mean ± standard deviation) of 46.1 ± 5.1 and 64.4 ± 8.3 using time-domain EEG signals and frequency-embedded PSD sequences, respectively. Peak intra-subject accuracies reach 54% and 82% using EEG signals and PSD sequences, respectively. For inter-subject (pairwise) evaluation, the best observed accuracy is 42%. Inter-subject (pooled) performance remains near chance level (23.3 ± 1.0 and 24.5 ± 0.4), highlighting inter-subject generalization as a key challenge in EEG-based BCI systems. These results demonstrate that while intra-subject performance is promising, inter-subject generalization remains a major limitation. Overall, the proposed approach demonstrates the potential of frequency-embedded PSD representations for improving EEG-based imagined speech classification, while motivating further work toward robust, user-independent BCI systems.

papers.title: The role of the right temporal lobe in neural network mechanisms during working memory encoding.
papers.abstract: Visual working memory (vWM) impairment is common in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) and is more severe in those with right TLE (RTLE), suggesting the significant role of right temporal lobe in WM processes. We recruited patients with left TLE (LTLE group, n = 20), RTLE (RTLE group, n = 20) and 35 healthy controls (Control), and examined their vWM performance while simultaneously recording task-based EEG. The alterations in the neural oscillations and neural network were analyzed during the WM encoding phase. In addition, we examined the relationship between the neural oscillations and WM performance, as well as the relationship between the neural network and WM performance, to further explore the role of the right temporal lobe in WM encoding. Remarkably lower accuracy (both p < 0.001) and significantly longer response times (LTLE vs. Control: p = 0.026; RTLE vs. Control: p < 0.001) were found in both LTLE and RTLE groups compared with controls. The RTLE group experienced notably delayed response time in comparison to the LTLE group (p = 0.026). In comparison to the LTLE group, the RTLE group displayed reduced theta power spectral density for the frontal (p = 0.024) and occipital (p = 0.011) regions, along with the Fz channel (p = 0.047). DTFF_outflow and DTFFz_outflow values in the RTLE group displayed reduction relative to the LTLE group (DTFF_outflow:p = 0.026; DTFFz_outflow: p = 0.037). The LTLE group showed weakened information flow from Fz to P3 (IFFz → P3, ANOVA, F = 3.45, p = 0.037; LSD, LTLE vs. Control: p = 0.013), whereas the RTLE group exhibited weakened information flow from Fz to P4 (IFFz → P4; ANOVA, F = 3.78, p = 0.028; LSD, RTLE vs. Control: p = 0.029), Fz to T4 (IFFz → T4; ANOVA, F = 4.67, p = 0.012; LSD, RTLE vs. Control: p = 0.009), and Fz to TP8 (IFFz → TP8; ANOVA, F = 3.11, p = 0.050; LSD, RTLE vs. Control: p = 0.017), which were positively associated with accuracy and inversely associated with response time. Abnormal information transfer from the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex to the superior parietal lobe during the encoding phase may causes WM deficits; damage to information transfer from the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex to the right middle temporal and right inferior temporal gyri exacerbates WM impairments.

papers.title: Mindfulness during exercise, positive mental health, and psychological resilience in older adults: serial indirect associations through sleep regularity, self-control, and quality of life.
papers.abstract: Mindfulness during exercise involves present-moment awareness and attentional regulation during physical activity and may be relevant to psychological functioning in later life. However, the cross-sectional associations linking mindfulness during exercise (ME) with positive mental health (PMH) and psychological resilience (PR) through sleep regularity (SR), self-control (SC), and quality of life (QL) remain insufficiently understood. This study examined the direct associations among these constructs and the serial indirect associations implied by a prespecified sequential model in community-dwelling older adults. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 486 community-dwelling older adults recruited voluntarily from communities in Guangdong Province, China. Data were collected using Chinese-language, contextually adjusted self-report measures of mindfulness during exercise, sleep regularity, self-control, QL, PMH, and psychological resilience. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to evaluate the measurement model and estimate the direct and prespecified serial indirect associations. Statistical inference was based on 5,000 bootstrap resamples with bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals. ME was positively associated with SR (β = 0.463, p < 0.001), SR was positively associated with SC (β = 0.425, p < 0.001), and SC was positively associated with quality of life (β = 0.517, p < 0.001). Quality of life was positively associated with positive mental health (β = 0.554, p < 0.001) and PR (β = 0.591, p < 0.001). All five prespecified serial indirect associations were statistically significant because their bias-corrected 95% bootstrap confidence intervals excluded zero. The serial indirect association between mindfulness during exercise and positive mental health through sleep regularity, SC, and QL was β = 0.056 [95% CI (0.035, 0.088)], whereas the corresponding association with psychological resilience was β = 0.060 [95% CI (0.037, 0.093)]. The model explained 30.7% of the variance in positive mental health and 34.9% of the variance in psychological resilience. In this cross-sectional sample of community-dwelling older adults, the observed associations were consistent with the pre-specified sequence linking mindfulness during exercise with sleep regularity, self-control, QL, PMH, and psychological resilience. The significant serial indirect associations suggest that sleep regularity, self-control, and quality of life may be relevant correlates for understanding how mindfulness during exercise is statistically related to psychological functioning in later life. However, the simultaneous measurement of all constructs precludes conclusions regarding temporal ordering, causal mediation, or intervention effectiveness.

papers.title: Feasibility of a randomized placebo-controlled trial of short-course dexamethasone for pediatric obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society

papers.title: Acute-Onset Bipolar Psychosis in an Adolescent Without Prodromal Symptoms: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Early-onset bipolar disorder often begins in adolescence and carries greater severity, comorbidity, and long-term impairment. Diagnosis is complicated by symptom overlap with normative developmental behavior, nonspecific prodromes, and conditions that can cause high-risk or impulsive behaviors, such as attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This report examines the case of an adolescent with the acute onset of bipolar disorder and psychosis without an identifiable prodrome, after stimulant-treated ADHD, with emphasis on evaluation, treatment, and outcome. A 15-year-old male child with a history of anxiety and ADHD since childhood (well-controlled on dexmethylphenidate hydrochloride extended-release (XR)) presented after two weeks of abrupt restlessness, racing thoughts, decreased sleep, pacing, pressured speech, disorganization, echolalia, episodic disrobing/soiling, and paranoid delusions. He was admitted to the inpatient adolescent psychiatry unit for altered mental status with mania and psychosis. Risperidone was initiated and titrated to 1 mg in the morning and 2 mg nightly, with marked clinical improvement in manic and psychotic symptoms within one week, suggesting an original decrease in dosage may have precipitated psychosis. No organic etiology was revealed on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), lumbar puncture, labs, or encephalitis panels. Given the patient's clinical improvement, he was discharged on risperidone with first-break psychosis clinic follow-up. The patient tolerated long-term dexmethylphenidate hydrochloride use without prior manic symptoms, and discontinuation did not improve his presentation, making stimulant-induced bipolar disorder less likely. An extensive workup, including MRI, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and infectious/autoimmune panels, ruled out encephalitis. The case documents an abrupt-onset severe bipolar episode with psychosis in the absence of a prodrome; the temporal risperidone reduction may have precipitated decompensation. This case highlights the need for thorough multidisciplinary evaluation to exclude medical etiology, structured medication-transition protocols, and close outpatient follow-up.

papers.title: Adherence to 24-h movement guidelines and psychosocial and academic functioning in children and youth with learning disabilities.
papers.abstract: The 24-h movement behavior (24-HMB) guidelines for children and adolescents integrate sleep, physical activity, and screen time, and have been associated with multiple health benefits. Nonetheless, the relationships between 24-HMB guidelines and emotional well-being, social skills, and academic achievement in youth and teenagers with learning disabilities (LD) remain insufficiently explored. A cross-sectional study design was employed using data from the 2022-2023 National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH) including children and adolescents aged between 6 and 17 years with LD. To evaluate the relationships between adherence to the 24-HMB guidelines and anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms, social functioning, and academic performance, multivariable logistic regression models were applied. Subgroup analyses were also conducted to explore potential effect modifications. Among 6,305 children and adolescents with LD, 35.3% reported anxiety symptoms and 15.9% reported depressive symptoms, with social challenges being common in this population. Only 5.67% of children with learning disabilities satisfied all three recommendations in the 24-HMB guidelines, while 21.48% of children did not meet any of the recommendations. Meeting all three guidelines was associated with lower odds of anxiety (OR = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.48-0.78) and depression (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.31-0.50, p < 0.01). Adherence to a greater number of guidelines was progressively associated with better social functioning and superior academic performance. Suboptimal adherence to 24-HMB guidelines persists among children with LD. Higher compliance is linked to significantly better health and developmental outcomes.

papers.title: Perioperative symptom clusters and candidate priority symptoms in unruptured intracranial aneurysms: developing a symptom-guided case management protocol.
papers.abstract: To analyze the symptom distribution, cluster structure, and candidate priority symptoms across perioperative phases in patients with unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs), and to develop a symptom-guided case management protocol. This retrospective study included 362 UIA patients undergoing elective microsurgical clipping or endovascular treatment with complete perioperative symptom assessments. Symptoms were assessed within 24 hours pre-treatment (T0), 48 hours post-treatment (T1), and 24 hours pre-discharge (T2). Exploratory graph analysis (EGA) identified symptom clusters; regularized partial correlation networks assessed conditional associations, with one-step expected influence (EI) gauging relative centrality. The top three EI-ranked symptoms per phase were selected as candidate priority symptoms. Evidence synthesis informed candidate management items, refined via two modified Delphi rounds. At T0, dizziness, worry/fear, and anxiety were prevalent; at T1, headache, fatigue/low energy, and sleep difficulties were common; at T2, fatigue and dizziness persisted. EGA identified 4, 3, and 2 clusters at T0, T1, and T2, respectively. The highest EI-ranked symptoms were headache, dizziness, and worry/fear (T0); headache, memory/attention difficulties, and numbness/tingling (T1); and fatigue/low energy, dizziness, and decreased appetite (T2). EI rankings showed limited stability. Evidence integration and two Delphi rounds yielded a final protocol with 3 phases, 9 secondary indicators, and 36 tertiary management items. In this cohort, symptom distributions and separately estimated networks differed descriptively across phases, with phase-specific candidate priority symptoms. The symptom-guided protocol, based on symptom structure, evidence, and expert consensus, offers a prioritized framework for symptom assessment and management. Feasibility and clinical effectiveness require validation.

papers.title: Neurocognitive and Behavioural Correlates of REM-Predominant Obstructive Sleep Apnoea.
papers.abstract: Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA, REM-OSA) is a phenotype in which obstructive respiratory events occur mainly during REM sleep, and may be associated with distinct daytime consequences. This study investigated the neurocognitive, behavioural, subjective sleep and polysomnographic profile of REM-OSA. Patients were classified as having REM-OSA when the REM Apnoea-Hypopnea Index (AHI)/Non-REM (NREM) AHI ratio was ≥ 2 and were compared with patients whose respiratory events predominantly occurred during NREM sleep (NREM-OSA). Patients evaluated for suspected OSA underwent a neuropsychological battery, including the Mini-Mental State Examination, Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test, Digit Span Forward/Backward, Trail Making Test (TMT), Frontal Assessment Battery and Raven's Coloured Progressive Matrices, together with questionnaires evaluating sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index), daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale), impulsivity (Barratt Impulsiveness Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Of the 91 eligible patients, 17 had mild OSA and were included in sensitivity analyses, while the primary analysis included 74 patients with moderate-to-severe OSA. Thirteen (17.6%) met REM-OSA criteria, and 61 were classified as NREM-OSA. REM-OSA patients had lower overall AHI and oxygen desaturation index and, after False Discovery Rate correction, longer TMT-A, TMT-B and TMT B-A (all q = 0.003). After adjustment for depressive symptoms, REM-OSA independently predicted longer TMT-A (β = 0.298, p = 0.002), TMT-B (β = 0.235, p = 0.016), TMT B-A (β = 0.258, p = 0.018) and higher impulsivity (β = 0.237, p = 0.043), but not global PSQI scores (β = 0.210, p = 0.086). Sensitivity analyses confirmed poorer TMT-A performance in REM-OSA. These results highlight the neurocognitive relevance of REM phenotype despite lower overall respiratory severity.

papers.title: Evaluation of Retinal and Choroidal Structural Parameters in Night Shift Healthcare Workers: An Exploratory Analysis of Sleep Quality and Psychological Distress.
papers.abstract: Evaluation of the retinal and choroidal changes in healthcare staff working night shifts and exploratory analysis of the mediating roles of sleep disorders and psychological distress in this relationship. A total of 60 night shift healthcare workers and 52 daytime healthcare workers were included in this cross-sectional observational study. The subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness, and ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness and mean macular thickness across the nine subfields of the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) map were evaluated with the optical coherence tomography (OCT) device. Total choroidal area (TCA), luminal area (LA) and stromal area (SA) were measured with the binarization method. The choroidal vascular index (CVI) was calculated as the ratio of the LA to the TCA. All participants were administered the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), and Depression Anxiety Stress Scale (DASS-21). The ISI, PSQI, ESS, depression, anxiety, and stress scores of the night shift workers were significantly higher than the daytime workers. There was no significant difference between the groups for SFCT, CVI, macular thickness, or RNFL and GCC thickness. LA, SA, and TCA, which represents the sum of these two components, were significantly lower in night shift workers, while CVI did not differ significantly between groups. In the exploratory mediation analyses, PSQI, ISI and stress scores were found not to statistically explain the relationship between night shift work and decreased TCA, LA, and SA. Working night shifts leads to decreased choroidal area parameters in addition to increased incidence of sleep disorders and psychiatric symptoms. However, PSQI, ISI, and stress scores do not explain the between group difference in choroidal area. Further research is required to clarify the mechanisms underlying night shift-related ocular alterations.

papers.title: Exploratory observations of sleep during contest preparation in a natural bodybuilder: a case study.
papers.abstract: Natural bodybuilders undergo prolonged caloric restriction combined with high training volumes in the lead-up to competitions to achieve extremely low body fat levels while preserving lean mass. Although sleep plays a critical role in recovery and metabolic regulation, its response to contest preparation remains under-explored. This case study followed a 24-year-old male natural bodybuilder across four months: off-season (AS-1) and a three-month contest preparation phase (AS-2 to AS-5). Body composition, energy status and sleep were assessed. The athlete lost 5.7 kg (6.6%) of initial body mass, including approximately 4.0 kg of estimated fat mass, reaching an estimated body fat percentage of 5.4% two weeks before competition. Energy intake dropped from 4345 to 2080 kcal per day, shifting energy balance from a 1159 kcal surplus at AS-1 to a 1052 kcal deficit at AS-5. Estimated energy availability progressively declined, reaching 23.9 kcal·kg FFM-1·day-1 at AS-5, below a proposed male-specific threshold for potentially low energy availability. Sleep quality deteriorated markedly: sleep efficiency declined from 93% to 83%, wake after sleep onset nearly tripled, and rapid eye movement sleep dropped from 30.8% to 4.4% at AS-4 and 12% at AS-5. Hypnograms showed sleep fragmentation and impaired REM transition. These findings suggest that sleep characteristics may vary during periods of severe energy deficit in bodybuilding contest preparation.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

papers.title: Current and emerging pharmacotherapy in infantile epileptic spasms syndrome.
papers.abstract: Infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) is a devastating, age-dependent epileptic encephalopathy characterized by clusters of epileptic spasms, a markedly abnormal interictal electroencephalogram, and, in most cases, developmental stagnation or regression. Despite more than six decades of clinical experience, treatment relies predominantly on hormonal therapy and vigabatrin, and long-term outcomes remain unsatisfactory for many infants. This review synthesizes evidence, identified through a literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov, for adrenocorticotropic hormone, prednisolone/prednisone, vigabatrin, and combination hormonal-vigabatrin therapy, together with adjunctive agents such as pyridoxine and other antiseizure medications. It then examines emerging pharmacotherapy, spanning preclinical discoveries (insulin-like growth factor-1 analogues, corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor-1 antagonists, immune-modulatory agents) and precision, mechanism-based approaches for monogenic etiologies including tuberous sclerosis complex and CDKL5-, STXBP1-, KCNQ2-, and SCN2A-related disorders. First-line therapy should be individualized by etiology, treatment availability, and informed family preference, without avoidable treatment delay - vigabatrin for tuberous sclerosis complex, hormonal therapy alone or combined with vigabatrin otherwise. The ketogenic diet and epilepsy surgery warrant earlier consideration rather than reservation as last resorts. The convergence of genomic diagnostics and precision therapeutics promises a shift toward rational, etiology-targeted treatment, contingent on sustained translational research.

papers.title: Modulating expectations through observational learning in chronic neck pain: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Chronic neck pain (CNP) substantially affects quality of life. Although motor control exercises are commonly used in CNP management, psychological factors such as treatment expectations may influence outcomes. This randomized controlled trial (RCT) aims to evaluate whether brief peer interactions designed to manipulate expectations affect clinical outcomes in individuals with CNP undergoing motor control training. This three-arm parallel-group RCT will recruit 134 participants with CNP. Participants will be masked to the study hypothesis and experimental purpose, while outcome assessors and data analysts will remain blinded to group allocation. Participants will be randomized to: (a) motor control exercise plus positive peer interaction, (b) motor control exercise plus negative peer interaction, or (c) motor control exercise plus neutral peer interaction. All participants will complete an 18-session motor control exercise program over six weeks. Immediately before the first exercise session, participants will undergo a single brief scripted interaction with a trained simulated patient corresponding to their randomized condition. The co-primary outcomes are neck pain intensity and neck-related self-reported functional disability, assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and three-month follow-up. Secondary outcomes include cervical kinematics, superficial cervical muscle activity, psychological measures, and treatment expectations. Analyses will primarily use baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance under the intention-to-treat principle. This trial will clarify whether a brief observational-learning interaction can modify treatment expectations and whether clinical outcomes differ across positive, neutral, and negative peer-interaction conditions within an otherwise identical motor control exercise program. https://www.irct.ir/ identifier is IRCT20211121053136N1.

papers.title: Machine Learning and Mediation Analysis Reveal Multiple Pathways of Severe Pain in Middle-Aged and Elderly People: Predictive Models and Mechanism Evidence From the CHARLS Database.
papers.abstract: This study systematically identified key risk factors for severe pain among middle-aged and elderly individuals using the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) database, developed and validated a nomogram and online risk calculator, and explored mediating pathways. Data from CHARLS 2011 (baseline) and 2015 (follow-up) were analyzed. Feature selection and model construction employed univariate analysis, LASSO regression, multivariate logistic regression, and SHAP analysis. An interactive web-based calculator was developed. Model performance was assessed via receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis using internal and temporal validation. Mediation models examined pathways linking education and rheumatic/gastrointestinal diseases to pain via sleep duration and medication use. Among 10,521 participants, seven predictors were identified: gender, smoking, education, sleep duration, gastrointestinal disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and rheumatic/immunologic medication use. The model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUCs: 0.729-0.786) and calibration. An online calculator was deployed. Mediation analysis showed that education influenced pain partly through medication use (mediation proportion: 43.74%-47.74%), while arthritis and gastrointestinal disease partially acted via sleep duration (5.8%-9.38%). This study identified predictors-gender, smoking, education, sleep, gastrointestinal disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and rheumatic/immunologic medication use-and developed an internally validated nomogram and online tool for risk stratification of severe pain in middle-aged and older adults. However, prospective external validation is required before clinical application. Mediation analysis indicated that education affects pain via medication use, while arthritis and gastrointestinal conditions act via sleep disruption, offering mechanistic insights for potential intervention strategies.

papers.title: Chronotype in children and adolescents with elevated Sluggish Cognitive Tempo symptoms with and without ADHD: A cross-sectional case-control study.
papers.abstract: This study compared chronotype preferences and daytime sleepiness in children and adolescents with clinically elevated Sluggish Cognitive Tempo (SCT) symptoms with those of healthy controls and SCT cases with comorbid Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). A total of 180 participants aged 6-18 years (High-SCT = 60, SCT+ADHD = 60, Control = 60) were assessed with the Barkley SCT Scale, DuPaul ADHD Rating Scale, Child and Adolescent Behavior Inventory, Children's Chronotype Questionnaire (CCTQ), Pediatric Daytime Sleepiness Scale (PDSS), and Pubertal Development Scale; psychiatric diagnoses were evaluated using the K-SADS-PL-T. After adjustment for age, sex, and pubertal development, both SCT groups showed significantly greater eveningness than controls (F(2,173) = 39.728, p < 0.001, partial η2 = .315), with the SCT+ADHD group scoring highest, followed by the High-SCT group and controls (all pairwise p ≤ 0.004). Eveningness chronotype was most prevalent in the SCT+ADHD group (75.0%), while morningness was highest in controls (16.7%). Daytime sleepiness was also significantly higher in both SCT groups than in controls (F(2,173) = 45.908, p < 0.001, partial η2 = .347) and correlated positively with eveningness (r = .310, p < 0.001). In the full sample, SCT severity was incrementally associated with chronotype after adjustment for ADHD severity (β = .315, p < 0.001), and this association was robust to the exclusion of children below the validated CCTQ age range (β = .342, p < 0.001). However, within the SCT-positive subsample, this association was not replicated (β = .077, p = 0.396), suggesting that the full-sample finding largely reflects threshold-based group differences. The high eveningness rate in the SCT+ADHD group suggests that sleep regulation and chronotype-based approaches warrant consideration in this subgroup, although intervention effects remain to be tested. Longitudinal studies including ADHD-only groups and objective circadian measures are needed.

papers.title: Co-Administration of Fluvoxamine and Morphine: Effects on Nociception and Central Nervous System Function in Healthy Volunteers.
papers.abstract: Background: Combining opioids with non-opioid analgesics is a potential strategy to improve pain management and reduce opioid requirements, but few such combinations have been systematically characterized in humans. Preclinical studies have shown that the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor fluvoxamine can potentiate morphine-induced antinociception. We explored the interactive effects of fluvoxamine and morphine on a battery of evoked pain tests, central nervous system (CNS) function (including electroencephalography (EEG)), and adverse effects. Methods: In a randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, four-way crossover study, 24 healthy volunteers received placebo, morphine (3 mg intravenous (IV) at 2 h plus 7 mg IV at 5 h), fluvoxamine (100 mg oral at 0 h), or the combination. Outcomes included responses to evoked pain tests, CNS function tests, and resting-state EEG. Results: The combination produced greater antinociceptive effects than placebo on cold pressor, electrical-burst, and pressure pain tolerance, but did not significantly enhance pain detection or tolerance thresholds compared with morphine alone. In contrast, the combination significantly reduced capsaicin-induced secondary mechanical allodynia compared with placebo and fluvoxamine monotherapy. These findings were accompanied by distinct reductions in frontal-midline beta- and delta-power on EEG that were not observed with either monotherapy. No significant effects on conditioned pain modulation (CPM) were observed, and additional CNS effects were generally modest. Conclusions: In conclusion, combination therapy with morphine and fluvoxamine was associated with reduced experimentally induced secondary mechanical allodynia and distinct EEG alterations, without additional effects on pain detection or tolerance thresholds compared with morphine alone.

papers.title: Plant-Derived Compounds in Monogenic Epilepsies: Mechanistic Evidence, Genotype-Relevant Models, and Translational Considerations.
papers.abstract: Monogenic epilepsies and developmental and epileptic encephalopathies are biologically heterogeneous, and evidence for plant-derived interventions ranges from ethnopharmacology to randomized clinical trials. This review critically maps that evidence using a four-level genotype-relevance framework while separating antiseizure, neuroprotective, mechanistic, and clinical endpoints. Highly purified cannabidiol (CBD) has the strongest evidence chain: antiseizure activity in Scn1a-based Dravet models is complemented by randomized clinical efficacy at the syndrome level. However, current trial evidence does not establish an SCN1A-genotype-specific treatment response. β-Caryophyllene has direct preclinical evidence in a genetically relevant Dravet model. Luteolin has direct CDKL5-model evidence for reducing microglial overactivation and improving neuronal and neurodevelopmental outcomes, but seizure-frequency or video-EEG efficacy in CDKL5 deficiency disorder has not been demonstrated. Curcumin, resveratrol, epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG), quercetin, and sulforaphane are supported mainly by non-genetic seizure models and therefore remain mechanistically plausible candidates rather than validated treatments for monogenic epilepsy. Medicinal plants, crude extracts, standardized preparations, and isolated compounds are considered separately. Translational prioritization should require a reproducible genotype-associated secondary phenotype, clinically meaningful functional outcomes, achievable systemic and brain exposure, acceptable safety and drug-interaction profiles, and reproducible formulation. Plant-derived compounds should therefore be viewed as potential adjuncts to established antiseizure, syndrome-specific, and gene-directed therapies rather than substitutes.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm-Related Modulation of Acetaminophen Oxidation Exposure at Term: A PBPK Simulation Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Acetaminophen (APAP) is widely used in pregnancy, and its oxidative metabolite N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine (NAPQI) may contribute to hepatotoxicity. Whether dosing time affects APAP oxidative metabolism during pregnancy remains undetermined. Methods: In a pregnancy physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of APAP, circadian rhythms in CYP2E1, hepatic blood flow (HBF), and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) were described by cosine functions. Maternal APAP and NAPQI-related exposure was simulated after a single 1000 mg oral dose at four dosing times at 40 weeks of gestation. Counterfactual analyses in which each rhythm was switched off quantified its contribution to the difference in the 20:00/08:00 exposure ratio relative to the no-rhythm reference. Rhythm amplitude, peak phase, and interindividual variability were also examined. Results: APAP exposure varied little with dosing time, with 20:00/08:00 ratios of 0.92 for AUC0-48h and 0.96 for Cmax. NAPQI-related exposure was highest at 20:00 and lowest at 08:00, with AUC0-48h and Cmax ratios of 2.42 and 3.52; virtual population simulations showed the same direction (median ratios, 2.52 and 3.51). Rhythm-removal comparisons showed that CYP2E1 had the largest conditional contribution (91.00% for AUC0-48h and 89.69% for Cmax, respectively), while HBF contributions were smaller and GFR contributed less than 1%. Increasing CYP2E1 amplitude widened the exposure change, whereas shifting its peak phase to 08:00 or 12:00 reversed the effect direction. Conclusions: These hypothesis-generating computational predictions identify biological timing as a determinant of modeled oxidative exposure at term. Clinical evaluation is needed before they can inform dosing decisions.

papers.title: Personalized Nutrition for Cardiometabolic Prevention: Integrating Multi-Omics, Digital Health, Functional Foods, and the Gut Microbiome.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Tailoring dietary recommendations to an individual's biological, metabolic, behavioral, and lifestyle factors may be a promising approach for supporting the prevention and management of chronic metabolic disorders. Methods: This narrative review summarizes the potential significance of personalized nutrition, focusing on digital technologies, functional foods, and the gut microbiota, by reviewing relevant data from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from 2019 to 2026. The evidence was synthesized narratively to critically evaluate the interactions among these components and their potential translation into clinically relevant cardiometabolic outcomes. Results: Genetics, epigenetics, metabolic phenotype, gut microbial profile, physical activity, sleep, stress, and other behavioral factors contribute to inter-individual variability in nutritional response. Technologies ranging from mobile health apps to AI and machine learning, wearable devices, continuous glucose monitoring, diet-tracking apps, and tele-nutrition allow real-time monitoring and adjustment of nutrition guidance. Probiotic, prebiotic, synbiotic, dietary fiber, polyphenol, omega-3 fatty acid, and phytosterol interventions could help support metabolic regulation, inflammation control, gut health, and cardiovascular function. Moreover, short-chain fatty acid production, immune regulation, gut-liver-brain signaling, and nutrient metabolism highlight the role of the gut microbiota in contributing to personalized responses. Conclusions: Emerging evidence suggests potential benefits of personalized nutrition approaches; however, their long-term clinical effectiveness remains insufficiently validated. Moreover, several challenges remain, such as inconsistent validation, heterogeneous study designs, variable evidence regarding functional foods, data privacy concerns, high costs, limited accessibility, digital literacy, and long-term adherence, which hinder clinical translation. Furthermore, the potential attributes of personalized nutrition lie in its coordinated integration; therefore, biological profiling informs targeted dietary interventions and digital monitoring supports continuous evaluation and adaptation.

papers.title: Clocking Impulses: Mealtime Intervention Shifts Impulsivity, Associated with Glucose Metabolism and Plasma Tyrosine.
papers.abstract: Impulsive behaviour has a daily rhythm and is greater in the evening. This can have negative health consequences, such as disinhibited food intake in the evening, associated with metabolic disease and obesity. Therefore, interventions targeting evening impulsivity are key to improving health. Through the role of mealtime as a circadian cue, we conducted a secondary analysis of a Time-Restricted Eating (TRE) trial, comparing early versus late TRE to shift mealtime and subsequently internal daytime. We examined whether this shift affects impulsivity and, if so, whether this is related to tyrosine, dopamine's precursor, and glucose metabolism. Twenty-eight female participants (Age = 56.9 ± 9.75 years, BMI = 30.3 ± 2.84 kg/m2 [mean ± SD], 13/28 with impaired glucose metabolism (IFG/IGT)) completed this preregistered, randomised crossover study (Clinical Trials identifier: NCT04351672, Open Science Framework osf.io/fuqwz). We applied two TRE interventions for two weeks each, early (mealtime 08:00-16:00) and late (13:00-21:00), to induce an internal daytime shift. After each intervention, fasted plasma tyrosine was assessed, followed by an impulsive decision-making task. Firstly, individuals made more impulsive decisions during the internal evening (after eTRE) compared to the morning (after lTRE), determined by mealtime intervention (χ2 = 12.31, df = 1, p < 0.001, OR = 1.27, 95% CI [1.11, 1.46]). Furthermore, tyrosine was positively associated with impulsive decisions, particularly for those with IFG/IGT compared to normal glucose metabolism (NGT) (χ2 = 10.00, df = 1, p < 0.01, OR = 0.87, 95% CI [0.75, 1.00]). Finally, in individuals with IFG/IGT, tyrosine was positively associated with impulsive decisions across both internal morning and evening, with a stronger effect in the evening (χ2 = 14.15, df = 1, p < 0.01, OR = 1.51, 95% CI [1.22, 1.88]). This study presents mealtime shift as an alternative, behavioural intervention for curbing evening impulsivity. Furthermore, we highlight tyrosine and glucose metabolism as biologically relevant associations in our female population with overweight/obesity. Future studies should determine whether this intervention influences other impulsive behaviours, such as impulsive food intake, particularly in the context of metabolic disease such as type 2 diabetes. NCT04351672, date: 17 April 2020.

papers.title: Food Insecurity and Obstructive Sleep Apnea Risk Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults in South Korea: A Cross-Sectional Study Using the STOP-BANG Questionnaire.
papers.abstract: Background: Food insecurity is a major global public health concern. A direct association between food insecurity and OSA may be expected, as food insecurity is accompanied by sleep disturbances, socioeconomic stress, and inflammation, all of which are associated with OSA. However, its association with OSA remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between food insecurity and OSA risk among middle-aged and older adults. Methods: A nationwide sample of 9555 individuals aged ≥ 40 years was analyzed. Food insecurity was classified as food secure, marginally food secure, and food insecure using the 18-item Household Food Security Survey Module. A modified STOP-BANG questionnaire was used to identify individuals at high risk for OSA. Logistic regression models were fitted to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: The weighted proportions of food-secure, marginally food-secure, and food-insecure individuals were 86.36%, 9.29%, and 4.35%, respectively. The weighted prevalence rates of high OSA risk by screening were 17.52% in the overall sample and 17.11%, 19.53%, and 21.44% among participants with food security, marginal food security, and food insecurity, respectively. In the overall sample, the ORs (95% CIs) for high OSA risk by screening were 1.24 (0.98-1.57) among participants with marginal food security and 1.36 1.35 (1.01-1.81) among those with food insecurity, compared with food-secure participants. Conclusions: Food insecurity was associated with a high risk of OSA by screening. However, future longitudinal studies using polysomnography are needed to validate our study findings.

papers.title: Meal Timing, Preceding Intake, and Diurnal Glucose in Late Pregnancy: A Chrononutrition Study Using Blinded Continuous Glucose Monitoring.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chrononutrition, the study of how meal timing affects metabolism, has rarely been applied to pregnancy. We examined how meal time of day, preceding intake, and the last intake of the day relate to postprandial and nocturnal glucose in late pregnancy. Methods: In a prospective cohort of 190 pregnant women in Japan without gestational diabetes (31.7 ± 2.2 weeks), glucose was recorded with blinded continuous glucose monitoring for a median of 11.5 valid days, and all intake was timed by linking a diet app with a paper diary. Outcomes were the incremental area under the curve 0-120 min after meals (iAUC) and mean glucose at 00:00-06:00, analyzed with within-person fixed-effects models. Results: Glucose was lowest at 05:30 (median 72.9 mg/dL) and highest after lunch (107.7 mg/dL). After adjustment for content and starting glucose (2061 meals), the iAUC was larger after lunch (+12.0 mg/dL × h; 95% CI 7.2 to 16.9) and dinner (+9.3; 4.4 to 14.3) than after breakfast; without adjustment for starting glucose, only the lunch-breakfast difference remained clear. Each 20 g of snack carbohydrate in the preceding 4 h was associated with a smaller iAUC (-4.1; -6.4 to -1.9), although total postprandial glucose was not lower, whereas each additional hour since the last intake was associated with a larger iAUC (+1.8; 1.1 to 2.6). Across 1310 nights, each 1 h later last intake was associated with 1.2 mg/dL (0.7 to 1.7) higher nocturnal glucose, whereas whole-day glucose changed little. Conclusions: In late pregnancy, when and in what sequence women ate was associated with their postprandial and nocturnal glucose. These exploratory, modest associations support testing meal timing as a target for dietary advice in pregnancy.

papers.title: Sweet Rewards: Preferred Candy and Money Elicit Equivalent Reward Positivity Responses.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Food is a salient reward that can influence dietary behavior, but it is unclear whether neural responses to food rewards differ meaningfully from responses to other salient rewards, such as money. The current study examined whether reward responses, as measured by the reward positivity (RewP) event-related potential, differed between individually preferred food and monetary rewards. Methods: Two one-sided tests (TOST) of equivalence along with null hypothesis significance testing (NHST) were used to determine whether observed differences were practically equivalent or significantly different. Participants (N = 158) completed food, monetary, and performance-feedback versions of a computerized doors task while electroencephalography data were recorded. Participants earned an individually preferred candy during the food task and money during the monetary task, whereas the performance-feedback task provided no tangible reward. Based on prior research, TOST equivalence bounds were set to dz = 0.25. Results: Manipulation checks confirmed significant RewP effects across all three tasks. Paired-samples t-tests showed RewP amplitude did not significantly differ between food and monetary rewards, and equivalence testing demonstrated that responses were practically equivalent within the prespecified bounds. Monetary rewards elicited significantly larger RewP amplitudes than positive performance feedback, whereas the comparison between food reward and positive performance feedback was inconclusive, with insufficient evidence to establish either a difference or practical equivalence. Conclusions: Findings suggest an individually preferred food can elicit reward-related neural activity comparable to a monetary reward. Results provide preliminary support that food and monetary reward salience may warrant consideration when designing monetary-based interventions to improve dietary behavior. Future work relating neural reward responses to dietary intake will help determine the clinical significance of neural indices of food reward.

papers.title: Nutritional Vulnerability and Frailty Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults in Abha, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examined nutritional vulnerability and frailty among older adults attending primary health care centers (PHCCs) in Abha, Saudi Arabia. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 410 adults aged ≥60 years were recruited by non-probability convenience sampling at five PHCCs randomly selected from ten centers in Abha. Nutritional status was assessed using the Mini Nutritional Assessment Short-Form (MNA-SF), and frailty using the FRAIL scale. Results: Overall, 50.7% were at risk of malnutrition, 33.7% had MNA-SF-defined malnutrition, and 15.6% had normal nutritional status; 44.6% were frail, 45.6% prefrail, and 9.8% robust. Higher MNA-SF scores were weakly associated with lower FRAIL scores (Pearson r = -0.254; Spearman ρ = -0.215; both p < 0.001). Unadjusted linear regression explained only 6.5% of FRAIL-score variation. In an exploratory ordinal model adjusted for age, gender, education, income sufficiency, physical activity, sleep duration, calf circumference, and number of medications taken daily, each one-point increase in MNA-SF score was associated with lower odds of a higher frailty category (aOR = 0.86, 95% CI 0.80-0.92, p < 0.001). Conclusions: Higher MNA-SF scores were associated with lower odds of greater frailty severity after adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, and clinical factors. Older age and polypharmacy were also associated with greater severity of frailty. Integrated nutrition and frailty screening, with attention to calf circumference and medication burden, may identify vulnerable older adults in primary care. However, their association was weak, and cross-sectional findings establish neither causation nor clinical benefit.
