Adjusted associations with foster care discharge (aOR 0.97, 95% CI 0.49-1.93) and parental involvement (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 0.66-2.32) were not statistically significant. ESC implementation was associated with shorter hospitalization and less pharmacological treatment after adjustment for measured differences between epochs. Unadjusted differences in foster care discharge and parental involvement did not persist after adjustment. The observational, sequential-epoch design precludes causal attribution.

papers.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing in Children with Down Syndrome in Saudi Arabia: Current Evidence and a Proposed Care Pathway.
papers.abstract: Children with Down syndrome are at increased risk of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), which cannot be reliably excluded by symptoms or examination. Saudi evidence remains limited. This review synthesizes international and Saudi evidence and proposes a pediatric care pathway incorporating the transition to adult services. We conducted a structured narrative review of the English-language literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, selected journal websites, and reference lists. The review focused on publications from January 2018 to 17 September 2026, retaining relevant earlier studies. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively without a new meta-analysis or formal risk of bias assessment. Published international estimates indicate that OSA affects approximately 50-79% of children with Down syndrome. American Academy of Pediatrics guidance recommends polysomnography (PSG) at ages 3-4 years regardless of symptoms, with earlier assessment when indicated. Nonrandomized infant intervention studies suggest potential benefits but do not establish an optimal universal screening schedule. Saudi evidence includes a small earlier PSG referral cohort and more recent caregiver surveys; no nationally representative PSG-confirmed prevalence study was identified. Arabic questionnaire validation in a mixed pediatric referral cohort does not establish Down syndrome-specific diagnostic accuracy. Published treatment evidence indicates that adenotonsillectomy often improves OSA, although residual disease commonly requires objective reassessment and individualized management. The evidence supports age-based PSG, earlier assessment when indicated, postoperative reassessment, and individualized multidisciplinary care. Building on this evidence, we propose a Saudi pathway linking referral tracking, family-centered positive airway pressure support, and coordinated transition. Regional networks and registry development remain unevaluated implementation proposals requiring stakeholder consultation, resource assessment, and pilot testing; they do not constitute an endorsed national guideline.

papers.title: Social Patterning of 24-Hour Movement Behaviors Among Spanish Adolescents: Cross-Sectional Accelerometry Evidence from the EHDLA Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The 24 h movement behavior (24HMB) framework integrates moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), recreational screen time, and sleep. Sociodemographic correlates of simultaneous guideline adherence among European adolescents remain poorly understood. We aimed to estimate 24HMB compliance with each guideline and their combination, identify sociodemographic correlates, and compare accelerometry- and questionnaire-based sleep models. Methods: Cross-sectional data from 444 Spanish adolescents aged 12-17 years in the Eating Healthy and Daily Life Activities (EHDLA) study, conducted in a single semi-rural municipality in the Region of Murcia, were analyzed. MVPA and sleep were measured by ActiGraph wGT3X-BT accelerometry (valid days ranged from 1 to 6); sleep and screen time were also self-reported. Firth's penalized logistic regression was applied uniformly across binary outcomes to provide a consistent estimation framework, with primary inference based on uncorrected p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction reported for transparency. Results: In the subsample with complete screen-time data (n = 403; 51.6% female; median age 14 years), compliance was 26.1% (MVPA), 20.3% (screen time), and 36.7%/40.2% (accelerometry-derived sleep period time/questionnaire self-reported time in bed); only 3.5-4.0% met all three guidelines simultaneously. Female sex was associated with lower MVPA (odds ratio, OR = 0.51) and screen time (OR = 0.44) compliance (both FDR-corroborated). Caucasian ethnicity was unexpectedly associated with lower MVPA compliance (OR = 0.29) in the primary complete-case analysis. Older age was associated with lower screen-time compliance (OR = 0.45; both FDR-corroborated). No predictor was significant for accelerometry-derived sleep period time compliance, and questionnaire self-reported time in bed associations did not survive FDR correction. Conclusions: Concurrent adherence to 24HMB guidelines is critically low and socially patterned. Female sex was an FDR-corroborated correlate of lower MVPA and screen-time compliance. The Caucasian ethnicity association with MVPA was specific to the primary complete-case analysis and attenuated under stricter wear-time criteria. Sleep compliance estimates and their sociodemographic correlates differed by assessment method. Future 24HMB surveillance should use validated, standardized, and clearly reported protocols, and cross-study comparisons should account for methodological differences in sleep assessment.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG Differences Across Two Sedation Conditions in a Child with Epilepsy: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Sedation is frequently required to obtain electroencephalography (EEG) recordings in children with neurodevelopmental disorders and structural etiologies of epilepsy. However, the extent to which different sedative agents influence quantitative interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) burden remains insufficiently characterized. A child with congenital cytomegalovirus-associated structural brain injury underwent EEG recordings under two sedation conditions: continuous low-dose propofol infusion and oral chloral hydrate. Quantitative analyses were performed using a duration-matched, within-subject design. Artifact-minimized EEG segments of equal duration (15.52 min) were analyzed. IED burden was quantified using spike frequency (spikes/min) and spike index (percentage of 10 s epochs containing ≥1 spike). Spectral power distribution and spectral edge frequency (SEF95) were also evaluated. The chloral hydrate recording showed a higher observed spike frequency than the propofol recording (14.11 vs. 4.12 spikes/min; descriptive rate ratio, 3.42) and a higher 10-s spike index (84.95% vs. 27.96%). Spectral analysis demonstrated lower SEF95 and greater delta predominance in the propofol recording, whereas the chloral hydrate recording showed relatively greater theta-alpha activity. The two recordings showed marked differences in apparent IED burden and background spectral characteristics. However, because they were obtained approximately one year apart and under different clinical circumstances, including intercurrent illness during the chloral hydrate recording, these differences cannot be attributed specifically to the sedative agents. This case illustrates the importance of considering sedation, clinical context, and vigilance state when longitudinally interpreting quantitative pediatric EEG findings.

papers.title: Autosomal Copy Number Variants in Neurodevelopmental Disorders Phenotypes: A 5-Year Retrospective Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Microdeletion/microduplication syndromes are rare chromosomal abnormalities causing diverse clinical features due to gene dosage imbalances caused by submicroscopic deletions/duplications (Copy Number Variations-CNVs) of contiguous genes in specific chromosomal regions. CNVs causing microdeletion/microduplication syndromes encoded in reference databases (Orphanet, OMIM) have a significant clinical impact in neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Methods: A retrospective study analyzed the molecular and clinical data of 446 pediatric patients referred for suspected NDDs to the Outpatient Clinic of the Child Neuropsychiatry Unit at University Hospital of Catania Italy, between 2020 and 2024. Final clinical diagnoses reflect comprehensive post-intake evaluations. Results: Over 446 patients, 156 (35%) had CNVs in autosomal chromosomes. Thirty-nine (8.7%), 28 males (71.8%) and 11 females (28.2%), with a mean age of 11.8 years (SD: 4.6), were diagnosed with microdeletion/microduplication syndromes. Chromosome 16 (30.8%, 12/39), chromosome 22 (12.8%, 5/39), chromosome 15 (7.7%, 3/39) and chromosome 7 (7.7%, 3/39) were more frequently implicated. De novo rearrangements accounted for 23.1% of cases (9/39), while 69.2% (27/39; 11 maternal, 16 paternal) were inherited from unaffected or pauci-symptomatic parents. Direct mapping to OMIM or Orphanet database entries was present in 22 patients (56.4%). The neurobehavioral phenotype was dominated by intellectual disability (ID)/developmental delay (DD) (26 patients, 66.7%), dysmorphic features (18 patients, 46.2%) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) (15 patients, 38.5%), followed by developmental coordination disorder (10 patients, 25.6%), Specific Language Disorder/Communication Disorder (SLD) (10 patients, 25.6%), Disruptive behavioral disorders (7 patients, 17.9%), ADHD (4 patients, 10.3%), microcephaly (3 patients, 7.7%), structural brain MRI abnormalities (3 patients, 7.7%), epilepsy (3 patients, 7.7%) EEG abnormalities (2 patients, 5.1%) and selective mutism (2 patients, 5.1%). The cumulative clinical burden ranged from 1 to 6 manifestations per patient (median: 2, IQR: 2-3), with 82.1% of patients presenting with 2-3 co-occurring features. Conclusions: The identification of CNVs syndromes and associated clinical phenotypes is of significant support in the diagnostic process and possible therapeutic management. ID and ASD represent the core diagnostic drivers, while the high rate of inherited CNVs and multi-domain comorbidity underscore the impact of variable expressivity and cumulative clinical burden in neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: Fenfluramine in SCN1A-Related Genetic Epilepsy with Febrile Seizures Plus (GEFS+): Toward a Precision Therapeutic Approach.
papers.abstract: SCN1A-related genetic epilepsy with febrile seizures plus (GEFS+) is characterized by marked intrafamilial phenotypic variability, ranging from asymptomatic variant carriers to severe, drug-resistant epilepsy. We present a two-generation family in which two clinically affected sisters inherited a causative heterozygous SCN1A missense variant (c.3824G>A) from the mother, who likely carries the variant in a mosaic state. The proband, a 23-year-old woman, presented with a long-standing drug-resistant febrile and afebrile epilepsy with onset in early infancy, complicated by mild intellectual disability, impulse control disorder, and behavioral comorbidities, leading to a delayed genetic diagnosis in adulthood. Following insufficient control by multiple antiseizure medications, fenfluramine was introduced at age 21, resulting in complete seizure freedom sustained over two years, alongside measurable neuropsychological improvements in cognition, adaptive functioning, socialization and quality of life. This case highlights the importance of systematic family history and targeted genetic workup in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, adds preliminary evidence for fenfluramine beyond Dravet and Lennox-Gastaut syndromes, and illustrates the potential of precise genetic diagnosis to guide treatment in SCN1A-related GEFS+.
keywords: genetic epilepsy with febrile seizures plus

papers.title: A Previously Unreported POU3F3 p.(Lys409Ter) Variant in Snijders Blok-Fisher Syndrome: Mechanistic Context of Expressed Truncating Alleles.
papers.abstract: Background: Snijders Blok-Fisher syndrome (SNIBFIS; OMIM #618604) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder associated with heterozygous POU3F3 variants and characterized by developmental delay, prominent speech and language impairment, behavioral abnormalities, and dysmorphic features. Case Presentation: We report a Chinese boy evaluated at 7 years and 9 months for longstanding developmental and language delay. He walked independently at 18 months, began using meaningful single words at approximately 24 months, and remained unable to produce complete sentences at 7 years of age. Wechsler intelligence testing yielded a full-scale IQ of 57. Clinical evaluation documented attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder, with a Childhood Autism Rating Scale score of 38. Additional findings included sleep-onset difficulty, low-set ears, an open-mouth appearance, a single transverse palmar crease, and left hyperopia. He had no history of seizures, and electroencephalography was normal. Trio whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous POU3F3 nonsense variant, NM_006236.3:c.1225A>T [p.(Lys409Ter)], absent from both parental blood samples and reported as de novo by the diagnostic laboratory. The variant was not identified in the published literature or publicly accessible variant resources searched through 8 September 2026. Conclusions: This case adds to the reported POU3F3 variant spectrum and illustrates the importance of considering the unusual behavior of truncating alleles in this intronless gene.

papers.title: A Digitally Supported Hybrid Exercise and Health Education Program for Textile Workers with Musculoskeletal Disorders: A Single-Arm Pre-Post Intervention Study.
papers.abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) are prevalent in physically demanding occupations and can impair health, functional capacity and work productivity. Textile workers face occupational risk factors, yet workplace-based interventions remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate changes in health and work-related outcomes following a hybrid intervention among textile workers with WMSDs. A quasi-experimental single-arm pre-post study with a 1-month follow-up was conducted among textile workers in Zaragoza, Spain. The 9-week intervention combined eight onsite health education workshops with an individualized, digitally supported home-based exercise program delivered via RehBody. Participants completed two weekly exercise sessions, remotely monitored by health professionals. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, postintervention, and at 1-month follow-up. Musculoskeletal pain intensity was the primary outcome; secondary outcomes included musculoskeletal symptoms, physical function, physical activity, work ability, sleep quality, psychological distress, health-related quality of life, and work productivity. Changes over time were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA or Friedman tests, as appropriate. Thirty-one participants completed all assessments (retention rate 79.5%). Musculoskeletal pain decreased significantly after the intervention and remained lower at follow-up (p < 0.01; Kendall W = 0.314). Significant improvements were observed in lower-limb functional capacity (p < 0.001; η2p = 0.773), work ability (p = 0.002; W = 0.195), and sleep quality (p = 0.004; η2p = 0.177). Seven-day shoulder symptoms and presenteeism also improved significantly (p = 0.013 and p = 0.047, respectively). Workshop attendance was 88.7%, while 69.6% of prescribed digital exercise sessions were completed. The hybrid workplace intervention was associated with improvements in musculoskeletal pain, physical function, work ability, and sleep quality. However, the uncontrolled design limits causal inferences. Larger controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings and assess their long-term sustainability.

papers.title: Profiles and Factors Associated with Intrinsic Capacity Impairment in Community-Dwelling Older Adults with Cardiometabolic Diseases: A Latent Class Analysis.
papers.abstract: Background: Cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs) are highly prevalent and contribute to functional decline. Intrinsic capacity (IC) is central to healthy ageing, yet evidence on IC impairment among older adults with CMDs in under-resourced regions remains limited. This study aimed to identify distinct IC impairment profiles and associated factors among community-dwelling older adults with CMDs in the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps (XPCC), China. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 813 older adults (≥60 years) with CMDs from three urban and two rural communities within the XPCC. IC was assessed across six domains: cognition, locomotion, vitality, psychology, vision, and hearing. Latent class analysis (LCA) identified distinct IC impairment profiles, and multinomial logistic regression examined factors associated with class membership. Results: Mean age was 79.11 years (SD = 6.2), and 66.5% were female. IC impairment was nearly universal (99.2%). Psychological impairment was more prevalent among those with cardiometabolic multimorbidity (40.94% vs. 28.09%, p = 0.002). LCA identified three subgroups: "Cognition impairment" (25.34%), "Vitality-Cognition-Locomotion" (24.97%), and "Multidomain IC impairment" (49.69%). Older age, single marital status, lower education, poor self-rated health, insufficient physical activity, and poor sleep quality were significantly associated with more severe IC impairment. Conclusions: IC impairment is highly prevalent and heterogeneous among community-dwelling older adults with CMDs. These findings support a shift from disease-centred to function-centred care, with risk-stratified, personalised interventions to promote healthy ageing.

papers.title: Sitting Time in Late Pregnancy and Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes in Women with and Without Chronic Diseases: A Matched Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sedentary behavior increases in late pregnancy, but its relationship with perinatal outcomes, particularly in women with chronic diseases, is unclear. This study examined the associations of daily sitting time (ST) with sleep quality, labor and neonatal outcomes in healthy pregnant (HP) women and pregnant women with chronic diseases (CDP). Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 102 women who delivered vaginally at 36-42 weeks of gestation were included: 51 CDP and 51 HP individually matched for ST. ST was assessed with the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form and analyzed continuously and dichotomized at the median (300 min/day). Sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, PSQI), labor and neonatal outcomes were obtained from questionnaires and medical records; all outcomes were considered exploratory. Data were analyzed with matched-pairs ANCOVA adjusted for age, gestational weight change and gravidity. Results: Neonates of mothers with long ST had lower hemoglobin than those of mothers with short ST (adjusted difference -0.93 g/dL, 95% CI -1.54 to -0.32; p = 0.003, ηp2 = 0.175; not significant after Holm-Bonferroni correction, p = 0.051), with no ST × health status interaction; ST correlated inversely with neonatal hemoglobin in both HP (r = -0.45) and CDP (r = -0.32). Longer ST predicted greater maternal daytime dysfunction (β = 0.38, p = 0.006), although the dichotomized ST groups did not differ. ST was not associated with labor duration, induction, episiotomy, perineal laceration or neonatal anthropometry. Independently of ST, CDP had poorer global PSQI scores, longer sleep latency, greater daytime dysfunction and a longer active phase of labor, and their neonates had higher birth weight and 1-min Apgar scores; only the differences in daytime dysfunction and Apgar score remained significant after correction. Conclusions: Longer sitting in late pregnancy was associated with lower neonatal hemoglobin and greater maternal daytime dysfunction. These exploratory, hypothesis-generating associations do not establish causality and require confirmation in prospective studies using device-based measures of sedentary behavior and data on key determinants of neonatal hemoglobin.

papers.title: Positive Screening for Sleep-Related Breathing Disorders Among Children in Jordan: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Parents.
papers.abstract: Background: Sleep-related breathing disorders (SRBDs) in children range from primary snoring to obstructive sleep apnea and can affect health, behavior and learning. This study aimed to estimate the proportion of children in Jordan who screen positive for SRBD and to identify associated factors. Methods: This was a cross-sectional survey study that was conducted in Jordan between 27 November and 15 December 2025. Parents completed the Arabic 22-item Pediatric Sleep Questionnaire (PSQ) scale online (using Google Forms). The primary analysis was restricted to parents who reported a single child age group (one year or older) and a single mode of delivery, so that answers most likely referred to one child. A positive screen was defined as eight or more "yes" responses. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify associated factors. Results: Of 1112 respondents, 476 met the criteria and were included in the primary analysis. Among them, parent reports for 108 children (22.7%; 95% confidence interval (CI): 19.2-26.7%) screened positive for SRBD. Habitual snoring was reported for 13.7% of children and witnessed breathing pauses for 10.9%. In the multivariable regression model, a positive screen was associated with a family history of snoring or sleep apnea (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 3.72, 95% CI: 2.07-6.71), sleeping in a noisy or shared room (aOR = 2.45, 95% CI: 1.38-4.33), and having a divorced (aOR = 2.97, 95% CI: 1.17-7.56) or widowed parent (aOR = 3.83, 95% CI: 1.04-14.16). Conclusions: About one in five parent reports in this online convenience sample met the PSQ screening threshold for SRBD symptoms. A positive screen indicates a need for further evaluation and does not confirm a sleep disorder. Asking about family history of snoring and the sleep environment may help primary care and school health staff identify children who need referral for sleep assessment.

papers.title: Protocol for a Double-Blind Randomized Pilot Trial on the Augmentative Effect of Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation Combined with Maintenance Medication in Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.abstract: Background: Adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with substantial functional impairment and represents a major public health concern. Although pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy are established treatments, a considerable proportion of adolescents experience inadequate treatment response, adverse effects, or poor adherence. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is an emerging non-invasive neuromodulation approach with potential therapeutic benefits; however, its feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical effects in adolescents with MDD remain insufficiently investigated. This study will evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical outcomes of adjunctive tACS treatment in adolescents with MDD. Methods: This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled pilot trial will enroll 30 adolescents aged 12-18 years with MDD, who will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive active or sham stimulation. Participants will undergo a 4-week intervention phase consisting of 20 stimulation sessions, followed by a 12-week follow-up phase, resulting in a total study duration of 16 weeks. Feasibility outcomes will include recruitment performance, treatment completion, and participant retention throughout the study period. Safety will be evaluated through systematic monitoring and recording of adverse events and serious adverse events. Exploratory clinical outcomes will include CDRS-R-defined response and remission, as well as changes in depressive symptoms, anxiety, suicidality, sleep quality, Clinical Global Impression scores, rumination, and health-related quality of life. Exploratory assessments will examine cognitive, neurophysiological, and behavioral changes associated with tACS treatment. Discussion: This pilot trial will provide preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility, acceptability, and safety of adjunctive tACS treatment for adolescents with MDD. The findings will help estimate potential clinical effects and inform the design of a future adequately powered randomized controlled trial.

papers.title: Music During Electronic Fetal Monitoring in Healthy Pregnancies: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-reactive non-stress tests (NSTs) in healthy pregnancies are often caused by fetal sleep rather than by fetal compromise, and music has been proposed as a simple means of increasing fetal reactivity. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether listening to music during electronic fetal monitoring changes fetal movements, baseline fetal heart rate (FHR), FHR accelerations and NST reactivity in healthy pregnant women. Methods: The review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024481527). Four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and ScienceDirect) were searched from inception to June 2024 (date of last search) for randomized, quasi-randomized, non-randomized or crossover-controlled studies, published in English or Turkish, comparing music during fetal monitoring with no music. Methodological quality was appraised with the JBI tools and the certainty of evidence with GRADE. Random-effects (restricted maximum likelihood) meta-analyses used Hedges' g, mean differences (MD) and risk ratios (RR); the primary analyses were restricted to uncomplicated pregnancies and were stratified by study design. Results: Twelve studies (1747 women) were included; eight contributed to the primary meta-analyses, three were used in sensitivity analyses only, and one was synthesized narratively. Music-mostly slow-tempo classical, instrumental or culturally familiar pieces, self-selected by the woman in four studies and delivered through headphones or a personal player for 10-30 min with playback volume adjusted for comfort where reported-increased fetal movements (6 studies, n = 549; g = 0.69, 95% CI 0.30-1.07; I2 = 74%) and FHR accelerations (7 studies, n = 688; g = 0.60, 95% CI 0.24-0.97; I2 = 78%) and modestly increased the proportion of reactive NSTs (5 studies, n = 687; RR = 1.29, 95% CI 1.04-1.59; I2 = 90%), without changing baseline FHR (8 studies, n = 909; MD = 1.3 bpm, 95% CI -0.5 to 3.2). Heterogeneity was high, prediction intervals included no effect, the reactivity effect was not robust to the Hartung-Knapp adjustment or to restriction to randomized trials, and the certainty of evidence was low (very low for reactivity). Conclusions: Music during the NST is a promising, low-risk adjunct that may increase fetal activity and accelerations without altering baseline FHR, but the evidence comes from small, heterogeneous and partly non-randomized studies identified in four databases and two languages; one study reported a shorter time to a reactive result with music, but no study assessed total test duration, downstream clinical management (repeat testing, additional investigations) or perinatal outcomes. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized music protocols are needed before music can be recommended for routine use.

papers.title: Economic Burden of Obesity in Italy.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Quantify the economic burden of obesity in Italy and explore, through an illustrative scenario-based approach, the potential budgetary implications for the Italian National Health Service (NHS) of full reimbursement of modern Obesity Management Medications (OMMs), including GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists. Methods: Narrative review based on literature searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar from inception to September 2026 and covering the epidemiology and economic burden of obesity in Italy, the current AIFA reimbursement landscape, cost-effectiveness evidence for approved OMMs, and international reimbursement models. Evidence synthesized from cost-of-illness studies, clinical trials, health technology assessments, and economic modeling. Results: Obesity imposes an estimated €13 billion annual burden on Italy (direct costs €7.89 billion; indirect costs €5.45 billion). AIFA currently restricts reimbursement primarily to patients with obesity plus type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) via Nota 13, excluding the majority of individuals with obesity. Modern pharmacotherapies, including semaglutide 2.4 mg and tirzepatide, achieve 12-22% weight reduction with favorable cost-effectiveness ratios in several non-Italian economic evaluations, whereas Italian-specific analyses are lacking. In an illustrative scenario-based estimate derived from indirect modelling assumptions (not a validated decision-analytic, budget-impact, or cost-effectiveness model, and without formal sensitivity analysis), full reimbursement could avoid approximately €2-4 billion in obesity-related healthcare costs over 10 years (gross avoided costs; medication expenditure was not netted off and net savings were not demonstrated) through prevention of T2DM, cardiovascular disease (CVD), obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), and other obesity-related comorbidities. Conclusions: Full reimbursement of evidence-based Obesity Management Medications (OMMs) may offer long-term value for the Italian NHS, although reimbursement decisions require dedicated Italian cost-effectiveness and budget-impact analyses. Policy priorities should include expanding AIFA Nota 13 criteria, implementing outcomes-based risk-sharing agreements, and formally recognizing obesity as a chronic disease in Italian health policy.

papers.title: Twenty-Four-Hour Movement Behavior Compositions and Uncorrected Visual Acuity Among Chinese Junior High School Students: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study Using Optimal Time Zone Analysis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Movement behaviors compete for a finite daily time budget. This study examined associations between 24-h movement composition and uncorrected visual acuity among Chinese junior high school students and explored model-derived candidate time allocations. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 865 students, split into derivation (n = 433) and internal validation (n = 432) samples. Robust regression modeled standardized log-transformed uncorrected visual acuity using isometric log-ratio (ilr) coordinates. The highest-predicted 5% of candidate compositions defined an exploratory region. Validation retained all 432 students; alternative search settings and bootstrap resampling assessed sensitivity. Results: The three ilr coordinates were jointly associated with the outcome (Wald χ2 = 28.433, df = 3, p < 0.001). Among 7488 candidates, 375 were selected. Marginal ranges were 190-360 min/day for light-intensity physical activity, 60-80 for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, 510-800 for sedentary behavior, and 310-490 for sleep. Two validation participants fell within all four ranges. Each additional marginal range met was associated with a 0.053-point higher visual acuity score (95% confidence interval: 0.005-0.100; p = 0.031). The corresponding confidence intervals included zero with a 5-min grid and alternative selection fractions. Conclusions: These findings provide preliminary evidence to inform research on daily activity patterns and their associations with uncorrected visual acuity among Chinese junior high school students. The candidate allocations remain exploratory and sensitive to analytical settings. Further studies addressing clustering, confounding, and measurement limitations are needed before specific activity or sleep recommendations can be made.

papers.title: Measuring the Mind Through the Body: A Critical Integrative Narrative Review of Stress and Psychological Inference in Consumer Wearables.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Consumer wearables measure physiological and behavioural signals that may correlate with stress or affect, but physiological stress, subjective distress and psychiatric symptoms require different validation standards. This critical integrative narrative review examines which validation claims are supported and under which conditions. Methods: Structured literature searches were conducted from 9 April to 30 August 2026 in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, APA PsycINFO and IEEE Xplore, covering publications from January 2015 to 30 August 2026, with earlier foundational sources considered where pertinent. Recorded Boolean search strategies, narrative eligibility criteria and a descriptive evidence-appraisal framework guided a targeted integrative synthesis. As a narrative rather than systematic review, database hit counts and exclusion tallies were not recorded, and no PRISMA selection flow is asserted. Results: Selected laboratory and short-term field studies support stress detection under defined conditions, and personalised approaches are promising. Naturalistic associations vary with the target construct and comparator: in a study enrolling 781 students, analysed outcome samples differed (stress, n = 730; sleep, n = 709; tiredness, n = 781). Wearable-self-report sleep associations were stronger than those for tiredness, and Garmin stress was only weakly associated with self-reported stress (standardised β = 0.026, 95% CI 0.019-0.033; n = 730). Sensor-equity findings have different endpoints and do not establish disparities in HRV-based psychological scores. Conclusions: Wearable validity should be assessed against the exact physiological, psychological or clinical claim. Five proposed, claim-sensitive checkpoints operationalise recurrent gaps identified across the five analytic axes and are mapped to established V3/V3+ and COSMIN concepts; they have not been independently validated.

papers.title: Evaluation and Management of Central Sleep Apnea in Adults: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.abstract: Central sleep apnea (CSA) comprises a group of disorders characterized by recurrent re-duction or cessation of respiratory effort during sleep, resulting from diminished or absent central ventilatory drive. This narrative review presents current knowledge about the pathophysiology, diagnostics, classification, and treatment of adult CSA. Methods: The literature was chosen from peer-reviewed studies, clinical trials, guidelines, and systematic reviews on adult CSA with particular focus on CSA related to heart failure, opioids, high altitude, treatment-emergent CSA, positive airway pressure modes, pharmacological therapy, and phrenic nerve stimulation. Results: Current data suggest that the phenotype-directed approach with PSG, respiratory effort, comorbidity, and pharmacological history assessment allowed for the classification of CSA syndromes in relation to hyperventilation, hypoventilation, treatment-induced, and cause-dependent forms. CPAP, oxygen, BPAP-ST, ASV, acetazolamide, and transvenous phrenic nerve stimulators have different efficacy in certain CSA types with unclear data on the long-term cardiovascular outcomes, especially in patients with heart failure and exposure to opioids. Conclusions: Adult CSA management should be individualized according to mechanism, comorbidity profile, symptom burden, treatment safety, and measurable clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Multi-Type Clinical Interaction Modeling for Identifying Factors Associated with Cardiovascular Disease in Obstructive Sleep Apnea via an Interpretable Heterogeneous Graph Transformer.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep disorder strongly associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). The relationship between OSA and CVD is complex, involving multiple physiological and clinical factors. Identifying key contributors to cardiovascular risk in OSA patients is essential for early intervention, personalized treatment, and improved patient outcomes. Methods: We propose a heterogeneous graph learning model, RiskHGT, to identify influential clinical factors and interaction patterns associated with CVD in a cross-sectional analysis distinguishing OSA patients with and without prevalent CVD. By leveraging the advantages of heterogeneous graphs in modeling multi-relational medical data, RiskHGT captures intricate relationships among clinical factors and enables interpretation of the most influential factors associated with CVD in OSA patients. The model was trained and evaluated on two large-scale clinical sleep cohorts, the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) and the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), with predictive performance assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Results: RiskHGT achieved superior predictive performance compared with baseline machine learning and graph-based models, reaching an AUROC of up to 0.94 and an AUPRC of up to 0.90. Fasting glucose, diastolic blood pressure, smoking status, and age were identified as the factors most strongly associated with CVD in OSA patients. Conclusions: RiskHGT provides interpretable, attention-based insights into clinical factors associated with CVD in patients with OSA. The framework may have potential for clinical use, but external and prospective validation is required before any clinical application.

papers.title: Dihydromyricetin Regulates Sleep and Protects Against Oxidative Stress in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.abstract: Sleep homeostasis is essential for health, and sleep disturbances contribute to multi-organ failure mortality. Dihydromyricetin (DMY), a flavonoid from Ampelopsis grossedentata, possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Although DMY alleviates sleep-deprivation-induced cognitive deficits, its role in sleep regulation remains unclear. Here, we show that DMY increases sleep duration and modulates sleep fragmentation in young, aged, and short-sleep mutant Drosophila. Transcriptomic and genetic analyses reveal that DMY alters the expression of neurotransmitter-related genes, including VGAT and Trhn, suggesting potential involvement of GABAergic and serotonergic signaling. In paraquat-induced oxidative stress models, DMY boosts antioxidant gene expression, alleviates oxidative damage and intestinal apoptosis, restores stress-disrupted sleep, and extends lifespan. Together, our findings demonstrate that DMY improves sleep-associated parameters, potentially involving neurotransmitter-related signaling pathways while concurrently mitigating oxidative stress-induced damage, thereby promoting organismal health and suggesting its potential for preventing and treating sleep disorders and aging-related decline.

papers.title: Phagocytic NADPH Oxidase (NOX-2) as a Central Oxidative Effector in Experimental Models of Transportation-Noise-Induced Cardiovascular and Cerebral Disease.
papers.abstract: Transportation noise is an established cardiovascular risk factor. More than 112 million Europeans are chronically exposed above the thresholds of the Environmental Noise Directive, with approximately 73,000 premature deaths and 1.5 million disability-adjusted life years attributed annually. Large cohort studies demonstrate near-linear exposure-response relationships with ischaemic heart disease, myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure and type 2 diabetes, and more recently with dementia, Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson disease, independent of air pollution, detectable below guideline limits and stronger for night-time exposure. The noise reaction model attributes these effects to annoyance, sleep fragmentation and activation of the sympathetic nervous system and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, converging on oxidative stress, inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. This review argues that the phagocytic NADPH oxidase NOX-2 (gp91phox) is a decisive oxidative effector within that cascade in experimental models of noise exposure. NOX-2 is upregulated in the vasculature and brain after aircraft noise exposure, is delivered to the vessel wall largely by infiltrating myelomonocytic cells, and drives superoxide formation, peroxynitrite generation, and uncoupling of endothelial and neuronal nitric oxide synthase. Genetic deletion of Nox2 prevents, essentially, the entire vascular phenotype and attenuates cerebral oxidative stress and neuroinflammation, whereas ablation of lysozyme M-positive myeloid cells reproduces the vascular but not cerebral protection. These causal data derive predominantly from short-term rodent aircraft-noise models and require further extrapolation in chronic human exposure settings. In line with this proposed mechanism of action, noise-mediated organ damage can be mitigated by pharmacological and lifestyle-associated anti-oxidant interventions that are also briefly summarised here.

papers.title: Effects of Empagliflozin on Oxidative Stress in Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Heart Failure: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and heart failure (HF) share pathways involving intermittent hypoxia and oxidative stress. This randomized clinical trial with blinded endpoint assessment evaluated systemic oxidative balance during sequential treatment with empagliflozin and continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP). Seventy adults with HF and predominantly obstructive OSA were randomized to empagliflozin 10 mg daily plus background HF therapy (n = 37) or background therapy alone (n = 33). Assessments were performed at baseline, month 3, and month 6; CPAP was initiated in both groups after month 3. The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in AHI change from baseline to month 3, estimated using a baseline-adjusted linear mixed-effects model. TOS, TAS, and OSI were exploratory outcomes. Median AHI (IQR) in the study and control groups was 58.9 (28.5-70.3) and 55.0 (29.9-67.8) at baseline, and 44.2 (22.4-59.3) and 52.2 (30.8-70.2) at month 3, respectively. The baseline-adjusted between-group difference in AHI change from baseline to month 3 was -11.04 (95% CI -16.72 to -5.35; p < 0.001). The exploratory mixed-effects models showed lower TOS and OSI and higher TAS in the study group at both follow-up visits (all p < 0.001). Empagliflozin initiation was associated with early reductions in AHI and improvements in exploratory markers of systemic oxidative balance before CPAP initiation. Although the shared CPAP phase did not allow separation of drug and CPAP effects, these findings support further investigation of the respiratory and redox effects of empagliflozin in patients with coexisting HF and OSA.

papers.title: TurboRhythmPat and Directed Rhythm Lobish: An Explainable Multi-Selector EEG Model for Recognising Attack and Post-Attack States in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiple sclerosis (MS) advances through attacks and partial recoveries, yet electroencephalography (EEG) has hardly been used to recognise an attack from the period that follows it, and most EEG models neither test unseen patients nor show which rhythm and electrode pair shaped a decision. Methods: We present an explainable model built around TurboRhythmPat, a feature extractor that codes each 15 s, 19-channel segment as 1805 addressable source-rhythm-target routes in five EEG rhythms. Four iterative feature selectors and their six pairwise intersections form ten selector branches, a self-organised k-nearest-neighbour classifier (tkNN) labels every branch, and iterative majority voting fuses the branch outputs. Directed Rhythm Lobish (DRLobish) decodes the routes behind the selected output into rhythm and electrode-pair statements. We analysed 57 recordings from 19 patients recorded during and after an attack and from 19 healthy controls. Results: Under fully nested leave-one-subject-out validation, in which every data-driven choice was made within the training participants, the attack and post-attack recordings of unseen patients were separated with 65.61% segment-level and 76.32% recording-level accuracy, and patient-level accuracy exceeded chance in 13 of 19 patients (Wilcoxon p = 0.0022). The between-person tasks did not exceed chance (37.92%, 52.51% and 33.17%), and the non-nested estimates (85.71% for attack versus post-attack) were inflated by model selection on the test participants. A permutation-based maxT test over all 1805 routes found no route after family-wise correction (smallest adjusted p = 0.076). Conclusions: Because the attack recording always came first, treatment timing was not documented, no dedicated artefact correction was applied, and the controls were older, the differences are not interpreted as relapse-related changes, and larger prospective cohorts are needed before clinical use.

papers.title: Lifestyle and Clinical Correlates of Myosteatosis Among African Caribbean Men and Women.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Myosteatosis, i.e., adiposity in and around skeletal muscle, is a hallmark of adverse muscle aging, more common among women than men, and associated with several major health outcomes, including cardiometabolic diseases and functional decline. We investigated lifestyle and clinical correlates of skeletal muscle adiposity among an understudied cohort of Afro-Caribbean men and women. Methods: Among 213 men and 530 women aged 50-80 from the Tobago Health Study, several lifestyle and clinical factors were assessed, including accelerometry-derived physical activity and sleep duration, diet, and medications. Lifestyle risk scores were based on smoking, alcohol, physical activity, and body mass index. Calf muscle density was measured using peripheral quantitative computed tomography, with lower values suggesting more muscle adiposity. Results: Women were more likely to abstain from cigarettes and alcohol, but less physically active, with more sugar intake and lower muscle density than men. Using Isotemporal Substitution, cross-sectionally replacing sedentary time with sleep or light-intensity physical activity was significantly associated with higher muscle density. In multivariable models, older age, larger waist circumference, and taking diabetes medications were cross-sectionally associated with lower muscle density, as well as shorter sleep among men and taking anti-hypertensive medications among women. Conclusions: Older Afro-Caribbean women vs. men had healthier substance habits, but lower activity and muscle density, suggesting more muscle adiposity. Modifiable behaviors, particularly sedentary time, sleep duration, and light-intensity physical activity were strongly associated with muscle density. Interventions that replace sedentary time with light-intensity physical activity and sleep may be feasible and sustainable approaches to reduce myosteatosis.

papers.title: Music Listening Prolongs Time to Exhaustion via Two Dissociable Neural Pathways: Evidence from EEG Network Analysis.
papers.abstract: Although music reliably prolongs time to exhaustion (TTE), the neural mechanisms behind this benefit remain unclear. We examined whether self-selected preferred music alters task-related electroencephalographic (EEG) network reorganization during a sustained handgrip to exhaustion. Thirty-four healthy young men completed a fixed-load (10 kg) handgrip task with and without music in a within-subject design, with each trial divided into early, middle, and late phases (0-30%, 30-70%, 70-100% of individual TTE). Source-localized EEG from three networks (central executive, salience, sensorimotor) was analyzed with phase-locking value and graph-theoretical metrics in four frequency bands. Music prolonged TTE by 20.6 s (t(33) = 4.67, p < 0.001, dz = 0.80) and raised local efficiency and the clustering coefficient in all four bands. Beta- and gamma-band coupling was lower in the middle phase than in the early and late phases under both conditions, with no condition × phase interaction. Although none of the 40 exploratory index-level correlations survived false discovery rate correction, the hypothesis-guided two-pathway model accounted for 36.1% of the variance in ΔTTE (F(2,31) = 8.76, p < 0.001; cross-validated Q2 = 0.233): both expressed as the change from no music to music, the increase in alpha-band local efficiency (β = 11.58 s/SD, 95% CI 4.50-19.15) and the reduction in gamma-band coupling (β = 11.92 s/SD, 95% CI 4.94-18.51) were each independently associated with the TTE gain (VIF = 1.01). The size of the benefit therefore tracked two dissociable pathways of comparable weight, an alpha-band efficiency pathway and a gamma-band effort-attenuation pathway.

papers.title: Phenotypic Characterization and Owner-Reported Course of Presumptive Paroxysmal Dyskinesia in Spitz Dogs: A Multicenter Retrospective Case Series.
papers.abstract: Episodes clinically classified as presumptive paroxysmal dyskinesia (PDx) in Spitz dogs remain poorly characterized. This multicenter retrospective observational case series evaluated 33 client-owned Spitz dogs whose recurrent episodes were clinically classified as presumptive PDx through neurology services in Belgium, Brazil, and Colombia. Clinical data, episode characteristics, triggers, treatments, dietary management, and owner-reported course were obtained from medical records, questionnaires, and videos. Among 31 dogs with available age data, median age at the first observed episode was 36 months (interquartile range [IQR], 21-71.5), and median age at first veterinary consultation was 52 months (IQR, 31.5-83). All dogs exhibited episodic involuntary motor abnormalities involving at least one limb; dystonic posturing or abnormal limb contractions were identified in available recordings. All four limbs were involved in 60.6%, axial signs were reported in 51.5%, recumbency in 57.6%, and tremors in 36.4%. Apparent responsiveness was preserved in available recordings, and no consistent pre-episodic or evident post-episodic abnormalities were identified. Salivation, mydriasis, and vomiting were reported in 33.3%, 9.1%, and 6.1% of dogs, respectively. Episodes lasted 1-5 min in most dogs. Owner-suspected triggers were identified in 24.2% of cases, most frequently stress and/or excitement. Most antiseizure medication regimens were not associated with owner-reported improvement. A gluten-free diet was attempted in 23/33 dogs (69.7%); owner-reported improvement occurred in 14/23 (60.9%), whereas response assessment was uncertain in the remaining nine dogs. Improvements were also reported spontaneously in untreated dogs. Dietary management was uncontrolled and not standardized; these observations do not establish dietary efficacy. Because simultaneous video-EEG was not systematically performed, the findings do not establish a nonepileptic mechanism and should be interpreted using an integrated assessment of episode phenomenology and temporal evolution.

papers.title: High Accuracy Is Not Generalization: Evaluation Design in EEG Mental Arithmetic Classification.
papers.abstract: Classification of rest versus mental arithmetic in the public EEGMAT dataset is often reported with accuracies of 88-99%. Such results usually come from subject-dependent designs, in which epochs from the same person appear in both training and test sets. This design is often intentional and can be appropriate for within-subject prediction. It becomes misleading, however, when the resulting accuracy is read as evidence that a model will work on unseen subjects. We tested how much of the reported accuracy survives a stricter evaluation. Balancing and augmentation were confined to the training data, test sets kept their natural class ratio, and models were selected on validation data. A multilayer perceptron on 57 simple time-domain features was evaluated under four protocols, with over 1000 trained networks and subject-level confidence intervals. Balancing before splitting gave kappa 0.77-0.88, with 45-47% of test items duplicated in training. A correct random epoch split gave kappa 0.29-0.58, so duplicate contamination explains most of the inflation. Leave-one-subject-out evaluation gave kappa 0.19-0.26 and ROC-AUC 0.66-0.71, which is above chance but modest. The remaining subject-dependent advantage (kappa difference 0.06-0.32) is consistent with subject-identity leakage but does not prove it. To our knowledge, no previous study on EEGMAT has examined this question. Results refer to the available 36-subject pool, not to the general population.

papers.title: Exploratory Characterization of Optical Filters and Visual Acuity Responses Using Estimated Algorithmic Complexity.
papers.abstract: To explore the estimated algorithmic complexity of encoded optical-filter transmittance spectra and visual-response data using the Block Decomposition Method (BDM), alongside conventional optical descriptors and symbol-frequency Shannon entropy. Four filters with different pigmentation times were each measured in a single spectral acquisition. Visual thresholds for detection, separation, alignment, and recognition were measured under baseline and four filter conditions in 235 eyes from 118 participants. Each spectrum and task-condition response column was independently min-max normalized and discretized. Wavelength-ordered one-dimensional BDM was the primary spectral analysis; two-dimensional arrangements were supplementary. Sensitivity to encoding, block size, observation order, remainder handling, and matrix representation was assessed. Visual changes were summarized descriptively within eyes; unavailable participant linkage prevented adjustment for fellow-eye dependence. Under the original binary encoding, spectral Shannon entropy increased with pigmentation time, whereas one-dimensional normalized BDM (nBDM) ranged from 0.010058 to 0.010326 and followed a different filter ordering. Several spectral and visual-response rankings changed across computational settings. Within-eye mean threshold changes were negative across filters for detection and recognition, while separation and alignment showed different patterns. Visual-response nBDM described the encoded sequences and did not directly quantify these threshold changes. BDM provided an exploratory characterization conditional on the selected representation and analysis settings. Sensitivity analyses did not establish sampling uncertainty or statistical robustness. The findings do not validate filter classes or demonstrate clinical benefit, causality, or prediction of visual outcomes from spectral complexity. Repeated measurements, broader filter sampling, participant-linked data, and independent validation are required to assess practical utility.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms Linking Chronic Stress and Chronic Pain: From Mechanisms to Multimodal Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Chronic stress may influence vulnerability to persistent pain, the transition from acute to chronic pain, and symptom maintenance through interacting neuroendocrine, neuroimmune, neuronal, and behavioral pathways. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and glucocorticoid regulation, inflammatory activation and resolution, glial-neuronal signaling, descending pain modulation, and emerging transcriptomic and epigenetic mechanisms. We distinguish findings directly demonstrated in stress-exposure models from mechanisms established in neuropathic or inflammatory pain and from largely associative human molecular observations. Experimental studies implicate pathways including FKBP5/FKBP51, microglial P2X4-p38 MAPK-BDNF-TrkB-KCC2 signaling, inflammasomes, and periaqueductal gray-rostral ventromedial medulla circuits; however, causal roles vary by model, stressor, disease stage, and pain phenotype. We also examine how sleep disruption, distress, physical activity, and fear-avoidance interact with pain processing. A stage-dependent, phenotype-sensitive synthesis differentiates susceptibility, chronification, and maintenance and distinguishes central sensitization from nociplastic pain. Established multimodal management should be guided by diagnosis, functional goals, and modifiable clinical factors rather than unvalidated endocrine or omics markers. Prospective stress-characterized cohorts, causal pathway testing, and biomarker-by-treatment trials are needed to determine whether molecular findings can improve prevention and individualized care.

papers.title: Aloysia citrodora (Lemon Verbena) and Sleep Regulation: Phytochemical Constituents, Molecular Mechanisms, Preclinical and Clinical Evidence, and Translational Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Aloysia citrodora (lemon verbena) is traditionally used to promote relaxation and sleep, but its clinical efficacy and underlying mechanisms remain uncertain. This narrative review critically evaluates its phytochemical constituents, potential sleep-regulatory mechanisms, preclinical and clinical evidence, pharmacokinetics, safety, and translational challenges. Literature published through 16 October 2026 was identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, supplemented by trial registries, regulatory documents, and reference screening. Evidence was qualitatively synthesized using methodological principles informed by SANRA and PRISMA-S. Aloysia citrodora contains phenylethanoid glycosides, particularly verbascoside, flavonoids, and volatile terpenoids. Preclinical investigations suggest sedative and sleep-modulating effects, with GABAergic and adenosinergic signaling representing plausible but incompletely validated mechanisms. Randomized clinical trials report improvements in subjective sleep quality and selected sleep-continuity parameters. However, objective improvements are modest, findings are heterogeneous, and human polysomnographic evidence is unavailable. Limited independent replication, uncertain systemic and central nervous system exposure, and insufficient long-term safety data restrict clinical interpretation. Aloysia citrodora may offer complementary benefits for selected sleep complaints, but evidence remains insufficient to establish efficacy for chronic insomnia. Independent, adequately powered trials using standardized preparations, prespecified clinically meaningful outcomes, objective sleep assessments, and integrated pharmacokinetic and safety evaluations are needed before broader clinical recommendations can be supported.

papers.title: NAD+/NADH as the Electrochemical Currency and Other Specific Electron Transfer Molecules in Health and Disease.
papers.abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, in its oxidized (NAD+) and reduced (NADH) forms, is a central metabolic cofactor that links cellular energy production to a wide array of signaling processes, including DNA repair, chromatin regulation, calcium signaling, and circadian control. Beyond its classical role as an electron carrier in redox reactions of glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation via Complex I of the electron transport chain), NAD+ serves as an obligate substrate for several classes of non-redox enzymes. These include the sirtuin family, poly (ADP-ribose) polymerases (PARPs), the ectoenzymes CD38/CD157, and SARM1. This dual functionality positions NAD+ as a key convergence point between metabolism and cell signaling. NAD+/NADH metabolism is highly dynamic and compartmentalized. Distinct subcellular pools exist in the mitochondria, cytosol, and nucleus, with very limited free exchange of the dinucleotide itself across the inner mitochondrial membrane. The NAD+/NADH ratio-rather than total pool size alone-serves as a critical readout of cellular redox state: cytosolic ratios are normally high (favoring oxidative metabolism and glycolysis), while mitochondrial ratios are lower. Both the ratio and absolute levels fluctuate with age, diet, nutrient availability, oxygen tension, and other contextual factors, yet remain tightly regulated through biosynthetic pathways (de novo from tryptophan, Preiss-Handler from nicotinic acid, and the dominant salvage pathway via NAMPT) and consumption by the enzymes noted above. Disruption of NAD+ homeostasis is now recognized as a hallmark of aging and a contributor to multiple age-related pathologies. Age-associated declines in NAD+ levels and shifts in the NAD+/NADH ratio impair mitochondrial function, sirtuin activity, DNA repair, and stress resistance, while promoting senescence, inflammation, and metabolic inflexibility. Altered NAD+ metabolism is equally prominent in cancer. Tumor cells frequently upregulate NAD+ salvage enzymes (especially NAMPT) to expand the total NADH pool, support high glycolytic flux through continuous NAD+ regeneration (primarily via lactate dehydrogenase), maintain redox balance, and enhance resistance to genotoxic stress via PARP activity. Compartment-specific changes are also critical: reverse electron transport (RET) at Complex I, enriched in certain cancer stem cells (e.g., glioma stem cells), lowers the mitochondrial NAD+/NADH ratio. This inhibits SIRT3, stabilizes HIF-1α, and sustains stemness programs (e.g., SOX2), thereby favoring tumor progression and therapy resistance. NADH reductive stress more broadly can drive metabolic reprogramming that supports proliferation and survival. This review examines the biochemistry and subcellular compartmentalization of NAD+/NADH metabolism, its physiological roles in healthy cells, the mechanisms by which malignant cells reprogram NAD+ metabolism to their advantage (including RET-driven redox shifts), and the therapeutic strategies currently under investigation. These range from NAMPT inhibitors (which face challenges of limited single-agent efficacy and dose-limiting toxicities in clinical trials) and NAD+-boosting precursors (nicotinamide riboside, nicotinamide mononucleotide, and related compounds) to agents that modulate Complex I/RET or other nodes of NAD+ homeostasis, with the goal of exploiting or correcting these alterations in aging and cancer. The primary aim of this review is to examine NAD+/NADH metabolism in the context of cancer within the broader framework of electrochemical network deregulation. Aging and neurodegenerative diseases are also briefly discussed.

papers.title: Association of Maternal Preconception Chronodisruption and Oocyte m6A Modification with Multi-Organ Phenotypic Alterations in Offspring.
papers.abstract: While the natural light-dark cycle is crucial for health, modern lifestyles are associated with increased artificial light exposure, including during reproductive windows. Although maternal light exposure has been linked to adverse offspring outcomes, comprehensive multisystem evaluations remain scarce. In this study, we established a rat model of continuous light exposure to simulate maternal preconception chronodisruption. We found that preconception chronodisruption was associated with multisystem abnormalities in offspring, including increased body weight, diminished cardiac function, thickened vessel walls, elevated blood pressure, and insulin resistance. Behavioral tests revealed stress-coping and behavioral despair-related responses along with impaired cognitive function. The m6A methylation patterns in maternal oocytes were altered and enriched in developmental pathways related to the brain, muscle, and cardiovascular systems. Collectively, preconception exposure to continuous light was associated with physiological and behavioral deficits in offspring, and these deficits were potentially related to m6A RNA modification changes in maternal oocytes. These findings underscore the importance of preconception environmental factors and suggest a potential link between oocyte epigenetics and developmental programming.

papers.title: Patient Perspectives Following a One-Week Medication Washout in Early-Stage Parkinson's Disease Patients.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Therapeutic washout protocols, where Parkinson's disease (PD) patients discontinue their medication, are used in clinical trials to evaluate disease progression without the overt influence of symptomatic treatments. While prior washout studies focused on clinical outcomes, the participant experiences of undergoing an extended washout have not been examined. This study characterizes early-stage PD participants' expectations, symptom experiences, emotional responses, and reflections following a one-week medication washout. Methods: Twenty early-stage PD participants enrolled in a one-week washout study (15 M/5 F; aged 65.7 ± 6.7 years; medication duration 1.8 ± 0.8 years; LEDD 490 ± 414 mg). Semi-structured interviews (~1 h) were audio-recorded, transcribed, and coded by trained coders. Transcripts were analyzed using an inductive-deductive approach to identify common themes and develop a conceptual framework. Results: All 20 participants were interviewed, including one who withdrew on day 5 due to intolerable symptoms. Recalled expectations ranged from confidence to fear of symptom exacerbation, and reassurance from study personnel reduced pre-washout anxiety. Symptoms included sleep disruption, restless legs symptoms, stiffness, tremor, and progressive motor decline that often intensified in the latter half of the week. Emotional responses ranged from frustration and isolation to equanimity. Upon resuming medications, recovery timelines varied. Many participants gained new insight into their medication's efficacy, and some perceived their unmedicated state as a glimpse of how they might function as their disease progresses. Conclusions: This study provides the first characterization of participant experiences following a one-week medication washout in early-stage PD. These perspectives can inform washout protocol design, participant support, and retention in future clinical trials.

papers.title: When Subject-Level Validation Is Not Enough: Acquisition Format Confounding in a Public Depression Electroencephalography Archive.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Participant-disjoint evaluation prevents electroencephalography (EEG) windows from crossing training and test partitions, but cannot remove cohort-wide technical variables aligned with outcome. We examined this distinction in the public Mumtaz/HUSM depression EEG archive. Methods: After excluding duplicate groups and performing fixed signal quality controlling, 53 participants were retained. Five whole-head relative-power features were evaluated using nested participant-disjoint class-balanced logistic regression with training-fold local scaling and selection. Results: In this exposed cohort, the model achieved mean balanced accuracy of 0.9158 and ROC-AUC of 0.9363; tested graph-recurrent and domain adaptation models were weaker. A subsequent 1000-shuffle nested permutation audit conditional on the selected five-band pipeline gave p=0.000999. Exploratory controls using file size, raw channel count, and normalized byte rates each achieved balanced accuracy of 0.9046, while duration alone achieved 0.6788. Raw European Data Format (EDF) channel configuration nearly determined archive label: 22/26 controls had 22-channel files, compared to only 1/27 depression-labeled participants (Fisher's exact p=6.80×10-10). Conclusions: These metadata expose a label-aligned acquisition/export structure, showing that strong participant-disjoint performance and permutation significance do not establish depression-specific EEG information when acquisition format and archive label are closely aligned. Therefore, public EEG studies should combine participant isolation with early metadata audits, and should require outcome variation within acquisition strata prior to physiological or clinical interpretation.

papers.title: EEG Functional Connectivity Differentiation Between Eyes-Closed and Eyes-Open Resting States Following Posterior Brain Damage.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Eyes-closed and eyes-open resting states rely on distinct patterns of functional connectivity, particularly within posterior cortical regions. Posterior brain damage affecting the visual system may therefore alter the typical modulation of functional connectivity across resting conditions. Methods: To investigate this issue, EEG recordings were collected during eyes-closed and eyes-open rest from hemianopic patients with left and right posterior lesions, control patients with anterior lesions, and healthy controls. Functional connectivity was assessed across frequency bands using phase-based measures. Results: Within-group analyses showed that the typical EC-EO decrease in posterior alpha-band functional connectivity observed in healthy participants and anterior lesion controls did not reach statistical significance in either hemianopic group. However, direct between-group comparisons revealed a significantly reduced modulation of posterior alpha connectivity across resting conditions only in patients with right posterior lesions relative to other groups. In addition, hemianopic patients with right posterior lesions also exhibited increased theta-band connectivity in the right hemisphere, independently of the resting condition. Conclusions: These findings suggest that posterior brain damage, particularly involving the right hemisphere, may affect the functional mechanisms underlying the state-dependent modulation of posterior alpha-band connectivity, providing insight into the electrophysiological consequences of damage to posterior cortical regions.

papers.title: Long-Term Music Training Is Associated with Auditory-Frontal Cortical Responses in Mandarin-Speaking Children with Cochlear Implants: A Clinical High-Density EEG Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Children with cochlear implants (CIs) develop speech and language under electrically mediated auditory input, yet it remains unclear whether cumulative musical experience is associated with cortical speech processing. This study examined whether music-training duration was related to prefrontal responses during Mandarin speech-feature processing in children with CIs using high-density electroencephalography (EEG) source localization. Methods: Thirty Mandarin-speaking children with CIs from the Tianjin Little Dolphin Hearing-Loss Children's Choir were grouped by cumulative music-training duration: short (<3 years), medium (3-5 years), and long (>5 years). Participants completed audiological and speech-perception assessments and underwent high-density EEG during a Mandarin multi-feature oddball paradigm including tone, consonant, vowel, duration, and intensity deviants. Mismatch negativity (MMN) responses were source-localized to characterize cortical activation. Results: Behavioral measures, including aided hearing thresholds and speech-perception accuracy, were comparable across groups. In contrast, source analysis showed progressively stronger prefrontal activation with longer music-training duration. This pattern was most evident for vowel and consonant deviants, whereas duration-related responses showed little variation. In adjusted linear models, longer training duration was positively associated with prefrontal activation for intensity (p = 0.002) and tone (p = 0.022), with marginal associations for consonant (p = 0.057) and vowel (p = 0.058) deviants. Conclusions: Longer music-training duration was associated with stronger auditory-frontal cortical responses during Mandarin speech-feature processing in children with CIs, despite comparable behavioral auditory outcomes across groups. These preliminary findings suggest that high-density EEG may provide a complementary clinical neurophysiological tool for evaluating rehabilitation-related cortical differences in pediatric CI users. Future longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these associations reflect training-related developmental changes.

papers.title: Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy with a Suspected Catamenial Component: A Neuroendocrine Trajectory.
papers.abstract: We report the nine-year neurological and endocrine follow-up of a woman diagnosed with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) during adolescence, whose treating neurologist noted a possible catamenial association. The patient retrospectively reported menarche at age 12 (summer 2013) anddaily awakening myoclonus lasting 15-20 min after awakening, beginning on 17 January 2014, with no meaningful improvement during lamotrigine treatment. Awakening myoclonus, dropping objects, without loss of consciousness, and a September 2017 electroencephalography (EEG) report describing 5-6 Hz epileptiform complexes supported the clinical diagnosis. Menstrual records showed cycles of 33-36 days in late 2017. Estradiol and progesterone were measured on 4 December (cycle day 5; 49.4 pg/mL and 0.27 ng/mL) and 20 December 2017 (cycle day 21; 455 pg/mL and 1.16 ng/mL). The latter sample preceded the next menstruation by 13 days, without confirmation of ovulation, and cannot establish a luteal defect or C3 (inadequate luteal-phase) catamenial pattern. Following neurological treatment adjustments in 2017, the last reported seizure occurred in October 2017, before the endocrine measurements and the subsequent dydrogesterone recommendation; seizure freedom continued after cyclic dydrogesterone was introduced in the therapeutic program. During follow-up, levetiracetam was discontinued in June 2023 and lamotrigine was gradually reduced. At the July 2026 visit, complete lamotrigine withdrawal was planned. This case illustrates the importance of accurate chronology and the distinction between suspected menstrual modulation, documented seizure remission under treatment and an untested hormonal mechanism.

papers.title: Missing and Superfluous Prosodic Accents in L2 English Focus Processing: Behavioral and ERP Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Second-language (L2) listeners interpret prosodic prominence in relation to contextual-focus expectations. This study examined behavioral and ERP responses to English prosody-focus mismatch across two recruitment-defined proficiency strata, two focus positions, and two linked word-locked prominence configurations. Methods: Thirty participants completed an auditory question-answer appropriateness-judgment task while electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded. Prosody-focus matching and focus position were manipulated. Event-related potentials (ERPs) were analyzed separately at the contextually focused word and the background word. Behavioral responses were modeled with mixed-effects models and time-resolved ERP trajectories were analyzed with generalized additive mixed models. Results: Mismatch reduced accuracy at both focus positions, with a numerically larger reduction for sentence-final focus. Reaction-time mismatch effects were not reliable within either position and did not differ reliably across positions. At focused words, missing prominence elicited predominantly negative-going effects, with nominal Group × Matching interactions at both focus positions in the 300-550-ms range. At background words, superfluous prominence elicited predominantly positive-going effects, with a nominal Group × Matching interaction under sentence-final focus in the 550-1000-ms range. Direct window-level comparisons further showed that mismatch responses differed between focused and background words, with nominal Group × Word Role interactions, whereas no reliable overall modulation of this contrast by focus position was observed. Conclusions: Missing and superfluous prominence were associated with different ERP response patterns, whose interpretation requires consideration of both local accentuation and contextual focus. Evidence for proficiency-related modulation remained uncertain, and the observed sentence-final accuracy difference was sensitive to random-effects structure.

papers.title: Postictal Brain Network Dynamics and Their Clinical Applications.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The postictal state encompasses complex changes in brain-network organisation, involving multiple pathophysiological processes whose interactions remain incompletely understood. An integrative approach across recording modalities and spatial and temporal scales may help elucidate the relationships underlying these changes. This review provides a network-centred synthesis of postictal dynamics, examining the ictal-postictal transition, operational definitions of recovery, and the potential clinical relevance of postictal network changes. Methods: We reviewed electrophysiological, metabolic, neurovascular, imaging and modelling findings across experimental seizure models, seizures in human epilepsy and electroconvulsive therapy-induced seizures, with particular emphasis on the temporal evolution of postictal brain activity and quantitative approaches to defining recovery. Results: Across modalities, seizure offset does not consistently mark immediate restoration of the preictal state. Postictal activity evolves over seconds to hours through changes in suppression and slowing, signal complexity, functional connectivity, information flow, perfusion and metabolism. These patterns are influenced by seizure propagation, severity, localisation and clinical context. Quantitative approaches further indicate that electrophysiological recovery may outlast visually apparent abnormalities and may dissociate from behavioural recovery. Postictal dynamics may provide clinically exploitable information for epileptogenic-network localisation and surgical prognosis, objective assessment of recovery, investigation of autonomic dysfunction and sudden unexpected death in epilepsy, automated seizure-state classification and therapeutic targeting. Conclusions: The postictal period encompasses heterogeneous network dynamics organised across multiple spatial and temporal scales, which may interact with pathophysiological processes underlying recovery. Its systematic characterisation may improve understanding of seizure termination and recovery while expanding the clinical utility of peri-ictal signal analysis.

papers.title: Deep Learning Method Using Temporal-Spectral-Spatial Feature Fusion for Epileptic Seizure Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Epilepsy is a recurrent cerebral disorder, and the sudden onset of seizures can result in accidental injuries or even life-threatening events for patients. In clinical practice, epileptic seizure prediction can provide warnings prior to the onset of seizures, alerting patients to take safety precautions and assisting neurologists in implementing timely interventions to suppress seizures. Therefore, accurate prediction is crucial for improving patients' quality of life and clinical treatment outcomes. However, due to insufficient extraction of effective features from epileptic signals, the performance of prediction models is often limited. Methods: In this study, a novel deep learning model was proposed that integrated temporal-spectral-spatial features to address this limitation. Wavelet convolutions and temporal convolutions were employed to achieve the temporal-spectral representation network. Subsequently, the fused features were further processed using bidirectional long short-term memory networks and a dynamic multigraph attention network based on time slices to extract temporal and spatial features for seizure prediction. Results: The performance of the proposed model was comprehensively evaluated on the CHB-MIT and Siena databases using both segment-based and event-based evaluations. For the CHB-MIT database, the model achieved a sensitivity of 96.09 ± 8.83% and a false prediction rate of 0.021 ± 0.032/h.
