Interviews revealed three thematic steps in the pathway from measuring high BP at home to seeking medical advice: understanding when BP is high, recognizing it as abnormal and urgent, and engaging with the health system. Most participants could distinguish normal from high readings and understood the risks of hypertension in pregnancy. However, this knowledge did not consistently prompt urgent action. Some attributed high readings to stress, poor sleep, or recent activity, and chose to rest and recheck. Others repeated previous telephone advice to self-manage before calling again. Decisions to contact the phoneline were shaped by prior advice, expected responses, and interpersonal experiences. Barriers included shyness, concern about disturbing midwives, and uncertainty about whether one high reading required action. Women were more willing to call when interactions made them feel reassured, valued, and cared for. Women generally recognized high BP as abnormal and potentially harmful, but patient interpretation, interpersonal communication, and inconsistent health service advice sometimes delayed contact with providers. Home BP monitoring programs in low-resource settings should strengthen patient training and ensure that telephone response staff provide supportive, standardized, and guideline-consistent advice.

papers.title: 24-hour movement-behavior guideline attainment and school functioning in children with and without co-occurring ADHD and learning disability: evidence from the NSCH 2018-2024.
papers.abstract: Twenty-four-hour movement behaviors, including physical activity, recreational screen time, and sleep, have been linked to child health and functional outcomes. However, most studies have examined general populations or single-diagnosis groups. We examined the association between 24-hour movement-behavior guideline attainment and school-related functioning in U.S. children, using ADHD × learning disability (LD) cross-classification to distinguish the overall movement-behavior gradient from diagnostic differences in baseline functioning. We analyzed pooled cross-sectional data from the 2018-2024 National Survey of Children's Health public-use topical files and included children aged 6-17 years. The survey was completed by parents or caregivers about selected children. Children were classified into four current ADHD/LD groups: neither ADHD nor LD, ADHD-only, LD-only, and ADHD + LD, with explicit handling of questionnaire-design skips and indeterminate current diagnostic status. The exposure was the number of 24-hour movement-behavior guidelines met, from 0 to 3. Outcomes were higher caregiver-reported school functioning and caregiver-reported school-initiated contact regarding school problems. Survey-weighted logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, family-structure, and survey-year covariates. Among 209,556 age-eligible children, 206,636 had classifiable current ADHD/LD status. Adjusted analytic samples included 196,143 children for higher school functioning and 197,776 for school-initiated contact regarding school problems. Compared with meeting 0 guidelines, meeting 3 guidelines was associated with higher odds of higher school functioning (OR 3.87, 95% CI 3.50-4.28) and lower odds of school-initiated contact regarding school problems (OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.44-0.54). The favorable graded pattern for higher school functioning appeared across all four ADHD/LD groups, while the ADHD + LD group remained on the lowest functional baseline. A non-monotonic school-contact pattern in the ADHD-only group at 3 guidelines was treated as an exploratory subgroup signal requiring replication. Additional component-specific, pattern-based, original-category, and sequential-adjustment analyses did not materially alter the primary interpretation. Greater 24-hour movement-behavior guideline attainment was associated with more favorable school-related functioning among U.S. school-aged children. ADHD × LD cross-classification added clinically relevant information by separating the overall movement-behavior gradient from persistent diagnostic differences in baseline school-functioning burden. Exploratory variation across strata should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.title: Cost-utility study of cognitive-behavioural management of auditory hallucinations in schizophrenia: a study protocol.
papers.abstract: Auditory verbal hallucinations (AVHs) affect 60-80% of patients with schizophrenia, causing significant distress and functional impairment. Although cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) has been shown to reduce AVH-related distress and relapse risk, its use remains limited in many countries, including France, due to insufficient clinician training and time constraints. Consequently, treatment continues to rely mainly on second-generation antipsychotics, which have moderate efficacy and notable adverse effects. A structured CBT program combining Coping Strategy Enhancement, relational therapy, third-wave CBT, and imagery-focused techniques has the potential to further reduce the intensity of AVHs and associated distress. This study evaluates the clinical effectiveness and cost-utility of this intervention, with a view to its broader integration into psychiatric care. This randomized controlled trial will assess the cost-utility and clinical effectiveness of CBT for AVHs in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders. A total of 240 patients, aged 15-60 years, experiencing distressing AVHs for at least three months, will be recruited from outpatient psychiatric services. Patients will be randomly assigned (1:1) to either the intervention group (CBT + treatment as usual, TAU), receiving 16 weekly one-hour individual CBT sessions in addition to standard care, or the control group (TAU alone), receiving standard psychiatric follow-up and pharmacological treatment without CBT. The primary outcome is the incremental cost-utility ratio at 12 months, expressed as cost per quality-adjusted life years (QALY) derived from the EuroQuality of life 5-dimension 5-Level questionnaire (EuroQol EQ-5D-5 L), comparing TAU alone with CBT + TAU. Secondary outcomes include changes from baseline at 4, 8, and 12 months in AVHs severity, depressive symptoms, suicidal ideation, quality of life, functioning, sleep quality, substance use, psychiatric comorbidity, pharmacological treatment exposure, and medication adherence. All endpoint assessments will be conducted by independent evaluators blinded to treatment allocation. This is the first large-scale medico-economic trial evaluating CBT for AVHs in France. Strengths include a randomized controlled design, stratification by illness severity, and blinded outcome assessment. By jointly assessing clinical efficacy and economic value, the findings could inform healthcare policy and support the implementation of CBT as a standard component of schizophrenia treatment. Clinicaltrials.gov. Number: NCT07134816. Registered February 4, 2025.

papers.title: Detecting cognitive motor dissociation in unresponsive brain-injured patients: a prospective cohort study using active task-based EEG.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to assess the prevalence and prognostic value of cognitive motor dissociation (CMD) detected by active task-based electroencephalography (EEG) in a cohort of patients with disorders of consciousness (DoC). In a prospective cohort study, we enrolled 56 consecutive clinically unresponsive patients with acute or chronic brain injury. Patients underwent EEG recording during an active motor imagery task following spoken commands. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOS-E) at 6 months. Ten healthy volunteers served as a control group. Among the 56 unresponsive patients, 6 (10.7%) were identified as CMD-positive. The favorable-outcome rate (GOS‑E ≥ 4) was higher in the CMD-positive group (2/6, 33.3%) than in the CMD-negative group (4/50, 8.0%), although the difference did not reach statistical significance (Fisher's exact p = 0.12). At 6‑month follow‑up, no deaths occurred in the CMD‑positive group (n = 6), compared with a mortality rate of 16% (8/50) in the CMD‑negative group. Given the limited sample size, these descriptive results are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger prospective cohorts. In the healthy control group, 9 of 10 participants (90%) were task‑positive; the only task‑negative participant reported having fallen asleep during the experiment. Most healthy volunteers reported feeling drowsy and easily distracted while performing the task. Active task‑based EEG can detect CMD in a subset of behaviorally unresponsive patients, and its presence was descriptively associated with more favorable outcomes. However, the detection rate in our cohort was lower than previously reported, and healthy controls frequently experienced sleepiness during the task. These findings support the prognostic value of EEG‑detected CMD while highlighting the need for more sensitive, patient‑adapted paradigms.

papers.title: Association between insomnia symptoms and social frailty in community-dwelling adults aged 75 years and older: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Insomnia has been associated with frailty; however, its association with social frailty remains unclear, particularly among adults aged 75 years and older. This study aimed to examine the association between insomnia symptoms and social frailty in community-dwelling adults aged 75 years and older. In this cross-sectional study, mailed questionnaire data were obtained from 2091 community-dwelling adults aged 75 years and older in Matsubara, Japan. Insomnia symptoms were assessed using the Japanese version of the Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS-J), with scores of ≥ 6 indicating insomnia symptoms. Social frailty was defined as a score of ≥ 2 on Makizako's five-item questionnaire. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with adjustment for sociodemographic factors and cognitive impairment in the primary model; an additional model further adjusted for physical frailty. Among participants with complete data on both AIS-J and social frailty, social frailty was present in 64.4% of those with insomnia symptoms and in 40.0% of those without insomnia symptoms. Insomnia symptoms were significantly associated with social frailty in the primary model adjusted for sociodemographic factors and cognitive impairment (OR, 2.35; 95% CI, 1.91-2.88). This association remained significant after further adjustment for physical frailty (OR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.56-2.40). Insomnia symptoms were significantly associated with social frailty in community-dwelling adults aged 75 years and older. These findings underscore the relevance of sleep to social vulnerability in late old age, although longitudinal studies are needed to clarify directionality.

papers.title: Australian Guideline for Growth, Health and Developmental Follow-Up for Children Born Very Preterm: Summary of Recommendations.
papers.abstract: Children born very preterm (VP), before 32 weeks' gestation, are among the most vulnerable in the neonatal population. Birth at this early stage of development, when all major organs are underdeveloped, greatly increases the risk of immediate and long-term health and developmental problems. These challenges can be distressing, profoundly affecting family wellbeing and mental health, and require significant health resources. Structured follow-up care is essential for early identification of issues. However, follow-up services for children born VP across Australia are inconsistent, leading to inequities in access, care and outcomes. To address this, the Centre of Research Excellence in Newborn Medicine (funded by the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council [NHMRC], GNT1153176) developed Australia's first evidence-based guideline to support the complex clinical needs of children born VP from birth to preschool age and their caregivers. The guideline provides two clinical consensus-based recommendations for children born VP and their caregivers. Provide structured, preterm-specific post-discharge follow-up to enable timely detection of growth, health and developmental issues: The follow-up schedule offers a minimum set of contacts and priorities from discharge from the neonatal intensive care unit until preschool age (4-5 years), including assessments of physical health, growth, sensory development, feeding, sleep, behaviour, developmental progress of cognitive, language and motor skills, and family wellbeing and mental health. Offer follow-up care to all children irrespective of the presence of risk or resilience factors: Services should be flexible, including telehealth to provide follow-up based on families' preferences, clinical needs, early assessment findings and other relevant factors. These recommendations provide a structured framework to promote consistent and equitable care across settings, optimising health, developmental and family outcomes for children born VP. The NHMRC-endorsed guideline is available at https://www.crenewbornmedicine.org.au/.

papers.title: Autosomal dominant inherited retinal dystrophies in Japan: clinical characteristics, genetics, and implications for precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Autosomal dominant inherited retinal dystrophies (AD-IRDs) constitute a clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of disorders in Japan, including retinitis pigmentosa (RP), and the disease category of "macular dystrophies" caused by numerous pathogenic variants across more than 25 genes. Although AD-IRDs represent a smaller proportion of IRDs when compared with autosomal recessive or X-linked forms, their clinical significance is substantial owing to high variable penetrance, marked intrafamilial variability, and the frequent presence of late-onset or mild phenotypes that remain underdiagnosed.The introduction of next-generation sequencing (NGS) enabled multigene testing and improved diagnostic yields in RP cohorts, with subsequent advances increasing detection rates to approximately 45%, particularly for AD-IRDs. More recently, IRD-specific variant interpretation frameworks have further enhanced diagnostic accuracy and nationwide genomic integration.These advances have clarified the genetic spectrum of AD-IRDs in Japan, with recurrent pathogenic variants in hotspots identified in RHO, RP1, RP1L1, PRPH2, and GUCY2D as major contributors. In parallel, deep phenotyping using multimodal retinal imaging, electrophysiology, and refined genotype-phenotype correlation analyses has revealed population-specific variant distributions associated with characteristic clinical patterns in Japanese cohorts. In addition, emerging therapeutic approaches have now been developed, including gene editing, allele-specific suppression, antisense oligonucleotides, RNA editing, and regenerative cell transplantation strategies.This review summarizes the large-scale cohort studies, molecular functions, phenotypes, and ethnic characteristics of Japanese AD-IRDs and discusses future directions toward precision medicine.
authors: IRD Genomic Research Promotion Taskforce of the Japanese Retina and Vitreous Society

papers.title: A whole-brain neural mass model incorporating astrocyte calcium dynamics for simulating tDCS-induced EEG modulation.
papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanism of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS) requires consideration of important brain cells and their interactions as well as biophysical aspects. Despite recent physiological studies showing sudden calcium signaling associated with astrocyte cells under tDCS, previous computational models aimed at simulating the effects of tDCS, have not included this cell in their equations. This paper proposes a mesoscopic model composed of astrocyte subpopulations as well as pyramidal neurons and interneurons populations. The model can simulate the effect of tDCS on cortical activity related to the average Somatosensory Evoked Potential (aSEP) and is verified by actual results from previous experimental studies on rats. Then a large-scale network model of 76 cerebral areas is considered to simulate the effect of tDCS on EEG signals from 62 scalp electrodes. Actual head meshes and electrodes are used to calculate the distribution of the electric field produced at the cortical level. The model's superiority over previous models lies in its inclusion of astrocyte cells and their interactions with neurons in the neuronal population as well as the simultaneous use of the real human brain connectome to interconnect different cerebral regions. Model parameters are set to produce alpha-like activity in simulated EEG signals. In this study, we focus on the astrocyte-mediated component of tDCS-induced modulation. Results show an increase in the power of the alpha band as well as high frequency components with greater power due to tDCS.

papers.title: Diet-microbiota Interactions in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by chronic inflammation and immunedysregulation. Increasing evidence suggests that the gut microbiota may mediate interactions between environmental factors, particularly diet, and immune responses associated with RA, although causal relationships remain incompletely understood. This review aims to critically evaluate the current evidence on the effects of dietary patterns on gut microbiota composition and function in RA, with particular emphasis on underlying immunometabolic mechanisms, methodological limitations, and clinical relevance. Emerging evidence suggests that the Mediterranean diet and predominantly plant-based dietary patterns are associated with potentially favorable changes in gut microbiota composition, microbial metabolite production, and inflammatory markers. However, evidence that these microbial alterations directly mediate improvements in RA disease activity remains limited. Intermittent fasting may influence microbial circadian rhythms and inflammatory pathways, although much of the mechanistic evidence derives from experimental studies and long-term clinical efficacy remains uncertain. Current evidence does not support routine gluten-free dietary interventions in RA, while probiotic supplementation has shown inconsistent effects on clinical disease activity despite potential improvements in certain inflammatory biomarkers. Diet-microbiota interactions may contribute to immune regulation and inflammatory processes in RA; however, available evidence is limited by methodological heterogeneity, small sample sizes, and potential confounding factors. Although microbiome-guided personalized nutrition represents a promising research direction, its clinical application remains limited by the lack of validated biomarkers and robust intervention studies. Further well-designed, large-scale randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify causal relationships, establish clinically meaningful benefits, and inform evidence-based nutritional recommendations for RA management.

papers.title: Post-treatment perspectives on digital CBT-I among heavy drinkers with insomnia: a qualitative study.
papers.abstract: Digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (d-CBT-I) shows promise for improving sleep and reducing drinking among heavy drinkers with comorbid insomnia, a population characterized by a bidirectional relationship between alcohol use and sleep disturbance. This qualitative study examined experiences of a subgroup of heavy drinkers with insomnia who completed SHUTi, a well-validated d-CBT-I program, as part of two sequential randomized controlled trials (NCT04564807; NCT05630118). Semi-structured post-intervention interviews of SHUTi completers (n = 46) were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis. Four themes emerged: overall impressions; advantages and disadvantages for sleep; advantages and disadvantages for alcohol use; and suggested program improvements. SHUTi was perceived as highly beneficial for sleep. Perceived alcohol benefits were modest and indirect, suggesting that the alcohol benefit is best understood as a clinically important hypothesis about alcohol use mediated by changes in insomnia severity as well as a rationale for future SHUTi adaptations to better support alcohol reduction. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT04564807 (Registered 09-22-2020) and NCT05630118 (Registered 11-17-2022).

papers.title: Adapting form and function of cereals to abiotic stress and production changes with a focus on crop canopies.
papers.abstract: Biological organisms respond to fluctuating conditions through changes to both form and function. In cereal crops, the canopy integrates these responses across scales, linking plant architecture, physiological processes and interactions with the external environment. In this review, we consider how cereal crop canopies can adapt to the abiotic stress challenges induced by climate and farming system change. We discuss the impacts of changing seasonal duration on crop development, highlighting that photosynthetic and metabolic phenology may provide additional layers of environmental responsiveness. We examine multivariate within-season abiotic stresses and the central role of stomatal regulation, hydraulic architecture and transpiration in mediating crop responses and the potential to target circadian clock-associated pathways to enhance crop resilience. Beyond climate-driven stresses, changing production systems act as designed stresses and will require new ideotypes. Cereal canopy design represents a dynamic, multi-scale optimisation challenge and we highlight tractable research and breeding opportunities for adapting cereal crops to new climatic and production conditions.

papers.title: Modulation of oscillatory activity in response to very low intensity transcranial magnetic stimulation in the human primary motor cortex.
papers.abstract: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) is widely used to probe and modulate human brain function, yet the neural effects of stimulation delivered at very low intensities remain unclear. Here, we show that very low intensity TMS can alter ongoing oscillatory activity in the human primary motor cortex. In healthy participants, we combined TMS with electroencephalography (EEG) and assessed neural responses to single pulses and rhythmic stimulation in the motor cortex. Conventional high intensity stimulation produced robust local evoked responses and synchronized beta-frequency oscillations in the directly TMS-targeted cortical area. Low intensity rhythmic stimulation, despite not evoking measurable responses, modified local oscillatory activity in a manner consistent with phase-dependent enhancement of ongoing rhythms. These findings suggest that cortical oscillations can be influenced by magnetic fields substantially weaker than those typically employed to date in human studies. Very low intensity stimulation may therefore offer a route towards portable, energy-efficient technologies for investigating and modulating brain networks.

papers.title: Multimodal spectral-imaging fusion with machine learning for non-destructive monitoring of Gardeniae fructus extract drying.
papers.abstract: Industrial drying of botanical extracts often suffers from variability due to empirical control. Here, we propose a real-time monitoring framework using Gardeniae fructus extract as a model system. A multimodal sensing system integrating RGB imaging and hyperspectral reflectance (350 - 2500 nm) was coupled with machine learning algorithms to monitor vacuum drying dynamics. Reference values for moisture content and chlorogenic acid (a key bioactive compound) were determined via standard methods. Spectral analysis identified the 1400 - 1900 nm region as critical for composition changes. Notably, fusing image texture features with spectral data significantly outperformed single-sensor approaches, achieving coefficients of determination of 0.99 for moisture and 0.96 for chlorogenic acid. This multimodal framework provides a rapid, non-destructive tool for process standardisation and quality control in functional food and nutraceutical production.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm disruption exacerbates periodontitis through BMAL1-regulated macrophage metabolic reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption (CRD) perturbs immune homeostasis and metabolic balance in periodontal tissues, however, the immunometabolic mechanisms linking CRD to periodontitis progression remain poorly defined. This study demonstrates that CRD increases macrophage infiltration and M1 polarization in periodontal tissues, leading to significant alveolar bone resorption and inflammation. Mechanistically, CRD was associated with downregulation of core circadian regulator BMAL1, enhanced glycolytic activity, lactate accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired oxidative phosphorylation in macrophages. These metabolic alterations drive macrophage polarization and exacerbate the progression of periodontitis. Through integrated CUT&Tag, RNA-Seq and ChIP-qPCR analyses, we reveal that BMAL1 is enriched at the promoter regions of key glycolytic genes, including Pfkl, Pgk1, Eno1, and Eno2, and restrains their expression through a TRIM28/H3K9me3-associated epigenetic mechanism, thereby limiting glycolytic reprogramming and inflammatory activation. CRD-mediated downregulation of BMAL1 may weaken this restraint, amplifying the periodontitis phenotype. Therapeutically, in the CRD-associated periodontitis model, 2-DG-mediated inhibition of glycolysis significantly suppresses M1 macrophage polarization, thus alleviating periodontitis severity. Our findings delineate a BMAL1-TRIM28/H3K9me3-glycolysis regulatory axis involving Pfkl, Pgk1, Eno1, and Eno2 that contributes to macrophage polarization and immune activation under CRD, providing a mechanistic rationale for targeted modulation of immunometabolic pathways in CRD-associated inflammatory diseases. Schematic illustration of the BMAL1-mediated immunometabolic mechanism underlying CRD-associated periodontitis. CRD suppresses BMAL1 expression, weakening the BMAL1-TRIM28/H3K9me3-associated epigenetic repression of glycolytic genes (Pfkl, Pgk1, Eno1, and Eno2). Loss of this regulatory restraint promotes macrophage metabolic reprogramming characterized by enhanced glycolysis, lactate accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired oxidative phosphorylation, thereby driving M1 macrophage polarization, periodontal inflammation, and alveolar bone loss. Restoration of BMAL1 expression or localized inhibition of glycolytic flux by 2-DG mitigates CRD-associated periodontitis progression by restraining macrophage inflammatory activation.

papers.title: Sleep duration means what people experience: Why public recommendations must remain anchored in experienced sleep.
Environmental factors associated with sleep health in middle-aged and older adults: Findings from the Canadian longitudinal study on aging.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association between environmental factors and dimensions of sleep health among middle-aged and older adults in Canada, including sleep satisfaction, sleep latency, and sleep duration. We conducted a cross-sectional study using data from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging Comprehensive Cohort (n=30,097), linked with environmental exposure data from the Canadian Urban Environmental Health Research Consortium. Binary sleep outcomes were analyzed using modified Poisson regression, whereas continuous sleep outcomes were analyzed using linear regression. Models assessed associations with environmental factors (green space, air pollution, noise, physical and social environments), adjusting for demographic, behavioral, and health-related covariates. Greater Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) was consistently associated with better sleep health, including lower risk of prolonged sleep latency and longer sleep duration. Higher intersection density was associated with sleep dissatisfaction and shorter sleep duration. Air pollution showed mixed results; higher NO₂ was associated with lower risk of prolonged sleep latency in both models, whereas ozone showed protective associations in domain-specific models. Higher relative humidity was associated with shorter sleep duration, as was nighttime light in domain-specific models. Environmental exposures may play a meaningful role in shaping sleep health among middle-aged and older adults in Canada. Urban greening and reductions in light and noise pollution may be promising strategies to improve sleep. However, associations with air pollution were inconsistent and warrant further investigation. These findings underscore the multifaceted environmental determinants of sleep health and the potential for targeted public health and urban planning interventions.

papers.title: Short-video addiction and circadian phase delay in Chinese adolescents and emerging adults: A three-wave longitudinal study with a nested dim-light melatonin assessment.
papers.abstract: To examine whether short-video addiction is longitudinally associated with endogenous circadian phase delay in Chinese youth, and whether health behaviors mediate this association differently across educational stages and genders. In a 3-wave longitudinal cohort of 1660 students (520 middle-school, 610 high-school, 530 university), short-video use was logged objectively and saliva was sampled at 23:00 on 3 nights per wave; a nested subsample (n = 120) completed overnight dim-light melatonin assessments each wave, enabling calibrated phase-delay estimation (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.89). The proportion in the Short Video Addiction Scale (SVAS)-defined high-score range rose across educational stages (18.3%, 27.7%, 36.4%). The phase-delay association per standard deviation of addiction strengthened from middle school to university (0.92 vs. 2.15 hours; ratio 2.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.8-3.1). In the extreme-groups laboratory subsample (n = 120; SVAS ≥ 31 vs. ≤ 15), health behaviors statistically mediated 65.7% (95% CI 58.3%-72.1%) of the total association-an estimate that applies to these selected extreme groups, with its magnitude across the full exposure distribution remaining uncertain; the dominant pathway shifted from physical activity (middle school) to sleep quality and diet (high school) to psychological stress (university), with educational-stage-dependent gender differences. A nighttime-use breakpoint near 90 minutes was internally consistent across all 3 waves and requires external validation; educational-stage-specific breakpoints and educational stage × gender pathway differences are hypothesis-generating. Short-video addiction is associated with circadian phase delay through educational-stage- and gender-specific behavioral pathways. Findings are associational and support tailored prevention research.

papers.title: The effect of subclinical concussion following intentional ball heading in adult female football players: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: To assess the impact of intentional ball heading on subclinical concussion in adult female football players, with a focus on symptom severity, cognitive function, and biomarkers of brain injury. Systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024487253). A comprehensive search was conducted across five databases (Scopus, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane) on 27 March 2024 and updated on 31 March 2026. Studies were included if they involved adult female footballers (≥18 years), assessed intentional heading, and provided quantitative outcomes. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Cochrane RoB tool. Due to methodological heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was performed. Fifteen studies met inclusion criteria. Eight reported cognitive decline in at least one domain (e.g., memory, psychomotor speed), and three studies showed worsening post-concussive symptoms, particularly in players with a history of concussion. One study found increased serum biomarker (S-100B) post-match correlated with heading frequency. However, three studies reported no significant cognitive impact. Structural neuroimaging showed no cortical thinning, whilst EEG data yielded mixed findings. Recent evidence identified altered fine motor and cerebrovascular changes following repetitive heading in female footballers. Overall, self-reported heading exposure and heterogeneous outcome measures limited comparability. Intentional ball heading may contribute to post-concussive symptoms and fine motor cognitive alterations in adult female footballers, particularly those with prior concussion. Whilst evidence of cognitive decline is present, findings remain inconsistent. Standardised concussion assessments and objective heading metrics are needed to better inform safety protocols in women's football.
papers.journal: Journal of science and medicine in sport

papers.title: Inherited retinal disease care pathway in the UK: a healthcare professional perspective.
Sleep Quality in Hospitalized Patients with Chronic Liver Disease: A Retrospective Study with an Exploratory Analysis of Covert Hepatic Encephalopathy.
papers.abstract: Objective Sleep-related disturbances are an important comorbidity of chronic liver disease (CLD) but are not routinely assessed in clinical practice. We evaluated sleep quality using the Japanese version of the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and explored its association with covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE).Methods This retrospective, single-center study enrolled hospitalized patients with CLD who completed the PSQI upon admission. Poor sleep quality was defined as a PSQI global score ≥6. Factors associated with poor sleep quality were evaluated using logistic regression analysis. CHE was assessed in a subcohort of patients who completed a neuropsychological test (NPT) battery.Results Among the 180 enrolled patients (median age, 68 years; 65.0% men), the median PSQI global score was 5 (interquartile range, 3-8), and 88 (48.9%) reported poor sleep quality. In a multivariate analysis, medication use for pruritus (odds ratio [OR], 5.24) and a SARC-F score of ≥4 (OR, 3.19) were independently associated with PSQI ≥6. The NPT-assessed subcohort comprised 41 patients (CHE, 24; non-CHE, 17). PSQI global scores were higher in the CHE group than in the non-CHE group (Hodges-Lehmann estimate [CHE - non-CHE], 3.0; p=0.013). Component-level analyses indicated a shift toward higher scores for PSQI component 5 (sleep disturbances) in the CHE group. CHE remained associated with PSQI ≥6 after multivariate adjustment in the subcohort (OR, 8.00).Conclusions Poor sleep quality was common among hospitalized patients with CLD and associated with medication use for pruritus and SARC-F ≥4. An exploratory analysis suggested an association between the CHE classification and poor sleep quality.

papers.title: Dual-Compartment Proteomic Analysis Reveals Inflammatory Signatures of Sleep Disturbance in Allergic Rhinitis.
papers.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is often accompanied by sleep disturbance, while the molecular mechanisms underlying sleep-related exacerbation of nasal symptoms remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the inflammatory protein signatures associated with poor sleep in AR using a dual-compartment proteomic approach. We first analyzed 3,731 adult participants from the 2005-2006 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) cycle to validate the association between sleep duration and AR. We then enrolled 40 AR patients (20 poor sleepers, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [PSQI] > 5; 20 normal sleepers, PSQI ≤ 5) in this cross-sectional clinical cohort study and performed Olink proteomic profiling in paired serum and nasal secretion (NS) samples. Differential expression analysis, functional enrichment, cross-compartment correlation, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and sequential multivariable linear regression were conducted. In NHANES, short sleep duration (<6 h) was significantly associated with increased odds ratio (OR) of AR (OR = 1.27, 95% CI 1.05-1.54, p = 0.013) and elevated serum total immunoglobulin E (IgE). In the clinical cohort, poor sleepers had higher Total Nasal Symptom Score (TNSS) (p < 0.001), Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI) (p < 0.001), and blood eosinophil counts (p = 0.011). Proteomics identified 27 serum and 20 NS differentially expressed proteins (DEPs), with 9 overlapping DEPs enriched in interleukin-17 (IL-17), tumor necrosis factor, and chemokine signaling pathways. A four-marker panel (serum beta-nerve growth factor [β-NGF], serum transforming growth factor-beta 1 [TGF-β1], NS interleukin-8 [IL-8], NS matrix metalloproteinase-1 [MMP-1]) achieved an area under the curve of 0.88 (95% CI 0.76-0.97, p < 0.001) for distinguishing poor from normal sleepers. Cross-compartment correlation analysis revealed significant serum-NS protein concordance, consistent with systemic-local inflammatory crosstalk. Sequential multivariable regression showed that serum β-NGF independently predicted TNSS severity even after PSQI adjustment (β = 2.22, p = 0.044), whereas nasal IL-8 was fully attenuated (β = 0.58, p = 0.391). Poor sleep is associated with exacerbated AR through coordinated systemic and local inflammatory responses. Serum β-NGF is independently associated with nasal symptoms, whereas the association of NS IL-8 with symptoms appears to be explained by sleep disturbance. Integrating markers from both compartments enhances the identification of AR patients with poor sleep.
papers.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology

papers.title: Acupuncture and Brain Clearance Systems: A Critical Narrative Review of Glymphatic Function, AQP4 Polarization, and Meningeal Lymphatic Drainage.
papers.abstract: Brain clearance systems, particularly the glymphatic pathway and meningeal lymphatic drainage, are increasingly recognized as important regulators of central nervous system homeostasis. These systems support cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange and contribute to the removal of metabolic waste, misfolded proteins, and inflammatory mediators. Aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarization at astrocytic endfeet is an important determinant of perivascular fluid transport, whereas meningeal lymphatic vessels provide an extracranial route for macromolecular and immune drainage. Acupuncture, especially electroacupuncture, has been reported to influence cerebral perfusion, neurovascular function, astrocyte activity, neuroinflammation, autonomic balance, and sleep-related physiology. These observations raise the possibility that acupuncture could influence physiological determinants of brain clearance; however, direct experimental evidence remains scarce and predominantly preclinical. In this critical narrative review, we evaluate the limited direct and near-direct evidence linking acupuncture to glymphatic transport and AQP4-related clearance, distinguish it from broader indirect mechanistic support, and identify meningeal-cervical lymphatic regulation as a largely untested hypothesis. We further propose a testable framework involving neurovascular modulation, astrocyte-AQP4 remodeling, inflammatory resolution, autonomic regulation, and sleep/arousal pathways. Particular emphasis is placed on methodological limitations, reverse causality, and the need for tracer-based imaging, spatial AQP4 analysis, lymphatic assessment, and pathway-specific interventions before brain-clearance regulation can be considered a causal mechanism of acupuncture-induced neuroprotection.

papers.title: Associations between systematic sports training and visual processing in adolescents: Behavioral and ERP evidence.
papers.abstract: Adolescent visual systems continue to develop, but their association with systematic sports training is not well understood. We compared 33 adolescents with more than 1.5 years of sports training and 33 peers without specialized training. Participants completed behavioral tests and an electroencephalography (EEG) task with occluded faces, complete faces, and buildings. Principal event-related potential (ERP) analyses included 29 exercise participants and 23 controls per face condition. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied within analysis families. Four behavioral differences survived correction: the exercise group responded faster on negative dot-probe and Go/No-Go trials and was more accurate in high-load multiple-object tracking and shape perception (all q <.05). The exercise group showed lower occipital P1 component amplitudes for both face positions (component-family q =.002; global q =.009). The complete-face occipital N1 difference attenuated after P1 adjustment (q =.604), whereas the frontal late slow-wave difference remained after adjustment for preceding components (difference = 2.88 µV, 95% CI [1.09, 4.67]; component-family q =.004; global q =.009). Some exploratory posterior comparisons were nominally significant, but none survived FDR correction. Systematic sports training history was associated with better performance on selected cognitive tasks and differences in early occipital P1 and late frontal activity in adolescents.

papers.title: Zhibai Anshen Oral Liquid Activates cAMP/PKA/CREB Signaling Axis and Promotes BDNF and Circadian Clock Protein Expression to Ameliorate Insomnia.
papers.abstract: Zhibai Anshen oral liquid (ZBAS) was optimized from classical traditional Chinese medicine formula Zhimubaihe decoction, and it has been approved for clinical treatment of insomnia for over 30 years, achieving a satisfying effect. However, its potential mechanisms are still unclear. This study aims to uncover the key mechanisms of ZBAS in ameliorating insomnia-like behaviors. Insomnia rats were established, and the effect of ZBAS on insomnia was assessed. Histological assessments via H&E and Nissl staining were conducted to evaluate the pathological alterations in the hippocampus, while the regulatory effects of ZBAS on neurotransmitters (5-HT, GABA, and NE) were simultaneously determined. To assess neuronal viability in rats, we monitored NeuN expression via immunofluorescence staining, alongside the quantification of circadian clock proteins (PER3 and CLOCK). Furthermore, network pharmacology was coupled with RNA-seq to filter key molecules of ZBAS against insomnia. To thoroughly substantiate the pivotal signaling networks mapped out by KEGG pathway enrichment, complementary in vivo assays were subsequently conducted. Our findings showed that ZBAS effectively counteracted insomnia-driven weight loss, while concurrently reducing sleep latency and extending total sleep duration in rats. These behavioral improvements were accompanied by enhanced neuronal viability and elevated levels of circadian clock proteins. A total of 151 potential targets of ZBAS in ameliorating insomnia were identified through RNA-seq and network pharmacology analysis. PPI analysis revealed that BDNF was a key molecule. KEGG enrichment analysis indicated that the amelioration of insomnia by ZBAS was closely related to the cAMP signaling pathway. Further results suggested that the ameliorative effect of ZBAS on insomnia-like behaviors in PCPA-induced rats was associated with activation of the cAMP/PKA/CREB axis and was accompanied by upregulation of BDNF and circadian clock proteins. Notably, MDL12330A (an adenylyl cyclase inhibitor) attenuated the ameliorative effects of ZBAS on insomnia. This study provides evidence that, in PCPA-induced insomnia rats, cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling contributes to the anti-insomnia effect of ZBAS, which is associated with upregulation of BDNF and circadian clock proteins; however, whether the upregulation of BDNF and PER3/CLOCK is required for the anti-insomnia effect remains to be experimentally verified.

papers.title: Digital Health and the Next Decade of Electrophysiology.
Alternative CLOCK isoforms specify a non-circadian timing circuit in Drosophila.
papers.abstract: Interval timing is a cognitive ability essential for behaviors such as mating, foraging, and decision-making, and it is distinct from circadian rhythm regulation. Despite the involvement of circadian clock genes in both interval timing and circadian rhythms, the mechanisms differentiating these functions remain unclear. Using Drosophila as a model, we indicate that CLOCK (CLK) and CYCLE (CYC), but not PERIOD (PER) and TIMELESS (TIM), are essential for interval timing. Neuronal CLK/CYC expression is required for sexual experience-dependent shorter mating duration (SMD) behavior. We identify a GAL4R54D11-positive clock-neuron population containing ion transport peptide-positive lateral dorsal neurons (ITP-LNd) and 5th small ventral lateral neurons (5th sLNv) as pivotal for SMD, with glutamatergic intersectional analyses pointing to ITP-LNd as the principal locus. Short CLK isoforms lacking the canonical DNA-binding motif are selectively required for SMD, whereas long- and short-isoform manipulations produce distinct effects on sleep duration. Our study uncovers a specialized circuit for interval timing and highlights the non-circadian functions of circadian clock genes.
papers.journal: Journal of genetics and genomics = Yi chuan xue bao

papers.title: Epigenetic Aging and Severity of Nocturnal Intermittent Hypoxia.
papers.abstract: Nocturnal intermittent hypoxia (IH) is a hallmark feature of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and contributes to oxidative stress and inflammation, which in turn may accelerate biological aging. Epigenetic clocks can estimate biological age from DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns. Is greater severity of IH associated with increased biological aging? We studied adults referred for suspected OSA in a multisite sleep and circadian research network, a cross-sectional observational cohort (2016-2021). IH severity was assessed using the 4% oxygen desaturation index (ODI) from home sleep apnea testing or in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG). DNAm from peripheral blood leukocytes was assayed using Illumina EPIC arrays. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and pace of aging were calculated using multiple DNAm clocks. Linear regression models were adjusted for leukocyte composition, age, sex, ethnicity, BMI, smoking, site, alcohol, diabetes, and hypertension. A false discovery rate of 0.05 was used. A total of 1364 participants were included (median age, 56 yrs; median ODI, 16/h; median BMI, 32 kg/m2; 57% male). Higher ODI was associated with EAA for PhenoAge (β = 0.028, adjusted P = .0048) and with pace of aging (DunedinPACE, β = 0.0005, adjusted P =.0012). No significant associations were observed for first-generation clocks. Greater IH severity, as assessed by ODI, was independently associated with increased biological aging as measured by PhenoAge and DunedinPACE clocks. These findings support a link between OSA and biological aging, raising the possibility of using epigenetic age measures as biomarkers of OSA-related morbidity.
